source.full: Twilight Imperium: Ships of the Shattered Empire

talent.name: Bail Out
description: When a vehicle or starship that your character is controlling is destroyed, you may spend 1 Story Point to have your character use this talent to escape the vehicle without suffering any wounds or injuries.

talent.name: Fight at the Front
description: When your character makes a skill check while "{@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|getting involved directly}" (see page 33) during {@rule mass combat}, if they fail, they reduce the wounds they suffer by their ranks in {@skill Resilience}.

talent.name: Know How to Handle It
description: Once per encounter while aboard a vehicle or starship, your character may use this talent to cause the vehicle to heal 1 system strain per rank of Know How to Handle It.

talent.name: One Last Push
description: After the active force makes a {@rule mass combat} check but before determining the results, your character may suffer strain no greater than twice their ranks in One Last Push to use this talent. For every 2 strain they suffer, the active force may reroll one {@dice boost} or {@dice setback}.

talent.name: Calm and Calculating
description: When your character makes a skill check while "{@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|leading the fight}" (see page 32) during {@rule mass combat}, they may use this talent to use {@skill Cool} or {@skill Knowledge (Culture)||eoti} instead of {@skill Leadership}.

talent.name: Force of Personality
description: When your character makes a skill check while "{@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|leading the fight}" (see page 32) during {@rule mass combat}, they may use this talent to use {@skill Charm} or {@skill Coercion} instead of {@skill Leadership}.

talent.name: Mech Toss
description: While your character is piloting a mech, they may use this talent to target another vehicle or adversary that is silhouette 2, 3, or 4 and make an opposed {@skill Driving} versus {@skill Driving} check. If they succeed, they throw or push the target up to medium range directly away from their mech. The target is knocked {@rule prone} (or the vehicle equivalent) and suffers 5 system strain, plus 1 additional system strain and 1 hull trauma per {@symbols a} generated on the check. {@symbols t} may be spent to inflict a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} on the target.

talent.name: Surgeon Commander
description: When determining the {@rule Mass combat: tallying the cost of battle|casualties} suffered at the end of a round of {@rule mass combat} (see page 35), your character may use this talent to make a {@difficulty hard|medicine}. If they succeed, their side decreases the size of their force by 1 less than they would normally (some individuals may still become casualties, but not enough to affect the size of the overall military force).

talent.name: Battlefield Decapitation
description: During a round of {@rule mass combat}, your character may use this talent to perform a {@difficulty hard} combat check (using a combat skill that makes sense given the circumstances of the combat). If they succeed, they eliminate or temporarily incapacitate a mid-level commander of the enemy forces, reducing the enemy force quality by 1 for the remainder of the current round.

If they generate {@symbols aaa} or {@symbols t}, they may either select a particularly vital target and reduce the enemy force quality by 2 instead of 1, or they may inflict a single {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury} on a notable adversary of the enemy forces (see page 35).

talent.name: Seize the Moment
description: Once per session at the beginning of a round of {@rule mass combat}, you may spend 2 Story Points to allow your character to use this talent to add a {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|crisis point} (see page 34) to the current round. The nature of the {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|crisis point} is up to you, but must be approved by your GM, as are the results if your group successfully resolve it.

talent.name: Stealthy Operator
description: While controlling a mech or other ground vehicle, your character may use this talent to make a {@difficulty hard|stealth}. If they succeed, their vehicle cannot be detected or attacked by other vehicles that are not within medium range.
At your GM's discretion, your character may not be able to use this talent if their vehicle is in very open terrain (such as a desert plain or large parking lot).

talent.name: Trusted Commander
description: When your character makes a skill check while "{@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|leading the fight}" (see page 32) during {@rule mass combat}, if they are commanding a force that shares their allegiance, the difficulty of the check is reduced to {@difficulty easy}.

talent.name: Boarding Party
description: While your character is not piloting a vehicle and is within engaged range with a vehicle, they may spend a Story Point to use this talent to climb on top of the vehicle, and cannot be dislodged for a number of rounds equal to their ranks in {@skill Coordination}.

While on top of the vehicle, your character may perform an {@difficulty average|Mechanics or Computers} to inflict 4 system strain on the vehicle plus 1 per additional {@symbols s}, or they may perform a {@difficulty daunting|Mechanics or Computers} to gain access to the interior of the vehicle.

talent.name: Fire Everything!
description: Once per session, after your character makes a successful combat check using a vehicle or starship weapon, you may spend one Story Point to have them use this talent to hit the target with all other weapons mounted on the vehicle or starship that have not fired during the current round. Each weapon inflicts one hit, dealing damage equal to its base damage plus the number of {@symbols s} generated on the combat check.

The weapons must be able to be fired at the target vehicle (be in range, be in firing arc, not be disabled, etc.) to be used by this talent. Any weapon used by this talent may not be used to make attacks for the remainder of the round.

talent.name: Sabotage!
description: Once per encounter, your character may use this talent to target a vehicle or starship within medium range and make a {@difficulty hard|computers}. If they succeed, they may select one {@sidebar Vehicle Components|component} on the vehicle (see {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook page 221) to become compromised. In addition, the vehicle suffers 1 hull trauma per {@symbols aa} and 3 hull trauma per {@symbols t}.

At your GM's discretion, this check's difficulty may be upgraded one or more times if the vehicle is particularly large and well-defended (a {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnought's|eoti} systems are harder to infiltrate than a civilian {@vehicle rambler|rambler's|eoti}, for example).

talent.name: Master and Commander
description: Whenever your character makes a skill check while aboard a starship, they may suffer 1 strain to use this talent to reduce the difficulty of the check by one, to a minimum of {@difficulty easy}.

This may even apply to skill checks that have nothing to do with operating a starship, such as a {@skill Charm} check to interact with a passenger. In these cases, you should describe how your character's familiarity and comfort with being aboard a starship allows them to perform the task more easily.

rows.difference: Initiating vehicle's speed is one or more higher than target vehicle.
Initiating vehicle is traveling at the same speed as target vehicle.
Initiating vehicle's speed is one lower than target vehicle.
Initiating vehicle's speed is two or more lower than target vehicle.

table.name: Table 1-2: Spending Advantage and Triumph in Starship Combat

options: A scan of an enemy ship reveals that their communications are using a weak encryption, offering a chance to jam their signals or possibly even hack into their computer network. The next {@rule Jamming} or {@rule Hack Enemy's Systems} action to target that ship adds {@symbols ss} to the result.
The pilot of an allied ship of silhouette 4 or smaller can use a {@rule Reposition} maneuver as an out-of-turn {@rule Incidentals|incidental}.
One of the crew manages to effect some temporary repairs, repairing 1 system strain for the character's ship.
The ongoing fighting leads to casualties aboard an enemy ship of silhouette 4 or larger. One weapon of your choice on that ship cannot be used next turn while it is being recrewed.
The captain, the first officer, the master gunner, or another crucial officer aboard the enemy vessel is injured in the fighting and suffers a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury}.

A sizable portion of the crew aboard the enemy ship have been killed or injured in the fighting. Add {@dice setback} to all checks made by crew aboard the enemy ship for the remainder of the encounter.

The captain, the first officer, the master gunner, or another crucial officer aboard the enemy vessel is severely injured or killed in the fighting. They suffer wounds equal to one more than their wound threshold and are {@rule incapacitated}.

Brilliant predictive maneuvering allows the character's ship to be in the right place at the right time. At the start of the pilot's turn, they may turn the ship up to 90 degrees as an {@rule Incidentals|incidental}. This is in addition to any turns from the {@rule Reposition} maneuver and can happen before forced movement.
The master gunner spots a flaw in the enemy's defense systems. The next combat check they make targeting an enemy ship treats the target's defense as 0.

One of the ship's crew hits a damaged component with their tools or fist out of frustration. To their surprise, the component starts working again! One {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} that compromised a component of the character's ship is automatically repaired.

table.name: Table 1-3: Spending Threat and Despair in Starship Combat

options: Overtaxing the systems causes the character's ship to suffer 1 system strain. This may be triggered multiple times.

The drive systems aboard the character's ship flare, making it easier to track. Add {@dice boost|2} to any attempts to track the ship. Weapons with the {@quality Guided} quality add {@dice boost|2} to combat checks targeting the ship. Both effects last until the end of the next round.

Solar flares or exotic energies interfere with communications and sensors on the character's ship. Increase the difficulty of all {@rule Jamming}, {@rule Plot Course}, {@rule Scan the Enemy}, or {@rule Hack Enemy's Systems} actions made aboard the ship by 1 until the end of the encounter.

Several crew members are wounded or killed during the fighting. One of the PCs (players' choice) adds {@dice setback} to all checks they make until the end of the encounter. If the injured are treated with an {@difficulty average|medicine}, the penalty is removed.
Exploding systems deal 2 strain and 2 wounds to one PC of the GM's choice. These are not reduced by the target's soak.

The drive systems fluctuate, increasing or decreasing the speed of the character's ship by 1 (to a minimum of 0 or maximum of its maximum speed). The change is up to the GM and should be inconvenient for the players.

A botched or desperate maneuver results in the character's ship heading toward a collision with an asteroid, derelict vessel, or even an enemy ship. Pick one large object in the encounter that the character's ship could hit; unless the pilot of the character's ship makes a successful {@rule Dangerous Driving} action before the end of the character's next turn, the ship will suffer a major {@rule Collisions|collision} (see page 222 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook) with it.
One PC of the GM's choice suffers 5 wounds (not reduced by soak) and a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury} as they are hit by explosions and shrapnel during the fighting.

An NPC who has an important role aboard the ship is {@rule incapacitated} during the fighting. Unless they are successfully treated with a {@difficulty hard|medicine}, they die at the end of the encounter.

An overloaded component aboard the character's ship explodes in sparks and flames. The ship suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}. When generating this {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, reroll any results of 127 or higher.

planetary: A troop of 2-3 mechs or armored vehicles.
space: A single starfighter squadron of 6-12 ships.

planetary: A squadron of 4-8 mechs or armored vehicles.
A platoon of 20-50 mechanized infantry (infantry riding in 2-4 armored vehicles) supported by 2-3 mechs.
A company of 10-30 mechs or armored vehicles.
A company of 50-200 mechanized infantry with 10-15 vehicles and a squadron of 4-8 mechs or tanks.
A regiment of 31-99 mechs or armored vehicles.
A battalion of 200-600 mechanized infantry in 20-40 vehicles with a company (10-20 vehicles) of armored support.
space: A fleet of 6-15 capital ships, with fighter escort and support.

planetary: A division of 100-300 mechs or armored vehicles.
A brigade of 600-2,000 mechanized infantry riding in roughly 100 vehicles with another 30-50 tanks or mechs providing heavy armor support.
space: An armada of more than 16 capital ships, along with their fighters and escorts.

example: Unarmed civilians.
Unarmed civilian vessels.
Armed civilians or ill-equipped militia.
Retrofitted civilian or industrial equipment used as makeshift weapons.
Civilian vessels with minimal weaponry.
Conscripted or drafted troops with a few weeks of basic training.
Obsolete or outdated weapons, vehicles, and equipment.
Fearless, utterly dedicated, but minimally armed troops, such as {@rule Nekro Virus|Nekro|eoti} drone swarms or {@adversary Mahact Thrall Clone|Mahact thrall clones|eoti}.
Warships from the reserve fleets with inexperienced reservist or drafted crews.
Basic soldiers with months of training and potentially some combat experience.
Modern and standard-issue equipment, vehicles, and weapons.

Fearless, utterly dedicated troops with standard equipment, such as {@rule Vuil'raith Cabal|Vuil'raith|eoti} berserkers, {@adversary L1Z1X Legionnaire|L1Z1X Legionnaires|eoti}, or {@adversary Arborec Letani Behemoth|Arborec Letani behemoths|eoti}.
Average battle line warships.

Elite troops with advanced training and combat experience such as {@adversary Sol Spec Ops Drop Trooper|Sol Spec Ops troopers|eoti}, {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} assault cohorts, or {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} stealth elimination teams.
Advanced equipment, weapons, and armor too costly or rare to give to an entire army.
Fearless, dedicated, and well-armed troops with full military support, such as an integrated {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti} army.
The core of any battlefleet.
The crew of any fleet flagship.
The deadliest, best equipped, and most highly trained soldiers in the galaxy with lethal experimental weaponry and advanced equipment.
Any {@rule Mahact Gene-Sorcerers|Mahact|eoti} force when a {@rule Mahact Gene-Sorcerers|Mahact gene-sorcerer|eoti} takes the field and unleashes the full might of their fell abilities.

table.name: Table 3-3: Boost and Setback in Mass Combat

rows.boost: The active force occupies a defensive position (such as a PDS [planetary defense system] installation, natural cover, or a trench system).
rows.setback: The enemy force occupies a defensive position (such as a fortress, hardened bunker, or natural choke point).

rows.boost: The active force had ample time to prepare for the engagement (such as setting traps or mines, laying in supplies, or scouting the terrain beforehand).
rows.setback: The active force is caught off guard, under extreme pressure, or otherwise unprepared for the battle (such as having weapons locked away, troops out of position, or scouts ambushed).

rows.boost: Weather or stellar phenomena provide the active force with cover, cloak their movements, or disrupt the enemy force.
rows.setback: Weather or stellar phenomena disrupt or distract the active force or provide the enemy force with cover or the element of surprise.

rows.boost: The active force has specialist equipment or arms particularly well suited for the task at hand.
rows.setback: The active force is low on ammunition or undersupplied.

rows.boost: The active force has irregular or non-combatant allies who provide useful support (such as providing extra food or supplies, offering their knowledge of the area, or even acting as scouts or spies).
rows.setback: The active force is hindered by non-combatant involvement in the battle (such as irregular troops aiding the enemy force or civilians the active force has to evacuate or protect).

table.name: Table 3-4: Spending Advantage and Triumph in Mass Combat

options: All allied player characters with the active force recover 1 strain.
Notice a key feature of the enemy force (such as an enemy officer, weapon emplacement, or support ship) and its position on the battlefield.
A probing attack by the active force reveals a weakness in the enemy force's deployment. Add {@dice boost} to the active force's next {@rule mass combat} check as it exploits this weakness.

Accomplish something that doesn't affect the course of the battle but does prove particularly useful to advancing one of the PCs' {@rule agendas||eoti}. After the battle, one PC completes a benchmark for their {@rule Agendas|agenda|eoti}. The group should decide which PC completes this benchmark, but the GM has the final say.

A previously unnoticed geographical feature on the battlefield (stand of trees, ravine, rock formation, or planetary ring, for example) offers the active force a vital advantage in the coming fight. The active force may downgrade the difficulty of its next {@rule mass combat} check as it exploits this vital feature.

The active force disables or destroys an important piece of enemy hardware, such as a heavy weapon emplacement, support mech, or starship, that provided the enemy force with some advantage in battle. Adjust the enemy force's quality accordingly in the next {@rule mass combat} check. Additionally, this may further affect the casualties the enemy force has suffered at the end of the battle.

The leader of the active force makes a rousing speech to inspire the troops or enacts a cunning strategy that may take the enemy force by surprise. The active force may upgrade the ability of its next {@rule mass combat} check once.

Overwhelmed by the ferocity of the active force, the enemy force is close to breaking. During its next {@rule mass combat} check, the active force may spend {@symbols t} to cause the enemy force to flee in a panicked rout.
A notable NPC in the active force performs a particular feat of heroism and valor. This provides the active force with a leader or warrior to benefit it even after the battle is over.
Reinforcements for the active force arrive, increasing its ranks in size once for all future phases.
A brilliant tactical maneuver cuts off, destroys, or captures a sizable portion of the enemy force, decreasing the enemy force's ranks in size once for future phases.

A dramatic narrative moment gives the PCs the chance to single-handedly change the entire course of the battle. This is a {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|crisis point} (see page 34) that—if the PCs take the opportunity and succeed—can allow them to win the battle automatically or gain a sizable advantage in future {@rule mass combat} checks, at the GM's discretion.

table.name: Table 3-5: Spending Threat and Despair in Mass Combat

options: All allied characters with the active force suffer 1 strain.

The fog of war creates confusion on the battlefield. Add {@dice setback} to the next {@rule mass combat} check as the active force attempts to sift through contradictory intel or enemy misinformation.
The enemy launches a probing attack that disrupts the active force's order of battle. Add {@dice setback|2} to the next {@rule mass combat} check as the active force must react to enemy movements.
One of the PCs involved with the active force (either chosen at random or by the GM, depending on the ongoing narrative) is injured in the fight and suffers 4 wounds.

The active force gets bogged down in difficult terrain, or the enemy force takes advantage of some unnoticed terrain feature. Upgrade the difficulty of the active force's next {@rule mass combat} check once.

A valuable heavy weapon or vehicle belonging to the active force is destroyed, or one of the PCs' vehicles suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}. This may also affect the size of the active force at the end of the battle.

The enemy force disrupts the command and communications of the active force by injuring a ranking officer, jamming communications, or hacking computer systems to introduce contradictory orders. Downgrade the ability of the next {@rule mass combat} check the active force makes once, or have one notable NPC in the command structure of the active force suffer a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury}.

One of the PCs involved with the active force (either chosen at random or by the GM, depending on the ongoing narrative) is grievously wounded in the fighting and suffers a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury}.
A notable NPC involved with the active force and chosen by the GM is killed in the fighting unless they are successfully treated with a {@difficulty hard|medicine} during the next phase.

Communications are completely disrupted, and the commander of the active force cannot send orders to their units in the field. Unless another officer or respected leader who can communicate to the active force steps in, the active force's quality is reduced by one for the remainder of the battle.
Reinforcements arrive to support the enemy force, increasing its force size by one for the remainder of the battle.
A brilliant tactical maneuver or terrible blunder cuts off, destroys, or captures a sizable portion of the acting force, decreasing the acting force's ranks in size once for future phases.

A calamitous event or bitter betrayal imperils the entire active force. This is a {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|crisis point} (see page 34) that the PCs must deal with personally. If the PCs do not resolve the situation satisfactorily, the active force is defeated. In addition, the PCs are too busy dealing with the situation to continue contributing to the ongoing battle in any way.

rows.effect: Increase armor by 1 and defense by 1. If the ship suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, automatically apply the {@b Hull Damaged} result (see page 230 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook) unless it is already suffering that result.

If the check generates {@symbols d}, the crew members or cohorts add {@dice setback} to all {@skill Cool} or {@skill Discipline} checks they make for the rest of the session.

Characters may spend {@symbols a} from checks to use the ship's sensors to inflict 1 system strain on any ship targeted by these sensors. The GM may spend {@symbols h} from these checks to inflict 2 system strain on this ship instead.

As a maneuver, the pilot may cause the ship to suffer 5 system strain to increase the ship's current and maximum speed by 1 and the damage of all shipboard energy weapons by 1. This lasts until the start of the pilot's next turn.

Choose a single beam weapon on the ship. The weapon gains the qualities {@quality Inaccurate|Inaccurate 1} and {@quality Vicious|Vicious 3}, and its range changes to short range.
Choose a single beam weapon on the ship. Increase the weapon's damage by 3, but each time it is fired, the ship suffers 2 system strain.

sidebar.name: Range Bands in Space
description: This sidebar echoes the {@sidebar Range Bands in Space|sidebar|crb} found on page 225 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook but goes into a little more detail on the topic. Here we discuss what {@rule range bands} represent in space for the {@setting Twilight Imperium||eoti} setting specifically, to help you visualize the distances involved.

{@b Engaged:} If your ship is engaged with something, it's generally docked with it, tethered to it, or no more than one hundred meters away. At this distance, someone can cross between two ships easily, though they likely have to put on a spacesuit.

{@b Short range:} If your ship is short range from something, it's within visual range and probably within twenty kilometers. Many starfighter engagements occur within short range. Two capital ships slugging it out at short range are likely to pummel each other into pieces very quickly, and some have weapons that cannot even be used against targets this close.

{@b Medium range:} Medium range is within roughly two hundred kilometers, which is far enough that ships must rely on enhanced optics to view one another. {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|Starfighters|eoti} can still shoot at one another with their primary armaments at this range, and capital ships sometimes engage at this distance.

{@b Long range:} If your ship is long range from something, it's within roughly five thousand kilometers. This is far enough that you're primarily looking at it on your scanner displays rather than out your viewports. While this seems like a great distance, ships and weapons can still cross it very quickly. Starfighter missiles can reach this far, and this is often the distance at which major capital ships engage with their primary weapons.

{@b Extreme range:} This range, up to one hundred thousand kilometers away, is the maximum direct engagement range for most ships. Only the beam weapons on the largest {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} can fire accurately at this distance, as well as some specialty weapons such as cruiser assault cannons. At this range, warships tend to engage more with anti-ship missiles and torpedoes.

{@b Strategic range:} This range includes anything within a star system. At this distance, only far-reaching weapons such as torpedoes, heavy missiles, and planetary defense cannons can hit anything accurately. Strategic range is also the longest distance that most starship sensors can detect something.

Obviously, strategic range includes a huge range of distances, anywhere from a few million kilometers to a few {@i billion} kilometers. It's reasonable to assume that some things may be beyond the range of even the most powerful weapons but still be within strategic range. Traveling to something at strategic range may take a matter of hours, rather than a few rounds in a structured encounter. Therefore, you can certainly tell your group that even though an enemy is within strategic range, it may take several hours to get close enough for a combat encounter to begin, despite the party having strategic-range weapons.

sidebar.name: Firing at Engaged Enemies
description: The rules on {@rule making ranged attacks while engaged} (see page 107 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook) prohibit firing {@skill Gunnery} weapons at engaged targets. These rules were primarily written with individual characters in mind (since it's hard to fire a missile launcher at someone trying to stab you with a knife). However, they also apply to vehicles. At extremely close ranges, most starships find it very difficult or outright impossible to bring guns to bear, while missiles or torpedoes don't have time to arm or to acquire targets.

However, at your discretion, there may be some circumstances where a ship can fire weapons "point blank" at an engaged target. In these cases, it's up to you as the GM to determine the difficulty and the potential risks associated with the action.

sidebar.name: Running Enemy Ships
description: Although these guidelines refer to a ship run by the player characters, you can also use them when directing an enemy ship full of NPCs. The goal in that case is the same: limiting the number of checks for each ship.

sidebar.name: Who Put You in Charge?
description: The concept of a captain (who typically has complete authority over their ship) is often antithetical to an RPG group composed of a bunch of friends who have equal say in group decisions. Therefore, we recommend that if one of your PCs has taken on the role of captain, the player controlling that PC makes sure to determine their "orders" with the rest of the players before having their character give them. These out-of-character discussions let the group decide on their actions jointly before returning to the ongoing story where the PC captain issues the orders as if they were solely in charge. This process requires a little bit of group cooperation and some brief pauses in the narrative to discuss plans, but it generally results in a much more fun experience for everyone.

sidebar.name: A Storytelling Tool
description: The rules presented here are meant to serve as a storytelling guide, providing a structure to help craft a narrative around a battle. You shouldn't think of them as prescriptive rules but as tools to aid in creating an interesting and consistent story structure that your group can participate in.

sidebar.name: What about the PCs?
description: Your player characters will have their own parts to play in the battle. No matter how imposing they are (or think they are!) do {@i not} count them as one of the units making up the active force.

sidebar.name: Story Points and Talents in Mass Combat Checks
description: Players cannot spend Story Points to upgrade {@rule mass combat} checks. The checks cover too many broad events to allow a single Story Point to have such an outsized influence. Likewise, GMs cannot spend Story Points to upgrade the difficulty of {@rule mass combat} checks.

Also, note that a {@rule mass combat} check is not a skill check. Talents that affect skill checks, combat checks, social skill checks, or other types of checks do not affect {@rule mass combat} checks.
The only talents or abilities that affect {@rule mass combat} checks are ones that specifically say they do in their rules.

sidebar.name: Considering Terrain
description: Although mechanically terrain can be distilled down to favorable (add {@dice boost}) and unfavorable (add {@dice setback}), you can still take some time to consider the terrain in play and how it might affect the ongoing battle. This extra level of detail helps bring the scenario to life.

For example, terrain might be advantageous for some forces but dangerous for others. Thick woodlands and muddy bogs would be good cover and concealment for light infantry, but tanks and armored vehicles would struggle to get through it. Mechs, however, can stride through this terrain without issue and often have the scanners to penetrate foliage and spot hidden infantry.

Likewise, fighting near a flaring star could be hazardous for {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|starfighters|eoti} and {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, as their weaker armor and shielding can't protect them from intense radiation. Heavy warships such as {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}, on the other hand, could be tough enough to ignore the flares long enough to win a battle.

In the end, you get to decide how the terrain may affect a battle for good or ill. But don't be afraid to enable your players' creative thinking when they consider how to use terrain in the ongoing fight.

sidebar.name: Ideal Difficulty
description: Although the {@rule mass combat} rules work for any size active and enemy forces, the most engaging mass combats tend to occur when the PCs and their active force begin the fight outmatched. The rules are designed to give the PCs a chance to make a crucial difference in the fight, so the narrative can be much more compelling when an outnumbered force of underdogs fights their way to victory, rather than a powerful force crushing a weaker foe.

sidebar.name: Notable Nemeses
description: Although the rules in {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|Getting the PCs Involved} apply to the player characters, battles may also be fought against enemy forces led and aided by notable and dangerous adversaries. They may even be individuals who the PCs have been clashing with over the course of entire adventures or campaigns, and you certainly want to make their presence felt on the battlefield.

All of the rules in {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|Getting the PCs Involved} can also be used by rival- or nemesis-level adversaries, meaning they can make a {@skill Leadership} skill check as described in {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|Leading the Fight}, perform other skill checks as described in {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|Supporting the Troops}, and even attack the acting force directly as described in {@rule Mass Combat: Where the PCs Fit In|Getting Involved Directly}. In all of these cases, just reverse the results of success.

items: {@b Leading the Fight:} They replace the enemy force's ranks in quality with their ranks in {@skill Leadership}, or increase the quality by 1.
{@b Supporting the Troops:} They either remove {@dice boost} or add {@dice setback} to the check, and if they generate at least {@symbols sss}, they can add {@symbols f} to the results instead.

{@b Getting Involved Directly:} Success adds {@dice setback} to the check, and any {@rule Critical Injuries} and {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hits} can be inflicted on the PCs and their vehicles.

description: Note that to avoid bogging down the {@rule mass combat}, we recommend having no more than half as many notable adversaries on the side of the enemy force as there are PCs in your group.

sidebar.name: Convoy Escort
description: This adventure seed works for cohorts that have ties to the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates'|eoti} militaries, or for cohorts assigned to the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} to help the {@rule Emirates of Hacan||eoti}.

The players' cohort has been given command of a {@vehicle Sebeko Escort|Sebeko} assigned to escort an important convoy of relief supplies to a world that has been blockaded by one of the Great Civilizations. The players' position is largely a formality; the convoy's main escort is a much larger and more powerful {@vehicle War Zebek}.

However, when the convoy stops to refuel, the cohort's {@vehicle Sebeko Escort|Sebeko} is set upon by a flight of six {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort starfighters|eoti} (page 144 of {@title Embers of the Imperium}). While the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} deal with the fighters, the {@vehicle War Zebek} is attacked by an unidentified cruiser, which destroys the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} ship but suffers heavy damage and retreats.

The convoy is still a week away from the blockaded world, and now the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} must escort six undefended merchant vessels on their own. Worse, the unidentified cruiser has been sent by {@i someone} to ensure the convoy never arrives. Once they make repairs, they will be back.

sidebar.name: Legends of the Lost Warship
description: While the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} insist that every grand sorbarrk that isn't currently in their possession has been lost or destroyed, rumors persist that at least one other grand sorbarrk still exists. The {@i Kamdorn Stillness} was lost during the chaotic years of the Twilight Wars, vanishing into Shifting Space when it was pursued by a {@rule Sardakk N'orr||eoti} battlefleet. Grizzled wayfarers and ancient spacers insist that if you can find your way through its labyrinthine depths and perilous grav-currents, you will find the grand sorbarrk in the heart of that cursed region, reactor still idling and systems on standby after three millennia.

sidebar.name: The Flying Squadron
description: One of the few squadrons that has continued in some form or another for the last few centuries, the Flying Squadron was said to have originally been formed during the Dark Years by a {@archetype Human||eoti} commodore who was a keen student of {@rule Jord||eoti}'s ancient history. At the time, the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} was in a standoff with the Nargoni Technocracy, a repressive dictatorship that already controlled several star systems and was lusting after worlds recently settled by the {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti}. Instead of trying to defend each colony individually, Commodore Burman recommended forming a squadron of fast cruisers that could remain nearby and quickly respond to any attack. The Flying Squadron soon proved its worth by routing a Nargoni invasion fleet, and later it fought with distinction during the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} campaign to disarm the Technocracy and liberate its subject worlds.

Today the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} maintains the Flying Squadron as a quick-response unit to any crisis among its holdings or stations scattered across the galaxy. It consists of half a dozen of the most advanced cruisers sailing under the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} flag, with experienced captains and crews chosen for their proven flexibility and quick thinking under fire.

sidebar.name: Boarding Party!
description: This adventure seed can work for any {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} cohort who is on good terms with the {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti}.

{@rule The Galactic Council||eoti} has voted to try a ruthless warlord for crimes against civilian populations and has dispatched the players' cohort as part of a task force to bring them to justice. During the resulting space battle, the PCs are given a {@vehicle Raider Assault Boarding Ram} and up to two {@vehicle Freebooter Interceptor|Freebooter interceptors} by a {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti} captain. The {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} must fight their way through a defensive screen of four {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor starfighters|eoti} ({@title Embers of the Imperium}, page 143) and fire from the warlord's {@vehicle Pirate Raider|pirate raider|eoti} flagship ({@title Embers of the Imperium}, page 152), then ram and board the vessel. Once aboard, the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} still have a tough fight against the warlord and their fanatical crew.

sidebar.name: Saar Naval Architecture
description: There's an old {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} saying, one that defines the culture's entire outlook on life: an individual must always be ready to look to the left side of their tools. In essence, every tool or implement has a second, often more martial, use. It also means that every {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} should be ready at a moment's notice to pick up their tools and use them to defend their fellows by any means necessary. The {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} spacegoing assets are likely the clearest and most fully realized expression of that ancient axiom. Every ship, no matter how small, is both a tool and a weapon—to be used one way in peace and wielded another way in war. This is reflected in the way the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} design their ships. {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} vessels are boxy and utilitarian with little care given to style or appearance. They are tools, made to be cherished, cared for, and used hard. They are also weapons, armed and armored to protect their crews, their cargoes, and, if worst comes to worst, the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} people in general.

sidebar.name: Find of the Century
description: This adventure seed works for any cohort who is willing to take on some questionably legal work on the side.

The players' cohort is on another mission when they're contacted by an old friend with criminal links. An ambitious {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} captain has found an ancient Lazax treasure barque. The only problem is the ship is deep within the immense ring system of a gas giant, and the captain's regular {@vehicle Scavenger Zeta Suit|Scavenger Zeta} jock crew refuses to negotiate the chaotic maze of shifting stone and ice.

If the PCs agree, they are provided {@vehicle Scavenger Zeta Suit|Scavenger Zeta suits} and sent to retrieve the riches aboard the barque. Charting a course through the rings and avoiding the erratic orbits of debris is bad enough, but when they arrive, they find the ship still has power, and several automated weapons open fire on them!

sidebar.name: Heavy Tractor Beam Emitters
description: Each floating factory is equipped with a handful of tractor beam emitters used for moving ships, dry docks, and gantries around the station. In a pinch, multiple emitters can be used to grab enemy ships and tear them apart—a slow but dramatic kind of destruction that makes many enemies think twice about approaching one of these behemoths.

If a ship has been {@rule immobilized} by the floating factory's tractor beam emitter array, the gunner of the emitter may make a {@difficulty hard|gunnery} as an action. If the check is successful, the target suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, plus 1 hull trauma per {@symbols s}. The gunner may spend {@symbols a} to add +10 to the results of the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} per {@symbols a} spent. {@symbols t} may be spent to either inflict 10 additional hull trauma or add +25 to the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} result.

sidebar.name: Covert Operations
description: This adventure seed works for any cohort on favorable terms with the {@rule Yssaril Tribes||eoti}.

The {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti} have taken control of a small neutral world, and {@rule The Galactic Council|the Galactic Council|eoti} has dispatched the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} to learn what has happened to the population before any member faction authorizes military action. The PCs' cohort boards an {@vehicle Orchestrator Ambush Carrier|Orchestrator ambush carrier} to sneak in close to the world, before being inserted onto the surface via high-altitude drop via {@vehicle Exfiltrator Air Raft|Exfiltrator air rafts}.

The cohort has to perform plenty of stealth and skulduggery on the surface, but the action heats up when they're discovered before their extraction. Now the PCs have to fight their way off the surface before the {@vehicle Orchestrator Ambush Carrier|Orchestrator} is forced to flee from the {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti}.

sidebar.name: Augmented Identify & Ideation (AII) Control Suites
description: The {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} have been experimenting with more advanced automation to replace a {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} pilot with a mechanical one able to calculate, predict, and respond to threats. While fast, responsive, and predictive, AII isn't really artificial intelligence. These automated units don't have sentience or sapience; a pet is more intelligent than these control systems.
An AII control suite counts as a minion with a rating of 2 in all characteristics; group skills in {@skill Gunnery}, {@skill Operating}, and {@skill Piloting}; and a wound threshold of 3.

sidebar.name: Bending the Laws of Physics
description: The {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} military is always trying to gain a strategic advantage over their enemies with the invention of new technologies. Nowhere is this more evident than with the recently developed spatial conduit cylinder and transit diodes.

As large as a midsized asteroid, the rapidly spinning cylinder is made of a classified hyperdense exotic material. When ships enter the cylinder, they are able to instantly accelerate to superluminal velocities previously thought unobtainable. This would be a game-changing technology…if the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Universities|eoti} can work out the kinks. Right now, the chief problem is slowing the ships down again. The speeds are so high that using superluminal engines to decelerate can take weeks, during which the ship overshoots its target (and sometimes the borders of the galaxy). The long-reliable alternative of steering toward a planet and using its gravity to decelerate has proved equally problematic. The ships do decelerate to subluminal speeds, but it happens so quickly that the vessels and their occupants crumple into a lump of degenerate matter.

Transit diodes—essentially stabilized micro-wormholes that allow instantaneous travel between two planets—would seem a better solution. However, aside from the problem of the huge energy drain involved in creating the wormhole, some of the transits have been a little {@i too} instantaneous. Violation of causality principles, while fodder for many a paper, can't serve as a basis for troop movements if it wipes out the existence of the troops in the first place. (See papers {@i Causality Violation Detection Parameters: Has This Already Will Have Had Happened?} and {@i The Folklore of "Ghost" Section 22H: Future Fact, Past Fiction.})

sidebar.name: Jol-Nar Ship Naming Conventions
description: As part of the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} doctrine of showcasing their military might as a deterrence, ships have both a {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} name and a univoca name. {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} diplomats claim that the use of univoca demonstrates their willingness to share information with the rest of the galaxy. Most military analysts from other Great Civilizations suspect {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} leaders just got tired of hearing other species butcher the names of their precious warships.

sidebar.name: For Science!
description: This adventure seed can work for any {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} cohort.

The {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar||eoti} has just approached the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} with an unusual request. One of their {@vehicle Tiirah Cabba (Sequester) Bulk Transport/Carrier|bulk carriers}, JNS {@i Kamtkora}, was conducting experiments on the edges of {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} space when it stopped sending back status reports. Now the ship seems to be fleeing as quickly as possible toward the edges of the galaxy and won't respond to hails. Worse, its engines appear extremely enhanced, and it is outrunning anything the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Universities|eoti} send after it.

To catch {@i Kamtkora}, the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Universities|eoti} want to put the PCs on a modified {@i {@vehicle Otoh Arsi (Questor) Cruiser|Questor}}-class cruiser and fire it out of their newest invention, a {@sidebar Bending the Laws of Physics|spatial transit cylinder}. Provided the PCs survive the transit and deceleration (see page 110), they must persuade {@i Kamtkora} to stop. Unfortunately, its captain is convinced that the black hole in the center of the galaxy is about to explode (based on his own "impeccable" mathematics) and the fleeing vessel is the only hope of preserving life. How the PCs make the captain listen to reason (and what horrors they might encounter beyond the galactic rim) should make an exciting adventure.

sidebar.name: Variant Technologies
description: {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} ships vary so wildly, it's impossible to document all the variants. Instead, you can apply one of these variant technologies to any of the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} ship profiles presented here to represent a vessel that has been modified beyond the norm. Choose a result or roll randomly on {@table 9-1: Variant Technologies}.

sidebar.name: War Suns Beyond Muaat
description: When the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} fled {@rule Muaat||eoti}, they took copies of all the data and designs from their shipbuilding complex there and later built additional {@vehicle War Sun|war suns} elsewhere. In time, {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar's|eoti} {@vehicle War Sun|war sun} designs spread among the Great Civilizations. Today, all Great Civilizations have at least the capability of constructing a {@vehicle War Sun|war sun} based on the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} design, though not all of them see much value in such a tremendous undertaking. As a result, operational {@vehicle War Sun|war suns} are exceptionally rare.

Other civilizations' {@vehicle War Sun|war suns} share the stats of the {@rule Embers of Muaat||eoti} {@vehicle War Sun (Muaat)|war sun} with a few modifications. Increase armor to 7; reduce FTL speed to average; remove the incendos flare array, the magmus reactor, and star forge vehicle special rules.

sidebar.name: Into the Fire
description: This adventure seed can work for any {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} cohort that is not affiliated with the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar||eoti}.

A few decades ago, the humanoid reptilian species known as the Natal'rie established a colony in the Calaxi system. Unfortunately, the Natal'rie were not the best astrophysicists and did not realize the Calaxi star was inherently unstable. A change in stellar weather caused the Natal'rie colony to be barraged with intense solar flares and plasma storms, forcing the colonists into underground shelters. With no sign of the storms dying down any time soon, the colonists must evacuate before they run out of supplies.

The Natal'rie have no ships capable of standing up to this severe weather, so their representative on the {@rule The Galactic Council|Galactic Council|eoti} has asked the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} for aid. The {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti}, in turn, have to approach the {@rule Embers of Muaat||eoti}, as the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} are the only ones with ships that can survive (and thrive) in intense solar flares.

The PCs have to convince the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} to loan them a carrier vessel (and ideally a cruiser escort). Then the PCs have to obtain {@gear Sealed Environmental Suit|environmental suits|eoti} so they can survive inside a {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} ship and help the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} convert passenger containers to house the equally flammable colonists without incinerating them. Piloting through solar flares should also be a challenge, but the whole situation may be an opportunity for an unscrupulous PC to try to access information on the classified magmus reactor.

sidebar.name: Arms Exports
description: After centuries of expanding its armed forces, the {@rule Federation of Sol||eoti} has a robust military-industrial complex that forms a powerful voting bloc within the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation's|eoti} House of Industry. As an industry is wont to do, it has consistently grown, outstripping the needs of even the Federal Army and Fleet.

To ensure that the military-industrial complex has a market, successive High Ministers have authorized the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation's|eoti} military to sell older hardware and vehicles to independent worlds with friendly relationships toward {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti}. This generates wealth that the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} can then spend on newer equipment, ensuring its military has the latest tech while also guaranteeing hundreds of smaller civilizations are armed with {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol's|eoti} surplus.

sidebar.name: Drop Assault
description: This adventure seed is best suited for any cohort.

When the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} orders the PCs' cohort to conduct a peacekeeping operation on a remote colony world, the last thing they expect is help from the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti}. The colony world is split between settlers from {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} and another major galactic power, but the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} seems willing to have the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} keep the peace between its people and their opponents. In fact, they even provide the PCs with some {@vehicle ZS Thunderbolt Mk2|Thunderbolt mechs} that they can drop directly into the hostilities to put an end to the fighting.

When the PCs deploy into the conflict zone, they have a chance to use force or negotiation to convince the armed settlers (who are equipped with two to three {@vehicle Predator Rambler|Predator ramblers} [page 39] and a {@vehicle Light Mech|light mech|eoti} [{@title Embers of the Imperium}, page 140] on each side) to stand down. But then they are attacked by mechs from the other galactic power. The twist, however, is that these are stolen mechs operated by {@adversary Sol Spec Ops Drop Trooper|Sol Spec Ops|eoti} forces. The {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} figures that a bunch of dead {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} will give {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} the perfect {@i casus belli} for a full invasion.

sidebar.name: Ground Support
description: Until recently, the Federal Fleet assumed it could meet all of the army's ground attack needs with its {@vehicle F5 Hurricane Mk5|Hurricane} squadrons. However, the series of skirmishes with {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} forces known as the Altreia Incident demonstrated how untrue that was. Too many {@vehicle F5 Hurricane Mk5|Hurricanes} were shot down by {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} air defenses while trying to get within strike range, and their lightning mass drivers proved to be wholly ineffective against hardened fortifications. The fleet recognized that a new approach was needed.

The {@vehicle B84 Typhoon Torpedo Bomber|Typhoon's} massive wing-mounted torpedo payload made it impossible to fly in an atmosphere, but {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} engineers developed a pair of weapon pods that were both lighter and much more aerodynamic. These pods could hold a shard missile system for standoff infantry support or a pair of massive stonecracker rockets for hardened targets. Although most ground support missions are still performed by {@vehicle F5 Hurricane Mk5|Hurricanes}, carriers now stock a supply of these weapon pods so that they can adapt their {@vehicle B84 Typhoon Torpedo Bomber|Typhoons} to atmospheric attack craft.

sidebar.name: The Crimson Baronet
description: This adventure seed is best suited for any cohort with obligations to the {@rule Barony of Letnev||eoti}.

The infamous Crimson Baronet has long been one of the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony's|eoti} elite ace pilots, but her skill is matched by her impertinence and disrespect for senior command. She finally went too far when she shot down a fellow pilot and fled.

The {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} wants her dead, but the Crimson Baronet is a military hero to {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} commoners. Therefore, a {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} official approaches the PCs. Their job is to kill the renegade without involving the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony's|eoti} military, so that leadership can claim the Baronet died "heroically serving all the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} people."

To maintain the charade, the PCs are not given any {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} equipment and have to scrounge fighters from other factions. To make matters worse, the Crimson Baronet's ground crew joined her little rebellion and stole a {@vehicle Denoz Warstalker}. So, the PCs have to contend with a corvette, an ace pilot in an {@vehicle Allired Voidcarver}, and three four-ship flights of {@vehicle Valeward Drone Fighter|Valeward drone fighters}. Things get even more complicated if the PCs learn why the Baronet rebelled (she refused to fire on a ship full of refugees that may have also been carrying smuggled weapons and killed her wingman when he went to destroy the ship). The PCs have to choose whether to kill the Baronet, side with her against the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti}, or invent some ruse to allow her to start a new life elsewhere. Perhaps the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} are hiring?

sidebar.name: Drone Fighters
description: Drone fighters are versatile, expendable forces that can operate under a rudimentary algorithm or the direct control of an authorized remote operator within strategic range. They can also escort high-value craft or ace pilots across chaotic battlefields.
Drone fighter squads can operate in the following modes (switching modes requires an {@difficulty average|computers} from an authorized user via a special encrypted comms frequency):

items: {@b Independent Mode}: Treat the drone as a minion group with 1 {@characteristic Agility} and the {@skill Gunnery} skill as a group skill. It can only respond to simple commands over the proper encrypted channel, such as attack target, defend target, travel to coordinates, and enter sleep mode.

{@b Remote Operator}: Use the remote operator's {@characteristic Agility} and ranks in {@skill Piloting} and {@skill Gunnery}. Increase the difficulty of all {@skill Piloting} and {@skill Gunnery} checks once, but add {@dice boost} to all {@skill Gunnery} checks for each drone in the minion group beyond the first.

{@b Escort Mode}: The drone minion group loses its turn in the {@rule determine Initiative|initiative} order and attaches to a control craft. Any time the control craft is the target of a successful attack, your character may sacrifice a drone to ignore all damage from a single hit as an out-of-turn {@rule Incidentals|incidental}. Also, when the control craft makes an attack, add {@dice boost} to the check if 1-3 drones are attached, {@dice boost|2} for 4-8 drones, and {@dice boost|3} for 9+ drones.

sidebar.name: Surgical Strike
description: This adventure seed works for any cohort that is on good terms with the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom||eoti} and has an honorable reputation.

The PCs' cohort has been seconded to a member of the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} intelligence services to resolve a tricky situation. A peace delegation of {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} negotiators were meeting aboard a space station with representatives from the {@rule Federation of Sol||eoti} and {@rule Barony of Letnev||eoti} when terrorists aboard a {@vehicle Corvette|corvette|eoti} captured the station. They have threatened to use the {@vehicle Corvette|corvette's|eoti} weapons to destroy the station if their demands (a public apology from both the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} and the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} for the occupation and destruction of {@rule Archon Ren and Archon Tau|Archon Tau|eoti}) are not met.

The terrorists are actually agents of a faction in the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} government working to embarrass the Baron. The Baron intends to send in a {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} to destroy the terrorists. The loss of all three delegations is acceptable to the Baron, but the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} don't want to see their people die because of {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} infighting.

The PCs are equipped with one or two {@vehicle Bbraj Tactical Bomber|Bbraj tactical bombers} (depending on the size of the cohort) and told to take out the {@vehicle Corvette|corvette's|eoti} weapons with a surgical strike before they can be used to kill the hostages. However, to ensure the strike won't cause collateral damage, one of the PCs must don a {@gear Space Suit|spacesuit|eoti} and sneak onto the outside of the space station in order to serve as an attack controller.

sidebar.name: Intercession and Intervention Orbital and Deep Space Cannons
description: The lynchpin of the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha's|eoti} defenses are their deep space cannons, whether in ground emplacements, orbital batteries, starships, or even {@vehicle Indomitus Heavy Mech|Indomitus mechs}. {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} deep space batteries use ultraheavy grav-repellers to hurl projectiles at a substantial portion of the speed of light. Each round is a cross between a shell and a missile; although they are fired from specialized launchers, they have pre-programmed target recognition algorithms and maneuvering systems onboard that allow them to track targets as they close the range. Both intercession and intervention cannons need either line of sight or precise targeting data from a spotter. Due to {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} caution about indiscriminate use of weapons, their smart missiles are programmed to favor self-destruction if a positive target ID cannot be achieved at the destination.

These weapons follow the expanded rules for strategic range combat (see {@b Firing Weapons at Extreme and Strategic Ranges} on page 9). Hitting a target without line of sight from the firing unit requires communication with a spotter. Crossing an entire system may take the projectile two, three, or even more rounds at the GM's discretion.

sidebar.name: Powered Armor Assault
description: This adventure seed works for any cohort that is on good terms with the {@rule Sardakk N'orr||eoti} and has a militaristic bent.

The {@rule Sardakk N'orr||eoti} colony on Kalonis Delta has come under attack! {@rule Vuil'raith Cabal|Vuil'raith|eoti} forces recently appeared out of wormhole fissures and began swarming across the moon, attacking {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} citizens en masse and overwhelming the small garrison. Evacuation is the only option, but the main colonial settlement is several hundred kilometers away from the only spaceport and currently under heavy siege.

The PCs happen to be in a nearby system when the call for help goes out. A {@rule Sardakk N'orr||eoti} {@vehicle Oss'orr "Exolander" Carrier|exolander} is close enough to respond, but the carrier was being used to transport mechs to {@rule Quinarra and Tren'lak|Quinarra|eoti} and has almost no soldiers aboard. The captain asks the PCs to join their rescue mission.

The {@vehicle Oss'orr "Exolander" Carrier|exolander} with the PCs lands at the Kalonis Delta spaceport, and the PCs have to set off on a hundred-kilometer trip to reach the settlement. There they need to organize the remaining colonists and escort whatever evacuation convoy they can arrange back to the {@vehicle Oss'orr "Exolander" Carrier|exolander}. The only bright spot is that although the {@vehicle Oss'orr "Exolander" Carrier|exolander} is short on soldiers, it is carrying dozens of brand-new {@vehicle Char'eet "Valkyrie" Exoskeleton|Valkyrie exoskeletons}—enough for every PC. Time to go monster hunting!

sidebar.name: Life Imitates Myth
description: {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} warship designs feature what many would describe as a sea creature or crustacean-based aesthetic, seemingly at odds with the insectoid species' own morphology and native environment. However, one need only study ancient {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} mythology for answers. Many of their epics follow G'orr, a warrior-envoy who journeyed through mystical realms to rescue and nurture the egg of the queen mother until her hatching.

The most popular stories feature G'orr negotiating an ocean-covered paradise realm, a natural fantasy for those born to the arid wastelands of {@rule Quinarra and Tren'lak|Quinarra|eoti}. The realm is filled with leviathans, both benevolent and selfish, at war over sharing their water. To the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti}, the sight of a {@vehicle Natat'torr "Exotrireme" Dreadnought|Natat'torr dreadnought} swimming through orbit generates pride, comfort, and awe at the thought of Sardakk the Queen Mother elevating herself from being at the mercy of the old gods to mastering them.

Critics of the theory ask how pre-superluminal {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} even knew what sea creatures looked like. The most likely answer is the discovery of smaller creatures with similar forms fossilized in dried-out subterranean lake beds. Unfortunately, the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} are notoriously poor record keepers and care little about ancient history, particularly not at the expense of fables that reinforce the queen's place in society, entertain the masses, and form cultural touchstones.

sidebar.name: Diapause and Starships
description: {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} troops and crews are capable of entering {@i diapause}, a form of hibernation that requires little food, water, or air. Such resting soldiers can come to full alertness at a moment's notice, and it's common for them to enter diapause in their crash restraints, unaware of a battle until their dropship is mere minutes from its landing zone. This ability allows the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} to pack far more crew and soldiers onto their ships than most other navies can without requiring excess space for food, air, and water stores.

sidebar.name: N'orr Naming Conventions
description: The other Great Civilizations have difficulty pronouncing and distinguishing {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} phonemes. As such, the {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} have settled on their own names and translations for many {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} warships and starships. Examples include the {@vehicle Kess'or "Fury" Fighter|"Fury" fighter} and {@vehicle Curr'soral "Exobireme" Cruiser|"Exobireme" cruiser}, among others. These names are rarely used by {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} forces, but are a lot easier to shout across a {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} bridge under combat conditions.

sidebar.name: Winnu Naming Conventions
description: In the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} military, each fleet or legion bears the name of its commander. This builds something of a cult of personality among the officer ranks. However, it also drives commanders to success, no matter the cost. After all, to fail is to see one's name stripped from the command, which for the proud officers of the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} is a fate truly worse than death.

sidebar.name: Winnu Vessel Appearance
description: Given the {@rule Winnu|Winnu's|eoti} adoration of the Lazax, it's no surprise that the aesthetics of their ships closely match those of their predecessors. White lacquered hull panels edged in gold or duranium alloy cover their surfaces, mirroring the colors the Lazax loved. The crest of the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} emperor is often featured prominently on the hull, a splash of brilliant color across the smooth plating.

sidebar.name: Coup Attempt
description: This adventure seed works for any cohort that is on good terms with the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} and has a penchant for undercover operations.

An agent of the Lumenari Inspectorate approaches the PCs' cohort with a significant problem. They have uncovered evidence that a captain in the Navis Guard is planning to assassinate the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} emperor by using their {@i {@vehicle Antiphon-class Principal Warship|Antiphon}}-class dreadnought to bombard the imperial palace on Winnu! Worse, the agent has evidence that members of the Inspectorate may be involved, including their own superiors.

To stop the coup before it starts, the agent enlists the PCs to steal a {@i {@vehicle Hyperion-class High Cruiser|Hyperion}}-class cruiser equipped with an oversight module. Once aboard, the agent will bring over a few Inspectorate crew members who can be trusted. Then all the PCs have to do is intercept the rogue {@vehicle Antiphon-class Principal Warship|Antiphon} on the edges of {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} space. Oh, but the agent wants the captain alive so that they can find out who the leaders of the plot are. That shouldn't be a problem, right?

rule.name: Facing and Turning
description: Positioning and facing already have some importance in vehicle rules, particularly when it comes to mounted guns. Most vehicle weapons have rules that give them a firing arc of some combination of front, rear, left, and right (or forward, aft, port, and starboard). Although smaller ships are often particularly agile and can spin and roll, larger ships are a bit too cumbersome to turn easily. To turn, they should use this modified version of the {@rule Reposition} vehicle maneuver.

description.title: Facing, Momentum, and Forced Movement
entries: The rules for {@rule Steering|steering} and forced movement (page 221, {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook) basically mean that as long as a vehicle is traveling at any sort of speed, it keeps moving. What direction it moves, however, is left up to the PC piloting the vehicle.

This works well as a base rule, especially since the rules have to cover all kinds of vehicles in all kinds of settings. However, in the {@setting Twilight Imperium||eoti} setting, momentum and direction of travel play a more important role, represented by the following rule.

{@b When a spaceship performs its forced movement during its turn, it must move in the direction it is facing at that moment.} For example, a character uses the {@rule Reposition} maneuver to turn a starship to the right at the beginning of their turn. Then at the end of their turn, the forced movement of their ship sends the ship to the right (relative to its original facing).

This lets the rules simulate a version of inertia in space without too many complex limitations or rules. It also makes the {@rule Reposition} maneuver very important for pilots, as that's how they steer the ship!

entries.title: Agile Fighters
entries: Smaller spacecraft like {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|starfighters|eoti} (or their atmospheric equivalents) have several advantages over larger vessels. One of these is their agility. {@b Any vehicle that is silhouette 4 or smaller can change its facing by any amount immediately before or after they perform their forced movement.}

rule.name: Updated Dangerous Driving Action
description: The Dangerous Driving action was originally designed for smaller vehicles, but it can also be used for larger vessels. If you use this action while controlling a vehicle with the {@skill Operating} skill, you make an {@skill Operating} check (instead of a {@skill Piloting} check) with a difficulty equal to half the vehicle's silhouette (rounding up).

rule.name: Reposition

items: {@b Pilot Only:} Yes
{@b Silhouette:} Any
{@b Current Speed:} Any (Special circumstances apply to stationary vehicles.)

description: If the vehicle's speed is 1 or higher, the pilot may move the vehicle to another location that is within short range of their current location. Alternatively, the pilot may change the direction that their vehicle is facing by up to 45 degrees.

If the vehicle is stationary, the pilot may {@i only} use the Reposition maneuver to change facing by up to 45 degrees (some vehicles, at the GM's discretion, may not be able to turn when stationary).
If a vehicle is silhouette 4 or smaller, the pilot may change their facing by any amount when performing the Reposition maneuver.

While smaller ships and vehicles can still pull sharp turns, this rule makes facing play a more significant role when commanding larger starships because the pilot cannot turn to confront a new opponent immediately. Facing also becomes more important when you factor in forced movement from the {@b {@rule Steering}} section on page 221 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook, as explained in the next section.

rule.name: Ramming and Boarding
description: Ramming an enemy ship with your own vessel and sending teams of raiders to board it with pistols and blades in hand may seem particularly fantastical, but it fits well into a space opera setting like {@setting Twilight Imperium||eoti}. This section describes how to use the existing rules to create both situations.

description.title: Ramming Attack
entries: A ramming attack is just a deliberate collision, and thus it is a tactic for the wildly desperate or the foolishly brave. However, sometimes that foolishness is called for in dangerous situations. Some shipbuilders even build rams or reinforced prows into their larger warships so that the ramming vessel can do much more damage in such situations.

Before a character can ram their vehicle into another, they first need to successfully reach the target. The best way to do this is to have the character perform a {@rule Dangerous Driving} action (see page 227 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook). If they succeed, they cause a collision. The difficulty should be set using {@table 1-1: Speed Advantage Difficulty}, which is {@table III.2-18: Speed Advantage Difficulty} on page 229 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook reprinted here for convenience. Basically, the faster the vehicle that is attempting to ram is going, the easier it is to maneuver to hit their target and the more difficult it is for the target to avoid them.

entries.title: Results of Ramming
entries: If the check is successful, a major collision occurs (see {@b {@rule Collisions}} on page 222 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook). Both the ramming vehicle and the target suffer a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, but they do have a chance to reduce the effects based on their defense. Remember that the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} may be more severe due to the speed that the ramming vehicle was traveling (see {@table III.2-14: Vehicle Speeds in Structured Encounters} on page 221 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook).

In addition to the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, you can also have the ramming vehicle inflict hull trauma or system strain on the target by spending {@symbols a} from the check (possibly on a one-for-one basis, but perhaps more if circumstances warrant it). Likewise, {@symbols h} or {@symbols d} can inflict additional damage on the ramming vehicle. If the check fails, you can still have both vehicles suffer a minor collision (described on page 222 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook) by spending several {@symbols a} or a {@symbols t}.

We should point out that ramming is likely as dangerous to the vehicle attempting the ram as it is to the target. This is by design; crashing two ships or vehicles together is usually fatal for both. Also, the rules for {@rule collisions} call out that, at your discretion, very large vehicles may simply ignore {@rule collisions} with much smaller vehicles (and the smaller of the two may be destroyed outright without even rolling a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}!). You can always tell your players that crashing their {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|starfighter|eoti} into the prow of an enemy {@vehicle dreadnought||eoti}—like a bug smashing against a car's windshield—isn't going to accomplish anything but their own demise.

description.title: Boarding Attacks
entries: Boarding an enemy ship can be the climax of a successful chase or the highlight of a daring rescue. Likewise, struggling to repel enemy boarders is a dramatic encounter where the stakes are nothing less than keeping your vessel in your own hands.

Boarding actions can be easily represented in the existing rules. However, there are a few points to keep in mind as they occur. Primarily, how close two vehicles need to be for one of them to attempt a boarding action and what the boarders need to do to get aboard their target.

Boarding actions should only occur when a vehicle is engaged with another vehicle. As noted in both the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook and the {@sidebar Range Bands in Space} sidebar on page 9, when dealing with starships, {@rule range bands} tend to represent much greater distances than they do on the ground. Only engaged, which represents two ships either docked together or at most one hundred meters apart, is close enough for people to travel from one ship to the other.

Sometimes ships have special pieces of equipment such as boarding tubes that allow them to basically latch onto another ship, drill through their hull, and create a passageway between the two vessels. The exact rules for this are covered in those ships' profiles. If a ship doesn't have that equipment, the boarders have to do things more dangerously by donning spacesuits and jumping or boosting themselves from one ship to the other. If this happens, remember that while the ships may be using {@rule range bands} that represent hundreds or even millions of kilometers, the boarders are still operating at personal scale. So it may take a whole turn (or more!) to cross the gulf between ships. If the two ships are still moving, the boarders may be left behind if they can't reach their target in time.
Once the boarders get to their target, they still must get inside. This can be handled narratively, but we have some suggestions for ways to attempt it:

items: {@b Hacking an airlock:} The boarders may find an airlock and hack its computer with a {@difficulty hard|computers} to unlock and open it.

{@b Prying open an airlock or hatch:} The boarders could attempt to pry open an airlock or hatch with an {@difficulty average|athletics} if they have the right tool (such as a {@gear sarween gamma press||eoti}).

{@b Cutting or blasting through the hull:} A more direct approach (admittedly with a risk of explosive decompression), this tactic does require the boarders to have powerful explosive charges or cutting tools. If they do, they can use them to make a {@difficulty hard|mechanics}. Failure here may result in the boarders doing the job too well and inflicting major damage on the ship.

entries: We also want to note that most military vessels have additional protections against boarding actions, such as more secure computers and thicker hulls and hatches. You should increase the difficulty once or twice for any checks made to attempt to board a military vessel.
Once the boarders make entry, they still have to face the enemy crew. This can be handled with normal structured encounter rules.

rule.name: Distant Missile and Torpedo Fire
description: In the {@setting Twilight Imperium||eoti} setting, factions build weapons with truly impressive ranges. Some can fire projectiles across star systems or to launch missiles that take hours or even days to reach their targets. To represent this, these weapons can fire out to {@b {@rule Range Bands|strategic range}}.

Strategic range is covered on page 224 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook, and the {@sidebar Range Bands in Space} sidebar. As noted in the sidebar, since strategic range covers such wide distances, you as the GM can determine that something is simply too far away for even strategic-range weaponry to hit. However, even when something at strategic or extreme range can be attacked, the weapons may take some time to reach their target. This is especially true with missiles and torpedoes.

Missiles and torpedoes tend to move as fast as the fastest starships, but that's still nothing compared to the eyeblink speeds of heavy mass driver weapons or beam weapons that travel at the literal speed of light. Missiles and torpedoes make up for this by having a greater absolute range, as well as guidance systems to home in on their targets when they get there.
To represent these slower but extremely long-ranged weapons, you can use the following rule.

description.title: Firing Weapons at Extreme and Strategic Ranges
entries: When you make an attack with a starship's torpedoes or missiles (or similar weapons) at a target at extreme or strategic range, spend an action to determine and build the dice pool (based on the current range of the target and other circumstances that affect the check), but do not make the check yet. At the end of the next turn of the target's pilot, make the combat check as an out-of-turn {@rule Incidentals|incidental}. If the target is no longer in range of the weapon or could not be hit by the attack for some reason, the check fails. If the attack misses but you trigger the {@quality Guided} quality of the weapon, use the rules for the {@quality Guided} quality on page 87 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook as normal (the missile or torpedo is now close enough to try to reacquire the target without further delay).

rule.name: Fighter Minion Groups
