vehicle.name: Pride of Kenara

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

weapons.name: Shoulder-mounted shard missile battery
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within medium range.

description: The war mechs of the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} tend to be quick-striding bipedal machines. All models are designed for long-distance operations in hostile environments, whether those are the deserts of the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} homeworlds or the alien environments on some distant planet. This gives the mechs and their crews the glamour and mystique of the cavalry troopers of ancient armies, ranging far beyond the main force, scouting the enemy, and conducting ferocious hit-and-fade attacks. Any soldier in an ordri desires to pilot a mech, and every mech pilot in the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} wants the chance to pilot a Pride of Kenara.

Although easily as large as most heavy mechs, the Pride of Kenara only requires a two-person crew. Though they carry lighter armor than the mechs of some other factions, they have an enviable top speed and impressive endurance, with lances of mechs staying in the field for weeks at a time. The Pride of Kenara also sports a unique weapon: an oversized shudder lance that can carve through enemy mechs and vehicles with a single blow. This only boosts the pilots' mystique as a sort of knight-errant, and if the senior commanders of an ordri take the field, they often do so at the helm of a Pride of Kenara.

vehicle.name: Scarhawk Fighter

weapons.name: Seeker missiles
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: The military philosophies of the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirate|eoti} armies have long focused on better endurance and self-reliance in their units. This may be because of their extensive experience with desert warfare, where the ability to travel long distances without support is vital. But whatever the source, it is a philosophy that still prevails in the ordrim and the Sword Fleet, and one that guides their preference in starfighters.

While the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} produce their share of interceptors, the heavier Scarhawk is the preeminent fighter craft among {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} pilots. Not only is it an absolute pleasure to fly and supremely adaptable, its sleek arrowhead shape makes it a beautiful machine. Different ordrim tend to paint their Scarhawks in sharp patterns of blues, blacks, greens, and even silver and copper, but only the fighters of the Sword Fleet bear the distinctive crimson and gold colors of the Quieron.

The {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} use the Scarhawk for both air support and space superiority missions. Instead of dedicated anti-ship missiles, the fighter carries an internal cluster pod that spews out bursts of smaller projectiles to attack ground targets or larger vessels. The weapons have limited range and are unguided, but most {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} aces prefer to fly close enough that they have a hard time missing.

vehicle.name: Condor Bomber
description: The main bomber in both the ordrim and the Sword Fleet, the Condor is slightly smaller than most {@vehicle Star Bomber|star bombers|eoti} and has no FTL capabilities. However, the gull-winged craft's aerodynamic lines allow it to operate just as well in an atmosphere as in the void, and it has impressive subluminal endurance. Condor crews claim they can fly from one end of their star system to the other without refueling or loiter on station for days before launching a strike.

Unfortunately, the Condor's slightly smaller size limits its payload, especially compared to other bombers. To make up for this, the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} eschewed traditional rocket or mass driver payloads, choosing instead to equip the Condor with a versatile plasma saker and a rack of mass-penetrating shard missiles that can be used against planetary targets or starships.

vehicle.name: Surbbak Enforcer

weapons.name: 1 dorsal dual heavy plasma scorpios turret
Paired anti-ship missile tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 3 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within short range.

weapons.name: 1 ventral antifighter beam turret
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, decrease difficulty by 1.

description: The Surbbak is an {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} customs {@vehicle Corvette|corvette|eoti} used extensively by the Sword Fleet and a few ordrim with extensive void holdings. The gull-winged craft look vaguely similar to {@vehicle Condor Bomber|Condor bombers} but have bulkier hulls and distinctive engine nacelles at the end of each wing. The powerful drives give the Surbbak fast subluminal and superluminal speeds—perfect for running down smugglers and pirates. They also provide the ship with the responsive handling customary of {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} vessels.

While the Surbbak's role is primarily customs inspection and enforcement, the Sword Fleet stations hundreds of the small {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti} at allied systems across the galaxy. Here they work in groups of two or three to protect the ships of the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates'|eoti} trade groups and merchant guilds. As with most {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti}, the Surbbak's limited superluminal range means they can't quickly respond to reports of piracy, so past Quierons have pushed their allies to accept these foreign deployments.

vehicle.name: Sebeko Escort
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 150 plus 1 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttle|eoti}

weapons.name: 1 forward and 1 aft dual heavy plasma scorpios turret
1 forward, 1 port, 1 starboard, and 1 aft tri-beam interceptor emplacements
weapons.fireArc: Forward or Port, or Starboard, or Aft
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, decrease difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: Dual dorsal hullbreaker torpedo tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within medium range.

description: Like most {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti}, the sebeko is designed to escort larger ships, protect against fighter attacks, and drive off raids from other {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti}. For the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti}, of course, those larger ships are often the bulk haulers and freighters of trade convoys. Sebekos play a critical role in the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan's|eoti} convoy escort plans, serving as the outriders who drive off pirate vessels and lightning raids before pulling inward in case of a major attack to defend against enemy bombers.

To accomplish these dual goals, the sebeko is armed with a mix of anti-ship and antifighter weaponry. However, it forgoes the mix of heavy flak cannons and turret guns most {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} carry in favor of a quartet of fearsomely powerful and murderously precise tri-beam turrets. Each is constructed to the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan's|eoti} own painstaking specifications and can shoot down a fighter in a single burst. For larger vessels, the sebeko carries a pair of torpedo tubes and two plasma turrets—a respectable armament for seeing off midsized craft.

In fact, the only area in which the sebeko lacks is its superluminal speed. Since the Sword Fleet only needs them to escort convoys and warships, not engage in raiding, sebekos are only built to keep up with their charges.

vehicle.name: War Zebek
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 400 plus 3 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

abilities.name: Massive
abilities.description: When making an attack targeting this vehicle, the Critical rating of any weapons used counts as 2 higher.

weapons.name: Triple ventral hullbreaker torpedo tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within medium range.

weapons.name: 1 prow, 1 port, and 1 starboard capital-grade beam turrets
weapons.fireArc: Forward and Port, or Forward and Starboard
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 1 dorsal and 1 ventral antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, decrease difficulty by 1.

description: Unlike many navies, the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} commission their {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} to escort convoys rather than raid them. For the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti}, any disruption to galactic trade, even to their enemies, has tended to affect their own bottom line. Therefore, they work to defend commerce, even going so far as to dispatch flotillas to escort neutral vessels or hunt down pirates in disputed or unclaimed territories.

Their war zebeks' biggest difference from other {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} is a slightly shorter interstellar range and the lack of a heavy assault cannon that defines so many {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}. Instead, war zebeks have heavier beam broadsides and triple torpedo tubes. This lessens their offensive power against larger warships but makes them fearsomely effective against most pirate vessels.

One would assume these sleek, ornate vessels would be sought-after commands in the Sword Fleet, but in truth, most {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirate|eoti} officers consider them an onerous duty. As ships often assigned to command convoy escorts, war zebeks see relatively little action, and when a convoy is attacked, they are tethered to their charges. Many an experienced captain has watched bitterly as a junior officer in a {@vehicle Sebeko Escort|sebeko} gets to chase after a raider, while all they can do is volley off torpedoes and reassure worried merchant captains.

However, the war zebek is still armed with capital-grade warship weapons, and in times of all-out conflict, it's more than capable of living up to its name. In fleet engagements, flotillas of war zebeks harry the flanks of an opposing force, peppering them with torpedo fire until the great {@vehicle sorbarrk} battle line crashes home. Then they close in, raking the foes who are pinned in place by the {@vehicle Sorbarrk|sorbarrks'} guns.

vehicle.name: Converted Bulk Transport/Carrier
vehicle.complement: 20 officers and crew, 100 additional crew if outfitted for fighter operations
vehicle.passengers: 100 soldiers (increase to 1,500 soldiers, 10 dust sleds, and 5 {@vehicle Heavy Mech|heavy mechs|eoti} if {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti} and {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} are removed)
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 1,500, plus 36 {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti}, 24 {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, and 10 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti} or {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

abilities.name: Combat Operation Center
abilities.description: While in the carrier's COC, as a maneuver, your character may direct up to four minion-piloted starfighters to merge into a new minion group. Starfighters must be of the same type to be affected.

abilities.name: Vulnerable
abilities.description: This ship is particularly vulnerable to incoming fire. All successful combat checks targeting this ship add {@symbols aa} to the results.

weapons.name: 1 dorsal and 1 ventral antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, decrease difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 1 modular antifighter missile pod
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: Unlike the fleets of many factions, the Sword Fleet does not maintain dedicated soldier or starfighter carriers. Instead, the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} have arrangements with most {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti}-owned trade groups or shipping guilds. These organizations receive subsidies from the Quieron to produce bulk transports with a set of very specific design characteristics. These include heavy hull bracing and structural reinforcement, more powerful engines, and modular cargo bays that can be quickly and easily removed.

In exchange for the financial support, the Quieron reserves the right to levy these ships and their crews in a time of war or state necessity. The cargo bays are removed and replaced with modular hangar bays or self-contained barracks. Command and control equipment is installed in rooms off the bridge specifically designed for the purpose, and in a matter of days the Quieron has troop or fighter carrier vessels ready to accompany the fleet.

While this is an undoubtedly cost-efficient and economically sound way of doing things, relying on these hybrid vessels rather than purpose-designed military ships does have some drawbacks. The foremost issue is that even with the extra design considerations, these ships are not armored or armed for combat operations. Unfortunately, they are manifestly vulnerable to attacks even by much smaller vessels and must be diligently protected by the rest of the fleet as well as by their own fighter and bomber screens.

vehicle.name: Sorbarrk
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 500, plus 12 {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti}, 4 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and 2 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}

abilities.name: Massive
abilities.description: When making an attack targeting this vehicle, the Critical rating of any weapons used counts as 2 higher.

abilities.name: Resilient
abilities.description: When this vehicle suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} while your character is operating it, you may spend a Story Point to roll a second result and choose the result you prefer.

weapons.name: 1 forward, 1 port, and 1 starboard double capital-grade beam turret
weapons.fireArc: Forward, Port, and Starboard, or Forward and Port, or Forward and Starboard
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 1 port and 1 starboard tri-beam interceptor emplacement
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, decrease difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 2 forward, 2 port, and 2 starboard heavy plasma scorpios casements
1 ventral plasma bombard
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} quality is triggered, all targets within medium range of the target suffer one hit; when attacking a target that is not an immobile station or planetary structure, increase difficulty by 2.

description: The sorbarrks are the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} equivalent of {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}, with comparable size and firepower. They form the core of the Sword Fleet, and their smooth lines and shining golden hulls are a common sight watching over the trade lanes and approach vectors of the {@rule Kenara System|Kenara system|eoti}. Though their range is shorter than the {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} of other factions, as the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} see their role as a fleet in being that defends the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} homeworlds, primary colonies, and tributary worlds with their very presence; each is a formidable and dangerous vessel.

Most sorbarrks are centuries old (and some are quite a bit older), with new ships being commissioned only rarely. The {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti} prefer not to scrap their largest and most powerful ships and build newer classes. Instead, they lovingly restore and modernize each ship as needed, so each sorbarrk becomes a living relic of their martial history. Some ships have nearly become legends themselves, because when a sorbarrk is destroyed, the Sword Fleet does not give the name to a new vessel. Thus, ships like the {@i Horizon of Burnished Brass}, {@i Hergash}, and famous {@i Urghan Vanquisher} (lost with all hands over {@rule Mecatol Rex||eoti} during the overthrow of the last Lazax emperor) are now immortalized in the legends and stories of the {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Emirates|eoti}.

All this means that, unsurprisingly, captaincy of a sorbarrk is one of the most sought-after postings in the Sword Fleet. Every junior officer hopes for the day when they see their name engraved on the panels of {@i aumite} stone that line the walls of a sorbarrk's Hall of Captains. Those who do receive that honor are some of the most dedicated and fearless officers under the Quieron's command.

Sorbarrks tend to have a somewhat varied armament, though the aforementioned modernization programs have assured standardization at the broadest level. Though the oldest ships were armed with bulky driver missiles and massive plasma basilisks, these obsolete weapons have been removed in favor of capital-grade beam weapons. However, most still carry a secondary battery of plasma scorpios and bombards, the latter of which can also be used for surface bombardment duties.

description: If the {@vehicle Sorbarrk|sorbarrks} are storied legends in the Sword Fleet, the grand sorbarrks are nigh unto myths. Each of the massive vessels has significantly more tonnage than a standard {@vehicle sorbarrk} and bristles with armament from an earlier age. Less than a dozen have been built in the entire recorded history of the Sword Fleet, and none within the last five centuries. Only one, the {@i Wrath of Kenara}, is currently in service, though the {@i Quieron's Sword} and {@i Legacy of Arretze} are in the midst of a decades-long refurbishment process. The others have long since been lost or destroyed in action.

The {@i Wrath of Kenara} is currently the flagship of the Sword Fleet and the personal warship of the Quieron whenever they choose to take the field in a conflict. Its smoothly curved hull is plated with gold and electrum, with bright crimson inlays and gunports wrought in the forms of desert beasts. The prow boasts the sigil of the {@rule Emirates of Hacan||eoti} with pressure-crafted rubies twenty meters across, flanked by curving platinum bars. The interior of the vessel is just as sumptuously furnished as the hull, with wide corridors carpeted in deep vermillion, sweeping viewports of reinforced crystal, and hand-sculpted furnishings of desert marble.

But beneath all the gilt decoration hides a true warship. Precious metals conceal duranium hull plates, and the ornamental gunports contain broadsides of shipkiller ordnance. The beating heart of the {@i Wrath of Kenara} is a reactor powerful enough to feed a modern city, linked to two {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti}-grade mass-drives. Other secrets may lurk beneath its hull, for the {@i Wrath of Kenara} was laid down before the Twilight Wars and with the aid of Lazax shipwrights. The ship may be capable of feats unknown to even its highly experienced engineering cadre.

Age does come with some drawbacks, however. Though the {@i Wrath of Kenara} was more than a match for any two {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} when it was launched, its guns are simply not the equal of modern weapons. Part of the {@i Quieron's Sword's} refit is to replace its plasma basilisks with capital-grade beam weapons, and if successful, the grand sorbarrk may take the {@i Wrath of Kenara}'s place as fleet flagship. But in the meantime, the {@i Wrath of Kenara} still serves as a valuable nexus around which to build a task force. In addition to its extensive command and control facilities, the ship has immense holds for fuel, munitions supplies, extensive barrack facilities, and cavernous hangar bays. With all this, the {@i Wrath of Kenara} can nearly supply and support a battlefleet by itself.

description: Although the Moll Terminus is a {@vehicle Light Mech|light mech|eoti}, it exemplifies the Coalition ethos in that it punches well above its weight. The mech looks like a four-legged spider with long, spindly limbs and comparatively large chassis. The main hull has room for a pilot and a squad of five Coalition marines, while an enclosed upper turret contains the mech's primary weapon and gunner.

That primary weapon is a boosted anti-armor beam cannon that is extremely powerful for a mech of its size. It's also the Terminus's only weapon. Instead of creating more powerful (and more expensive) mechs that could deal with a variety of foes, the Coalition Marine Corps asked for a mech that could provide ground transport, be deployed from a {@vehicle Combat Dropship|combat dropship|eoti}, and kill any vehicles too heavy for its marine passengers to deal with.

The Terminus serves reasonably well in all those respects. Its four legs allow it to move over extremely rough terrain, to the point where it can climb nearly vertical cliff faces if they are rough enough to provide handholds. It can also do so quickly, allowing it to get into position to launch flanking attacks and ambushes on slower enemies. This all comes at a cost, however. The Terminus is exceptionally fragile for a war machine, and its pilots grimly joke that its best defense is not to get hit in the first place.

Afterwards, reduce the number of shots the scatterblast wingpods can make by 1. If the scatterblast wingpods are out of ammunition, this ability cannot be used.

description: The {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti} does not invest heavily in its starfighter corps, believing the best way to destroy enemy warships is with torpedo or assault cannon strikes from its {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} and {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti}. It sees the role of fighters as entirely defensive, keeping other fighters away from their ships while they make the kills. This is the design ethos behind the Freebooter interceptor.

A stubby, tri-winged starfighter with enough aerodynamic surfaces to allow it to operate in space or atmosphere, the Freebooter is blisteringly fast, lightly armed and armored, and has extremely limited endurance. The interceptor's small frame allows half of a squadron to fit inside the crowded hangars of Coalition {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} and {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}, and the Freebooter's short range doesn't matter when its job is to escort its mothership and drive off enemy fighter and bomber attacks.

The light armaments do mean the Freebooter has a hard time tangling with heavier {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti}, but to help in its defensive duties, the Coalition design workshops gave the fighter a unique weapon loadout. Beyond a single beam cannon, the Freebooter has three scatterblast wingpods, essentially short-ranged cannons firing sprays of explosive, semi-guided flechettes. The wingpods can shred unsuspecting fighters and even destroy or disable incoming missiles, giving the Freebooter a potent defensive tool when protecting the navy's precious warships.

vehicle.name: Raider Assault Boarding Ram

abilities.name: Ramming Speed
abilities.description: To ram and board a target ship, your character makes an {@b opposed {@skill Piloting} check versus the controlling skill of the enemy vessel}, downgrading the difficulty once for every silhouette rating the target is larger than the Raider. If the check succeeds, the Raider hits the target vessel and latches on. At the end of the current round, it cuts into the target ship, and the passengers and crew of the Raider may board the target ship during subsequent rounds. If the check fails with {@symbols aa}, the Raider misses the hull but runs into something important; the target ship suffers a {@rule Collisions|major collision} while the Raider suffers a {@rule Collisions|minor collision} (see page 222 in the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook). If the check fails with {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d}, the Raider bounces off the target's hull armor and is damaged in the process, suffering a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}.

description: Although most of the navies in the galaxy don't emphasize boarding enemy ships as a tactic, the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Mentak Coalition's|eoti} focus on commerce raiding and barely deniable piracy forces them to excel at it. In addition to the boarding tubes on their larger ships, the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} has radically reimagined the concept of a shuttlecraft into what can only be described as a "boarding ram."

The Raider is the latest of these designs, and extremely lethal and efficient given its anachronistic concept. The boarding ram is basically a massive engine sitting behind a heavily armored and reinforced life support module with room for up to ten marines. There is no pilot; every person aboard the ram needs to be prepared to fight upon arrival. Instead, one of the marines operates the relatively simple controls from their reinforced crash-harness.

Forward of the module is an even more heavily armored nose, ringed by mag-clamps and cutting beams. The Raider has a simple job; it flies to an enemy ship as quickly as possible, then rams into the ship's hull, burrowing in as far as it can before latching on with the mag-clamps and activating the cutting beams. Once it bores a hole into the target's interior, the nose splits open, allowing the marines to board the enemy vessel. If the marines need to leave quickly, the Raider can quickly detach and return to the ship that launched it.

Although most of the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition's|eoti} boarding rams are officially reserved for its Marine Corps, a significant number of the assault craft end up in the hands of sanctioned privateers each year. The {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} claims the boarding ram design is easy to replicate, but many a bitter merchant captain has recalled being boarded by rams with the {@i exact} design specifications of the Raider, save that pirates, not Coalition marines, came boiling out of it.

description: As with many of the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition's|eoti} ships and vehicles, the Marauder is a {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti} designed to punch well above its weight. The {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti} treats their {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} almost as if they're ultralight {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}, giving them a range and endurance equal to the heavy {@i Corsair}-class vessels.

The Coalition Navy uses the {@i Marauder}-class as raiders and fleet antistarfighter escorts, and the class is armed with larger versions of the scatterblast pods carried aboard the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition's|eoti} interceptor fighter. However, its lean, angular hull is built around a lighter version of the {@i Corsair}-class' heavy assault cannon. It uses this instead of the more traditional torpedoes, and the weapon allows the {@i Marauder}-class to join the Coalition {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} in devastating opening barrages in naval conflicts.

The {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} aren't large enough to carry {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor fighters|eoti}, but each has enough room for a single {@vehicle Raider Assault Boarding Ram|Raider boarding assault ram} in their cramped hangar deck. This, plus their increased endurance and range, means the Coalition Navy also uses their {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} to patrol the borders of Coalition space instead of dedicated {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti}. Most Coalition captains see their first {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti} as a chance to prove their worth and earn the chance to command one of the larger {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}.

description: The old {@i Ranger}-class light {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} were a staple unit of the {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti} Navy for years, especially as the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} began to expand beyond its small corner of the galaxy and reconnect with other civilizations. However, in the past decades they have been largely decommissioned as the larger and more capable {@i Corsair}-class comes online. A few remain in the navy for patrol work and showing the flag at distant duty stations, but for the most part, the ships have been sold to the Coalition-affiliated privateers.

As part of the process, the navy pays for some basic retrofits to the design. The ships lose most of their already limited ordnance stocks, with the space going to extra fuel tanks and cargo holds. They do keep their older Mk2 assault cannons, but otherwise the ships are left with an armament entirely consisting of beam weapons which, like the newer {@i Corsair}-class, means they don't risk running out of ammo and have more room for fuel and supplies.

Despite its age, the cruiser is an incredibly popular choice among pirates and privateers. The ships retain the impressive speed common to Coalition vessels, but more importantly, are incredibly reliable with multiple redundancies and easily-repaired mechanisms. Finally, the {@i Ranger}-class is tough. There are plenty of stories in the drinking dens of {@rule Moll Primus||eoti} about a little cruiser getting into fights with foes twice its size, only to limp home battered but unbowed.

description: Every captain in the Coalition Navy dreams of commanding a {@vehicle Cruiser|cruiser|eoti}. Mentak culture romanticizes swashbuckling and piratical actions, daring raids, and long patrols far from friendly ports. {@vehicle Cruiser|Cruisers|eoti} are made for these actions, and Mentak {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} like the {@i Corsair}-class are exemplars of their type.

The {@i Corsair}-class follows the same blunt lines of most Coalition designs but is longer and leaner with a blunt, knife-edged prow that houses a massive spinal assault cannon. The lessened armor makes room for heavier engines and more thrusters, meaning that the Corsairs are some of the fastest and nimblest capital ships in the galaxy, especially at superluminal speeds.

The {@i Corsair}-class keeps what shipwrights across the galaxy would call a "standard" {@vehicle Cruiser|cruiser|eoti} weapons loadout but adds just enough hangar space to house six {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor starfighters|eoti}. The extra starships give them enough protection to operate on their own. They also forgo any ordnance beyond rounds for their powerful Mk5 assault cannons (which the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar||eoti} claim are a stolen design that infringes on {@archetype Hylar||eoti}-owned copyrights). An energy-based weapon load means they don't risk running out of ammunition on long voyages and can devote the space to greater stores and stowage capability.

description: Although in no way glamorous ships, the {@i Rover}-class carriers play a vital role in the Coalition Navy. Since the Coalition Navy doesn't rely on waves of {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} to attack their targets, their carrier vessels have evolved to serve a very different role. Instead of carrying wings of heavily armed starfighters and {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, the {@i Rover}-class carriers are designed to be mobile refueling and resupply ships.

The boxy, ungainly ships carry large stocks of ammunition, supplies, and fuel and sit in the depths of space far beyond Coalition territory. There, the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition's|eoti} commerce raiders can rendezvous to take on additional supplies and fuel, effect minor repairs, and off-load any looted cargoes they have obtained. Though the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} denies it, it is widely rumored that {@i Rover}-class carriers have been used to service squadrons of privateers as well.

Although their main role is as a mobile refueling and resupply dump, the {@i Rover}-class also carries multiple squadrons of {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor starfighters|eoti} for defense. It also is one of the few modern Coalition warships to carry anti-ship missiles; its cargo holds have plenty of room for reloads, and a carrier has no interest in closing with the foe. Occasionally, {@i Rover}-class carriers are refitted as fleet escort carriers, ridding themselves of the extra fuel and supply stores to double their complement of fighters.

description: Even with the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Mentak Coalition's|eoti} love affair with light and medium warships, the Table of Captains long ago noted that they would need at least some heavy void combatants to potentially go toe to toe with the fleets of other civilizations. If nothing else, a complete lack of heavy units might incite another galactic power to attempt an invasion, assuming the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} was vulnerable to a main battlefleet.

Since the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Mentak Coalition's|eoti} shipyards were not large or sophisticated enough to build these large warships, the first Coalition {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} were captured during skirmishes and border wars with other civilizations. In one case, a covert team even snuck aboard a {@rule Federation of Sol||eoti} {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} while it was in space dock and flew the warship right through a stunned picket squadron and into Coalition hands. But eventually, the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} expanded their shipbuilding capacity, and the {@i Liberty}-class is the first fruit of those labors.

{@i Liberty}-class dreadnoughts have the lean, angular hulls of most Coalition warships, and though they are far larger than even the new {@i Corsair}-class {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}, they are a bit lighter and faster than the {@vehicle dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} of other navies. They also have an impressive range and endurance, though even Coalition shipwrights couldn't figure out how to boost their superluminal speeds to the equivalent of {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}. In addition to the normal complement of capital-grade beam weapons, the designers also added a pair of oversized spinal assault cannons that run most of the length of the ship. This gives the dreadnoughts a fearsome punch at long ranges that only grows more deadly as they close in.

Unlike most navies, the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition|eoti} seldom groups its dreadnoughts into single flotillas or squadrons. Instead, it spreads the dreadnoughts out in ones and twos with {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti} and {@vehicle Carrier|carrier|eoti} escorts, allowing them to project power all out of proportion with their raw numbers.

description: The flagship of the Coalition Navy got its odd and slightly irreverent name from the citizens of {@rule Moll Primus||eoti}. As the {@rule Mentak Coalition||eoti} expanded its military forces, the designer Tok Miro Sevanta proposed building a vessel even larger than the new {@i {@vehicle Liberty-class Dreadnought|Liberty}}-class ships just starting to be launched from the orbital yards. The ship would be the ultimate command and control vessel, capable of housing the senior leadership of the Coalition Navy and coordinating battles that stretched across star systems.

Intrigued, the Table of Captains and Erwan's Hand agreed to the proposal. Work began on the new flagship, but quickly ran into difficulties as no orbital space dock was large enough to accommodate it. Instead, the ship was built in close orbit around the planet, where its massive size soon rivaled the three natural moons when viewed from the ground.

Cost overruns and design challenges plagued the ship's construction, which meant that a project that should have taken several years ended up stretching over two decades. By the time the new flagship was actually ready for commissioning, an entire younger generation on {@rule Moll Primus||eoti} had grown used to seeing it hanging in the night sky. They called it, jokingly, {@rule Moll Primus|Moll Primus's|eoti} "fourth moon," and the name stuck.

{@i Fourth Moon} still spends much of its time around {@rule Moll Primus||eoti} but does take regular trips to the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Mentak Coalition's|eoti} main colonies and allies to show the flag. It also participates in the biannual Navy war games in the barren Kalanedes system. The completed ship towers over other vessels, with huge sheer sides and a double-stepped, blunt prow. Inside, the {@i Fourth Moon} has massive cargo holds for hauling fleet supplies (and also gathering the looted fruits of the {@rule Mentak Coalition|Coalition's|eoti} commerce raiding). It also has barracks for a sizable percentage of the entire Coalition Marine Corps, hangar bays full of fighters, {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}, and mechs, and elaborate and incredibly powerful scanners and communications arrays.

The one thing it doesn't have is firepower, at least when compared to the {@i {@vehicle Liberty-class Dreadnought|Liberty}}-class dreadnoughts. To be sure, the {@i Fourth Moon} has guns—antifighter defenses, anti-ship missiles, beam weapons, and even a spinal assault cannon—but given its tonnage exceeds any three {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}, the weapons seem somewhat lackluster. However, it has indeed become the ultimate command and control vessel. Not only does it have the facilities to direct a system-wide battle, but its networking is so effective that it can coordinate fire from dozens of ships on the same target.

description: Gavar's Hope survey ships are the eyes and ears of the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} diaspora. Each {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropship|eoti}-sized vessel carries a team of four to six {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} surveyors on long-range survey missions, searching the stars for resources to exploit and lucrative scrap fields to salvage. They're lightly armed and armored but fast and maneuverable. Hopes carry a powerful long-range sensor array that operators claim can pick out a single bolt in a system-wide debris field and scan planets down to a single blade of grass.

The survey teams themselves are trained in planetary surveying, EVA, and some stellar science—metallurgy, geology, xenobiology, etc. The ships carry enough tools, EVA suits, mission-specific equipment, food, water, and air to keep a survey team in the field for six months. These survey teams have numerous small rituals to be performed before, during, and after a mission, and they are among the most superstitious {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} around.

In a pinch, Gavar's Hope ships can be fitted for combat, a perfect expression of the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} {@i look to the left side of your tools} axiom. Their standard weapons loadout and powerful sensors make them perfect for force reconnaissance missions, and they can carry small teams of saboteurs or special forces operators.

description: These are tiny, one-person, multi-role aerospace fighters. XS1s are primarily defensive, but can perform interdiction, light attack, and interceptor missions. Along with the {@i {@vehicle Aggero's Wrath-class Modular Picket Ship|Aggero's Wrath}}-class modular picket ships, with which they often work, XS1s are the most martial ships in the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} fleet. The {@rule Clan of Saar||eoti} builds these in bulk on hidden space docks in the {@rule Jorun Asteroid Field||eoti}, then distributes a majority of the fighters to the captains of the larger starships, with the remainder kept for the forces protecting the asteroid field and any {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} extrasolar holdings.

description: Named for the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} hero who developed the terrifying Armageddon Relay, Aggero's Wrath ships are the only purely military subcapital ships in use by the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} today. Built on a basic {@i {@vehicle Corvette|corvette|eoti}}-class keel, Wraths were designed to fill the various self-defense, system patrol, and force projection roles left vacant by the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} primarily mercantile and industrial fleet.

Wrath corvettes are used primarily to patrol star systems, provide security for {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} facilities and trade routes, and act as force multipliers in civilian fleets. They are operated by professional, military-trained crews and—along with the powerful {@vehicle XS1 Escort Fighter|XS1 fighters}—make up what passes for an actual combat-ready {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} navy. The corvettes can even be carried aboard some of the larger {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} vessels, allowing those bigger ships to bring their own escorts along for the ride.

The standard Aggero's Wrath is a good all-around combat vessel—respectably fast and agile, well armored, and sturdy. The weapons loadout includes a solid mix of autocannons and missile batteries, and the ship is well-equipped to fight at nearly any range.

Along with the standard Wrath configuration, the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} have developed various {@i blocks}, or modification packages, that allow these vessels to operate in dedicated antifighter, anti-capital ship, and electronic attack roles. They provide the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} small professional naval forces a respectable amount of space battle versatility and allow {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} formations to perform well against larger, more heavily developed navies.

items: The {@b Block I Slugger} is made for antifighter and anti-small craft work. It bristles with flak cannons, autocannons, and antifighter missiles—all controlled by advanced fire control systems that can track dozens of targets at once. Sluggers typically fight in pairs, coordinating their attacks and filling local space with deadly clouds of lethal submunitions.

The {@b Block II Spearheads} are fitted with a pair of torpedo tubes, making them dedicated anti-ship platforms. A handful of Spearheads with fighter support can easily handle most {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} and {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}, and in the right circumstances, they can even pose a serious threat to {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}. The downside to all this firepower is that, as single role vessels, Spearheads are woefully inadequate for nearly any other mission.

The {@b Block III Sunburst} variant corvettes are dedicated electronic attack platforms. They carry fewer weapons but are loaded down with powerful electronic warfare systems designed to jam comms signals, scramble sensors, and generally make it impossible for enemy ships, mechs, and troops to see, hear, or communicate with one another.

description: The Scavenger Zeta Suit is a broad, thickly built {@vehicle Light Mech|light mech|eoti} roughly three meters tall and equipped for construction, salvage, mining, and shipbreaking. More a suit of powered armor than a proper piloted mech, the Zeta was developed from an older basic labor mech typically used in heavy construction and asteroid mining. They are heavily armored, shielded, and environmentally sealed, allowing the mechs and their pilots to operate at peak efficiency in a vacuum, deep in the belly of an asteroid, under water, or in hostile planetary environments for hours on end.

Zetas are, at their core, labor mechs, and their equipment loadout reflects that. Each suit is loaded down with tools and systems designed to render ships, asteroids, and scrap into their component parts. Thanks to their sturdy frames, dense armor, and advanced myoelectric mobility systems, these mechs are incredibly strong and tough. They are also surprisingly maneuverable despite their bulk thanks to a clever gyrostabilization system and strategically placed vernier thrusters. To assist them in their work, Zetas are equipped with powerful sensors as well as a diagnostic computer.

Thanks to all their dangerous tools, advanced sensors, and brute strength, Zetas are surprisingly good in a scrap. When forced into a fight, there's typically very little left of the aggressor since the pilots salvage what little isn't melted, rent, or dissolved by the suit's onboard tools. These burly mechs and their pilots—commonly called Zeta jocks—are famous in the {@rule Jorun Asteroid Field||eoti} and throughout the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} diaspora as rowdy, death-defying, two-fisted {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} of action who work hard and party harder. In fact, there are a handful of very popular {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} media franchises centered around the adventures of galaxy-hopping Zeta jocks.

description: These vessels are some of the most important assets in the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} far-flung mercantile and industrial fleet. The size of a {@vehicle Carrier|carrier|eoti} (and similar in function), the Reclamation of Bounty salvage ships—known colloquially simply as Reclamation Ships or Reclaimers—are spacegoing industrial sites. They are foundry, recycling center, smelter, factory, and mill all in one and crewed by some of the most resourceful and competent {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} technicians, laborers, and salvage specialists. They provide the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} with the bulk of their raw materials, and spend months—even years—in space mining asteroid fields, salvaging wrecks, and picking over the remains of long-lost spacefaring civilizations. Reclaimers are the purest expression of the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} resourcefulness and tenacity, and a symbol of their pride and industriousness.

Reclaimers act as a base for numerous {@i {@vehicle Gavar's Hope Survey Ship|Gavar's Hope}}-class survey ships and {@vehicle XS1 Escort Fighter|XS1 escort fighters}, and are home to hundreds of Zeta jocks, engineers, technicians, surveyors, pilots, and workers. They are long, boxy, square-shouldered vessels with midship-mounted docking bays and launch facilities. In the bow, a pair of massive doors provide direct access to the ship's industrial facilities, and Reclaimers are often seen moored to asteroids with their bows resting on the surface as if they were beached.

While in space, Reclaimers take in scrap, salvage, and raw materials and render them down to their base elements. These ores and alloys are forged into ingots and, when the ship has reached capacity, delivered to the nearest {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} installation or void factory. They are surprisingly well armed and heavily armored, and more than one pirate fleet has disappeared during an encounter with a Reclaimer—their crews dead and their ships stripped and melted down.

description: The various ship classes that fall under the umbrella of the  "Lament of the Oppressors" name are a collection of heavily armed, small and medium freighters that make up the bulk of the numerous {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} mercantile fleets. While they vary wildly in shape, design, cargo capacity, weapon loadout, and performance, they all share a few characteristics in common—enough to be considered the same class of ship at least.

The typical Lament armed trader is a ship roughly the size of other factions' {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti}, configured to carry smaller, higher-value cargoes than their massive Strength in Solidarity cousins. Many Lament type vessels also operate regular passenger service between {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} holdings and between {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} facilities and galactic civilization at large. They are often armed for both antifighter and light anti-ship work with the ubiquitous {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} flak and autocannons, but many carry a few parasite rockets to take enemies by surprise. These one-shot weapons are all massive warheads and oversized drives, allowing them to plow into a stunned foe before they recognize the danger.

Lament vessels are also commonly used as antifighter escorts for larger vessels (much like a {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti} in a proper navy) and can be found providing defense and firepower for mercantile and industrial fleets. Lament captains and crews are often courageous, proud, and aggressive, the very model of {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} tenaciousness and can-do spirit. They reflect the values of {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} culture in their design and use, and are as much a symbol of the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} people as the Lay of Lisis chant.

description: {@i Strength in Solidarity}-class ships are {@vehicle Cruiser|cruiser|eoti}-sized bulk freighters that make up the core of the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar's|eoti} mercantile fleet. They are long, heavy, snub-nosed vessels built for hauling power and maximum efficiency rather than speed or style. Their cavernous holds can be configured to carry containers, bulk cargo (ores, pressurized gases, raw materials, liquids, etc.), livestock, and nearly anything else that can be shipped through space along the galaxy's high-value trade routes.

Solidarities are mostly automated, with all inventory, organization, loading, and unloading, as well as most of the navigational and piloting duties, handled by a savant-level AI. These vessels are perhaps best known for their curious internal organization. They are owned, crewed, and maintained by entire clans or groups of clans, and the ships are both their homes and their livelihoods. Each vessel is its own shipping company, and any profits made go to maintaining the ship and providing for the clan or clans who own it.

A {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} trade fleet centered around a Strength in Solidarity-class freighter is a very tough nut to crack. These ships are heavily armed, like most {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} vessels, and carry a lot of their weapons in the cavernous holds, meaning many enemies don't spot the weapons until a hangar door opens to spit out a volley of missiles. These ships always travel with armed escort fleets composed of smaller {@vehicle Lament of the Oppressors Armed Trader|armed traders}, {@vehicle Aggero's Wrath-class Modular Picket Ship|modular picket ships}, and light {@vehicle Carrier|carriers|eoti} packed with {@vehicle XS1 Escort Fighter|XS1 fighters}. Those foolish or desperate enough to tangle with a Solidarity trade fleet, if they're not destroyed outright, often find themselves ruined both by {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} tenacity and by the owners of whatever cargo is aboard.

description: These sprawling, {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti}-sized ships are essentially crowded, multi-decked, spacegoing bazaars. Unlike the roving {@rule Emirates of Hacan|Hacan|eoti} vessels that trade in exotic and proscribed items, Prosperity for All ships travel from world to world buying, selling, producing, wheeling, dealing, and trading in common goods and bulk commodities. Within their cavernous holds are countless markets, bazaars, specialty purveyors, wholesalers, refineries, factories, smelters, and numerous other commercial and industrial concerns. In addition, Prosperities are often home to numerous artists and artisans who make their living selling their work throughout the galaxy.

In and among all the commerce, industry, and art, there are whole sections of these ships dedicated to leisure and entertainment. These areas range from clean and quirky to seedy and sleazy, often on the same deck or within a few minutes' walk. They are typically packed with music venues, restaurants, bars, and various other entertainments commonly found in dense, planetside cities. Nearly anything can be found in the stalls and corridors of a Prosperity ship, and almost any taste can be catered to.

Prosperity for All trade vessels travel established trade routes with regular stops and are reliable enough that whole planets coordinate their various harvests to coincide with a ship's arrival. The appearance of a Prosperity in orbit is often cause for celebration, and many worlds declare planetwide holidays that last for weeks to allow citizens enough time to do what business they need and pursue what pleasures they desire with the visiting {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti}. For many people, especially in the galactic hinterlands, the arrival of a Prosperity is a life-altering event. Indeed, many individuals don't return to their worlds once they see the densely populated, cosmopolitan trade vessels, and Prosperities tend to have incredibly diverse crews and passenger lists.

description: The {@i Labor's Paradise}-class floating factories/mobile space docks are, aside from the truly massive {@i {@vehicle Son of Ragh}}, the largest spacegoing vessels built by the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti}. Less a ship than a slow-moving space station, Labor's Paradises serve as roving, deep space hubs for far-flung {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} survey and trade fleets. They can tend to the needs of dozens of ships at a time and have all the onboard production facilities needed to make themselves self-sufficient.

As their classification suggests, Labor's Paradises are spacegoing shipyards designed to maintain and repair other ships. A typical example consists of a central hull—usually cylindrical or oblong—surrounded by seemingly endless kilometers of gantries and docking facilities. The hull contains the Labor's Paradise's living quarters, public spaces, life support systems, and housing for those laying over while their ship is refit or repaired. The sprawling gantries house production facilities, warehouses, dry docks, hangars, and everything else needed to keep {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} ships up and running.

Although they're not warships by any measure, Labor's Paradise mobile space docks are heavily armed with antifighter and light anti-ship weaponry for defense. The hull and gantries of a typical Labor's Paradise bristle with flak cannons, autocannons, and the odd parasite rocket, enough to make even the most powerful enemy task force think twice about attacking. They can even turn the leavings of their factory yards into deadly projectiles with scrap drivers.

Labor's Paradises are a rare sight in the spacelanes since they typically operate off of heavily trafficked transit routes in deep space, servicing long-range trade, survey, and salvage fleets. They are so rarely seen, in fact, that most other spacefaring cultures think they're a legend. The {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} work hard to keep the quasi-legendary status of their mobile space docks intact, and other civilizations' navies or freelancers who {@i do} stumble upon one rarely live to tell the tale.

description: {@i Son of Ragh} is the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} flagship, one of the largest spacegoing vessels in the galaxy and the culmination of generations of {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} naval research and development. It's a truly {@i massive} self-sufficient generation ship built for deep space travel, exploration, and colonization. Its systems are the most advanced ever created by the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti}, the bleeding edge of propulsion, computer, navigation, life support, biomedical, and weapon technologies. The weapons are designed to protect the ship from all directions, creating a "kill bubble" that gets substantially more lethal the closer an enemy gets. At close ranges, the {@i Son of Ragh} can unleash floods of fire from its octuple autocannon turrets—enough to overwhelm medium ships and starfighters equally well. And there's plenty worth protecting; the ship is packed to the gunwales with living quarters, production and agricultural facilities, and contains hundreds of thousands of stasis pods for transporting {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} in cryosleep. It is a staggering feat of engineering and the pride of the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} people.

The {@i Son of Ragh} has been under construction or undergoing refitting for centuries, and even the Council of Captains claims not to know who first laid down its keel. Some {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} claim the vessel was originally an ancient {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} generation ship—a long-range vessel designed to transport a population at subluminal speeds from one star system to another—discovered drifting between the stars and salvaged. A few even maintain that the {@i Son of Ragh} was one of the {@i first} generation ships, built by the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} as part of their people's diaspora from their fabled homeworld.

Whether or not that is true (though if it is, it would make {@i Son of Ragh} one of the very oldest ships in the galaxy), the ship's numerous redesigns have morphed it into a vessel nearly unrecognizable from its original self—a heavily armed, nearly indestructible command and control ship equipped with all the self-maintaining systems of a generation ship. It is, more than any other {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} vessel, the ultimate expression of {@i looking to the left side of your tools}.

Now that they've built it, though, neither the Admiralty nor the Council of Captains know quite what to do with it. Some want to use it to look for the long-lost {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} homeworld. Others want to pull up stakes and just {@i leave} the galaxy aboard it, using it to move the entire {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} people elsewhere. Still other, more idealistic, {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} want to use it as a spacegoing embassy, a ship that travels the stars showcasing {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} culture and technology and reintroducing the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} to the galaxy at large. Many think the latter plan will go exactly as well as might be imagined, but hope springs eternal.

Thankfully, the CoC has a while to make up its mind, since {@i Son of Ragh} is still on a decade-long shakedown out in the deep space fringes where it won't be bothered. It's the best-kept secret in the galaxy right now; only the {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} know it exists, and only select members of the CoC know where it even is. The {@rule Clan of Saar|Saar|eoti} are {@i very} intent on keeping it that way and will defend at all costs to keep the ship's location and disposition a secret until it's ready for its big unveiling.

description: Sometimes even the nigh-impossible to detect {@vehicle Yssaril Infiltrator|Yssaril Infiltrator|eoti} is too large to approach a target without being detected. This is where smaller air raft orbit-to-ground aircraft bridge the gap between {@vehicle Yssaril Infiltrator|Infiltrator|eoti} vessel and {@vehicle Blackshade Infiltrator Light Mech|Infiltrator mech}. These air rafts can carry a strike team of up to six commandos with minimal equipment but mount only a light assault cannon which should be used only in a last-ditch defense.

Exfiltrator air rafts are designed to stealthily deploy from {@vehicle Yssaril Infiltrator|Yssaril Infiltrators|eoti}. Squat, angular, and stealthy, these air rafts attach externally onto {@vehicle Yssaril Infiltrator|Infiltrators|eoti} to prevent detection from any emissions leakage that opening hangar doors might cause.

All models receive an anti-sensor coating to further enhance the sensor baffling properties of their reflective hull design. The latest models, assigned only to the most critical missions and the most proven agents, boast prototype miniaturized Light/Wave Deflector technology that can render the air raft invisible to any visual detection.

description: These {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} {@vehicle Light Mech|light mechs|eoti} add firepower and mobility to their commando forces. Lanky, hunched over, and with multiple hinge points, the Blackshade Infiltrator is a bipedal exoskeletal suit optimized for speed and agility at the expense of resiliency. Blackshade crews know not to get stuck into prolonged combat, preferring to lay in wait for the ideal moment to achieve their mission before withdrawing at speed. To aid in stealth operations, they forgo explosives in favor of a mag-powered flechette weapon that is almost entirely silent.

Specifically designed to work with the {@vehicle Exfiltrator Air Raft|Exfiltrator air raft} and {@vehicle Yssaril Infiltrator|Infiltrator|eoti} class of ships, the Blackshade Infiltrator can transform into a folded storage mode for transport. Jamming equipment and an integrated data drill make this a platform for intelligence gathering raids.

Blackshade Infiltrators can also be deployed from high orbit using specially constructed drop pods which provide extended life support for the occupant, and more importantly, concealment as space debris or shooting stars. These mechs can either be recovered or destroyed by remote self-destruct if the operators need to exfiltrate on their own.

description: The {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} do not have much of a starfighter culture within their military. This is because starfighters are a tactical weapon suited for large scale battles against {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} and other fighters, exactly the type of battles the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} seek to avoid. However, since the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} do see a role for long-range strategic {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, they decided to try and build a starship that could fit both roles.

Straddling the line between {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighter|eoti} and {@vehicle Star Bomber|star bomber|eoti}, Eliminator heavy fighter-bombers are large strike craft with oversized cockpits, engines, and fuel tanks housed in a central nacelle with four forward-facing booms. Three {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} crew the ship, which includes the luxury of cramped but dedicated cabin space to allow the off-duty crew member to rest as part of their rotation.

While carrying a heavier arsenal and boasting slightly more resilience than the standard {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighter|eoti}, the {@i heavy} in heavy fighter truly comes from its range. Eliminators chiefly exist to launch strategic raids into enemy territory, deploying their heavy fortress-buster missile or hullbreaker torpedo before fleeing. Against enemy fighters, the Eliminator prefers a stand-off engagement with its seeker missiles, rather than a dogfight where it is at a severe disadvantage.

description: A weight class above the customs cutters and reconnaissance {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti} used by many other powers, the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril's|eoti} Disruptor patrol frigate class is a true warship akin to a general-purpose {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti} in miniature. These frigates are capable of independent operation across interstellar distances for presence patrols, security, or support to covert operations.

Often deployed in small flotillas to screen sectors of space, these frigates fan out to operate across one or more systems and only come back together to harass or ambush interloping vessels. Such screens are often placed under the command of an {@vehicle Inhibitor Mission Effects Destroyer|Inhibitor destroyer}. Should this force come, {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} frigates mitigate the undergunned nature of {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} destroyers while receiving protection from the destroyer's defensive systems.

description: As with most {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti} class vessels, the Inhibitor was designed to protect larger vessels with a secondary task of engaging starfighters and other small warships. While other factions pack {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} with flak cannon analogs and beam turrets, the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} take a different approach to protection. Dubbed a {@i mission effects} destroyer, the Inhibitor mounts defensive systems designed to shoot down incoming ordnance and scatter enemy beams.

Mounting these systems is a trade-off. To fit kinetic interceptor turrets and beam-scatter bombpod launchers to the hull necessitated the removal or downgrade of traditional flak and beam weapons. These limited ammunition systems cannot hold off an assault forever, but they can stymie an enemy advance long enough for the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} to achieve their true mission objectives; objectives that rarely are focused on winning any specific battle.

description: Functionally similar to standard fighter and troop {@vehicle Carrier|carriers|eoti} in basic operation, the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} Orchestrator carrier differentiates itself with stealth and straight-line speed. The Guild designates the Orchestrator as an "ambush carrier" designed primarily to extend the range of {@vehicle Eliminator Heavy Fighter-Bomber|Eliminator} squadrons when they launch their strategic deep-strike missions. The Orchestrator is also a capable troopship, though the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} doctrine de-emphasizes ground invasions.

Most carriers are too large to hide using expensive light/wave deflectors. Instead, these craft are designed to hide in plain sight by building into hollowed-out asteroids or by bolting on space debris to appear as derelicts when operating in low-power mode. Low power systems and integrated heat sinks reduce the Orchestrator's sensor signature. Anything but haphazard, these efforts are closely supervised by senior technicians and pilots to ensure stealth does not compromise the launch of strike craft and vice versa.

While seen as primitive by some other powers, the low-tech camouflage of these ambush carriers cannot fail due to some software glitch or power surge. The bulked out exterior structure also provides additional ablative armor. Powerful engines provide straight-line speed, but unfortunately, the increased mass means Orchestrators are truly unwieldy to fly.

Strategically, carriers remain in reserve, hidden behind {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} fleet screening forces until forward deployed for a specific mission. These carriers hide in complex space terrain or coast to their targets unpowered before disgorging attack craft. Once the ruse is exposed, ambush carriers use their powerful engines to make a straight-line getaway even before their strike wing completes their objective. Carrier captains trust the speed and skill of attached crews and thus trust they will not become too decisively engaged to catch up to a slowly accelerating carrier.

description: Cruising missions such as commerce raiding, reconnaissance, and small-scale engagements in far-flung space form the core of the Guild's naval strategy. As such, the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} call upon their cruisers to fight further into enemy territory and with even less support than their counterparts in more traditional navies.

The Instigator is dubbed a light cruiser because of its lesser tonnage and slightly reduced armament. Since {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} nanometallurgy is as advanced as any other power, the Instigator's armor provides strong protection, but this lesser tonnage results in reduced staying power in protracted combat. Of course, such a downside is no matter for cunning Instigator captains who know how to pick their fights wisely.

Despite the {@i light} moniker, Instigators still equip the spinal assault cannon that in part distinguishes {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} as a capital ship and not an oversized {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti}. In keeping this heavy weapon while pushing the superluminal cruising speed, {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} engineers have crafted a vessel capable of outrunning almost any warship capable of destroying it, while being able to prey upon smaller vessels at will.

Service aboard an Instigator is considered a great honor and opportunity for {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} warriors. The famed admiral Sskril, known more broadly as the Shadow and Spear, describes Instigators as his trusty spears, at hand to pierce and dance until even the largest predator falls from blood loss. The Guild deploys single cruisers scattered across the galaxy, so that they are available to respond to crises wherever they occur. Given the extreme limits of superluminal communication, the Guild trusts its Instigator captains to take their own initiative to protect the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Tribes|eoti}. It is this combination of freedom and responsibility that makes service aboard an Instigator so prestigious.

description: Eschewing the type of battle line tactics that favor titanic {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} slugging it out for decisive victory, the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril's|eoti} largest standard class of capital ship is the Terminator battlecruiser. For most of the great powers, {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} are weapons of intimidation and deterrence that are too expensive to lose (or even use). In contrast, the Terminator is meant for extended deployment.

Few great powers incorporate battlecruisers into their fleets. A classic battlecruiser is a warship that punches like a {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} but with less protection. This trade-off allows for a faster vessel at interstellar cruising speed. Boasting speed and endurance more akin to a {@vehicle Cruiser|cruiser|eoti}, captains of these vessels aim to fight anything smaller than them and run from everything else. If forced into a set piece battle, a Terminator squadron attempts to focus their fire on a single point in the enemy line in order to break through and escape to open space. With their greater speed and endurance, the squadron can return days or even weeks later when the enemy is disorganized or unprepared.

Since the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} forgo {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} and have no dedicated bombardment platform, Terminator battlecruisers carry a small stock of superheavy munitions that provide a limited surface bombardment capability. The limited ammunition, however, means the Terminator simply cannot crack proper planetary defenses. Fortunately, the Guild has plenty of ways to bring down such fortifications from within.

description: The {@i Y'sia Y'ssrila} cuts an imposing figure when it can be seen. Two dark metal crescent moons interlocking at a perpendicular angle dominate this flagship's form. Were the ship not so massive, it might look spindly. While this may not be a robust design for a superdreadnought, the installation of numerous light/wave deflection projectors along the arms reveals the design choice. Not only can the {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} flagship become functionally invisible, this negative space provides ample room to huddle in allied ships not able to maintain their own cloaking field.

Much like their {@vehicle Terminator Battlecruiser|Terminator battlecruisers}, the {@i Y'sia Y'ssrila} constantly moves throughout the galaxy to extend the influence of the Guild and to serve as a second headquarters for the Cqaark. Hundreds of the best commandos, solo operatives, and analysts operate from the flagship. Onboard they enjoy the finest in holotraining suites, datalinks, and even a reasonable reproduction of a small section of {@rule Retillion and Shalloq|Retillion's|eoti} Fianni swamp. The latter serves as a place of contemplation and inspiration, especially for high-ranking {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} when considering whether to send operatives on the riskiest missions.

Although equipped with {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti}-grade firepower, the {@i Y'sia Y'ssrila}'s traditional weapons are intended for self-defense. The {@rule Yssaril Tribes|Yssaril|eoti} flagship's true weapons are the strike teams of Guild spies, hangars of {@vehicle Yssaril Infiltrator|Infiltrators|eoti}, and wings of strategic {@vehicle Eliminator Heavy Fighter-Bomber|fighter-bombers}. The {@i Y'sia Y'ssrila} allows the Guild to maintain a powerful presence in the farthest reaches of the galaxy.

The Guild strictly controls access to the {@i Y'sia Y'ssrila}. Few high-ranking agents ever receive the honor of even seeing the ship, let alone boarding it. Non-Yssaril are unheard of aboard. Rumors abound, however, that the ship is crewed by legendary agents long presumed dead or captured.

Despite the secrecy, the Guild will from time to time deliberately reveal the {@i Y'sia Y'ssrila} to show foreign intelligence services it does indeed exist. In this way, it may not be as showy a deterrent as a fleet of {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}, but strategists across the galaxy must contend with the fact that the Guild could be plotting anything, and this flagship could be in any system.

vehicle.name: Dool Felnni (Shield Paling) Light Mech
vehicle.complement: 1 pilot and 1 gunner, or 1 remote link to an {@vehicle Urri Chathe (Oversight) Heavy Mech|Oversight heavy mech}

description: As part of the protocol to support {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} troops, the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} designed a suite of war mechs to provide defensive shielding for soldier-scientists but also engage in long-range bombard-and-move cover fire.

A mass of articulated tentacles around a central pod, the Shield Paling can slide over any terrain. When gathered together like a central trunk, the tentacles can raise or lower the pod as needed, and any damaged ones are replaceable in the field. The tentacle mass can also curl up around the pod into a ball, allowing the mech to roll with surprising speed. However, their most important feature is the set of magen screen projectors that run the length of each tentacle. The Shield Paling can use these to defend allied soldier-scientists and other mechs in close formation.

vehicle.name: Urri Chathe (Oversight) Heavy Mech

abilities.name: Ablative fractal tentacle barrier
abilities.description: When this vehicle suffers a hit, after damage is calculated but before armor is applied, your character may cause the Oversight to suffer 1 system strain to reduce the damage by 2. This ability can only be used once per hit.

description: This heavy gun and research platform is a mass of articulated fractal tentacles with a central hub that slowly slithers over any terrain. Each fractal tentacle can be sacrificed in protection of the whole, making the Oversight essentially a deployable bunker composed of reactive armor. Replacement fractal tentacles are easy to install. Despite this, the Oversight is not intended for frontline combat. Instead, these heavy mechs mainly serve as command and control hubs for up to six {@vehicle Dool Felnni (Shield Paling) Light Mech|Shield Paling light mechs} and as transports for infantry teams. Even though the fractal tentacles are effective in combat, Oversight pilots prefer not to get any closer to the enemy than necessary for firing their plasma howitzers.

vehicle.name: Aashaa Logli (Axiom) Flak Fighter
vehicle.complement: 1 pilot and 1 {@sidebar Augmented Identify & Ideation (AII) Control Suites|AII control suite}

weapons.name: AII seeker missiles
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: Historically, the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} have not had a strong fighter development program, mostly due to the demands of {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} physiology. Currently, they have implemented a new fighter engagement doctrine nicknamed "notional flak." The Axiom flak fighter utilizes a wide variety of defensive systems, such as miniaturized magen defense grids, high-energy emitter jammers, holographic decoys, ablative shielding, and adaptive false sensor data info-spikes. The goal of these systems is to overwhelm an enemy fighter with visual, sensor, and conceptual flak. In fact, the only thing the systems don't use is actual physical shrapnel.

In order to recruit more {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} pilots, the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} military has loosened standardization restrictions; all pilots have permission to modify their assigned fighter as they see fit for efficiency, safety, or experimentation. Thus, while its core design resembles a sleek-finned aquatic creature, the longer a fighter has been in service, the more external modules, components, projectors, and sensor spines it accumulates. This lax standardization draws in plenty of young and arrogant recruits, as many romanticize the life of a hotshot tech on the edge of danger.

vehicle.name: Othani Huul (Maxim) Star Bomber

weapons.name: AII seeker torpedoes
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within short range.

description: Per weight, the Maxim should be a heavy bomber, but that figure reflects the {@archetype Hylar|Hylar's|eoti} environmental/life-support equipment and impact padding for the crew, not engines or armaments. Over the years, the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} have implemented various technologies to protect fighter and bomber pilots with mixed success. These include an inertia damper force field, a cockpit filled with aerated impact superfluid and cybernetic implants to "harden" the {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} pilots themselves. Each technology either inconveniently increases the mass of the bomber, sacrifices armor or armaments to the point of uselessness, or trades the health and well-being of the pilot too much for the public to stomach.

The Maxim has the telltale {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} organic, bulbous look, with a small, cramped saltwater tank central module and a pair of stubby wings that resemble fish fins. It is armed with a quartet of advanced seeker torpedoes for hunting enemy starships. However, it has almost no other weapons and typically skulks around the edges of a battle before firing its torpedoes and fleeing as soon as possible.

vehicle.name: Raftha Pulch (Apprentice) Destroyer
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 100, plus 1 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttle|eoti}

weapons.name: 8 point-defense autocannons
weapons.details: These weapons are scattered across the hull of the destroyer, so only two may be fired at any one target.

description: The Apprentice usually serves as an escort ship attached to a {@vehicle Cruiser|cruiser|eoti}, {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti}, or {@vehicle Carrier|carrier|eoti}. Unlike the heavier weight classes, {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} destroyers do not have a science or infiltration lab, and thus have no incentive to travel alone on deep space missions. They also don't sport the experimental and/or over-engineered add-ons that the heavier ships do. This makes them far more reliable combat vessels. For that reason, the military leans on their rapidly aging destroyer wings for basic tasks more than they should. Many a {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} graduate has had a career dead-end on one of these workhorses that provide little to no place to experiment or perfect a thesis.

description: The {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} Fleet currently leans heavily on the upper range of starships, including {@vehicle Carrier|carriers|eoti}. Like most {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} capital ships, {@i Sequester}-class carriers also serve as mobile research labs, but they are much more than that. They typically have a high-energy laboratory, a sensor suite, biological and digital storage, quarantine facilities, stasis pods, and {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} training facilities. Carriers often maintain several DRI groups for either large extraction operations or to seed single teams on multiple worlds within a jump or two.

While Sequesters have research capabilities, they often do not sport experimental weapons, as their missions don't involve direct engagements. Their crews tend to have an equal number of Wun-Escha graduates (with that university's emphasis on theory) and Nuun-Dascha graduates (with their emphasis on practice) working in their labs. Thanks to their fully stocked research labs, these carriers engage in a lot of "rogue science" to solve problems. Carrier crews often receive commendations and awards when they return home for "science above and beyond the call of duty"—or they never come home at all.
