description: The {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} taxonomy for the classification of capital ships requires that they have a full scientific laboratory and perform the two-pronged mission of deep space military spacecraft. That is, the protection of {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} space and the acquisition of new science and technologies. By this rubric, the Questor, though technically a cruiser, qualifies as a capital ship. This grants them free rein to patrol alone. {@i Questor}-class cruisers frequently sport experimental technology in the fields of weaponry, propulsion, power generation, sensors, and even crew methodologies. They also have an attached DRI group, as well as a quarantine suite to isolate and analyze materials and individuals exposed to {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti}-unfriendly environments.

The {@i Questor}-class serves as an example of {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} cruiser capability, and its design has the usual fins, spines, and bulbous center. However, the multitude of {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} cruiser classes (Questor, Seeker, Aspirant, etc.) reflects ever-changing standards and endless technical nudges. The silhouette and behavior of any individual {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} cruiser differs so much from others that many inhabitants of the galaxy immediately assume any strange ship is {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti}.

description: {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} dreadnoughts serve as giant mobile universities that happen to have orbital bombardment capabilities. They have full research laboratory support (complete with exotic particle accelerators and quarantine units), as well as diplomatic suites for vector groups specializing in more "targeted" investigation (what many consider a "spy wing"). Dreadnoughts always sport one or more experimental modifications to field-test new technologies and applied sciences. This makes the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar's|eoti} the most unpredictable of all the Great Civilizations' dreadnoughts—but also the most unreliable.

Inquisitors have expansive subatomic boson computing networks not only to process data but also to run both scientific and tactical simulations. The onboard DRI analysis center is devoted to eliminating errors and variables to get near 100% confidence intervals. These ships tend to be data hungry as a result.

The {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} use dreadnoughts mostly as a show of strength in "vulnerable" systems, sometimes even sending them out of sector for diplomatic missions. The ship itself often acts as a remote institution of higher learning, serving as a hub where other capital ships can report back, submit papers, and receive resources and approval for experiments. Some {@archetype Hylar|Hylar|eoti} prefer to pursue their education aboard these vessels, especially if their research tends to focus more on the "applied" portion of physics or thermodynamics.

description: JNS {@i Hylarim} exemplifies the latest {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} design aesthetic. Ancient ships had a practical design, but the past centuries have seen a push toward the current organic look. {@i Hylarim} has sleek, rounded angles; attenuated spines; and a central bulbous hull that recall the aquatic life on both planets. The flagship of the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} Fleet does sport heavy weaponry but not to the extent of planetary bombardment capability. It allocates significant space and mass for its laboratory facilities, diplomatic wings, and saltwater environment quarters.

As the flagship of the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti}, {@i Hylarim} has to be in the forefront of technological and scientific innovation. While {@i Hylarim} has deployed on key missions, it more often performs diplomatic courtesy calls and academic recruiting drives. On each trip out, it sports a different experimental tech as a matter of pride but also for public relations. {@i Hylarim}'s current testing suite consists of quantum collapse disruptor cannons, which have proved promising if unreliable—for now.

When not on a diplomatic or combat mission, {@i Hylarim} acts like an {@i {@vehicle Dilioor Baliith (Inquisitor) Dreadnought|Inquisitor}}-class dreadnought, serving as a mobile university and research hub. Many non-Hylar who manage admission into the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} educational system start their first year aboard {@i Hylarim}, due to its proximity but also for prestige.

vehicle.name: Ember Colossus
vehicle.passengers: 4 on external mounts; passengers gain vehicle's defense
description: The Ember Colossus is essentially a scaled-up version of the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai's|eoti} {@archetypeAbility Ember Suit|Ember suit|eoti}, augmented with a variety of heavy weapon systems. Standing nearly ten meters tall, each Colossus boasts a magma rocket battery for softening heavily armored targets and a pair of scinta cannons that fire white-hot shrapnel bombs for antipersonnel work.

Each Colossus is operated by a pair of well-trained {@i novash} (pilots), and has four external mounts for interfacing with standard {@archetypeAbility Ember Suit|Ember suits|eoti}, allowing the Colossus to carry additional soldiers into battle. The mounts give those soldiers some protection from enemy small arms while allowing them to return fire with their own weapons, granting the Colossus improved antipersonnel capabilities in the process.

description: After multiple engagements indicated a need in the {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} navy for a small-scale warhead delivery system, the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} chose Fire Warden Aloash to devise a solution. The result was the Cendos heavy bomber, a {@vehicle Sparesh Superiority Fighter|Sparesh} fuselage integrated with a new module consisting of a defensive autocannon turret, a pair of interchangeable weapon pods for ordnance, and a heavy engine assembly.

The Cendos' ordnance is formidable. It can mount a pod that holds the same rockets as the {@vehicle Ember Colossus}, a powerful torpedo, or—for particularly devastating close-in strikes—a pod containing a nova bomb designed specifically for the Cendos.

vehicle.name: Sparesh Superiority Fighter

weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: The {@rule Embers of Muaat||eoti} military doctrine places a greater emphasis on a wide range of midsized capital ships than on robust starfighter forces. Nevertheless, they employ a sizeable force of a heavily armored, multirole craft called Sparesh. Spherical except for the protruding engine assembly, the Sparesh is built to be a jack-of-all-trades but a master of none. The Sparesh is less nimble but more resilient than most multirole fighters employed by the fleets of other civilizations. It makes up for subpar maneuvering capabilities with weapon placements around its spherical hull that give the Sparesh relatively few blind spots.

vehicle.name: Firos-class Corvette

weapons.name: Paired anti-ship missile tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 3 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

description: The {@i Firos}-class corvette is the primary small support and patrol craft of the Muaat Defense Fleet. Their main role is watching for enemy incursions or raids by pirate bands. Unexpected visitors in {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} space are quickly met by a corvette on patrol. Freighter convoys moving between worlds in {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} space, or to their friendlier interstellar neighbors, are also usually escorted by at least one Firos.

{@i Firos}-class corvettes see more limited use in solars operating outside of {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} space. When a Fire Warden does employ corvettes in their solars, they are usually as support craft for larger capital ships. Most often, this is to provide additional combat support against small enemy craft. Occasionally, these corvettes are also used as advanced scouts in uncharted territory.

description: The {@i Ammash}-class destroyer is the primary workhorse of the {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} fleet. These destroyers operate in squadrons to initiate quick and overwhelming strikes on small targets, or in larger groups to launch coordinated wave attacks on more implacable foes. They are highly standardized so that they can easily be built by {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} war suns. With their powerful incendos cannons, they can inflict serious damage, rupturing hulls and igniting infernos that can last for several minutes. While the enemy crew focus on dousing the flames before they completely consume their own vessel, the {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} destroyers retreat to rejoin their battle lines.

description: Carriers fill an awkward role in the {@rule Embers of Muaat|Muaat|eoti} navy. Detractors see little point in maintaining a large number of ships specifically for transporting military forces to other combat theaters. Development of such a vessel remained a point of contention between militarists and anti-militarists until Fire Warden Shesh Olt requisitioned several heavy freighters for their solar during the Plateau's Rift campaign. Olt's engineers converted the cargo modules into high-capacity fighter and infantry bays. These vessels proved invaluable in the completion of the solar's mission, and swayed enough {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} to approve development of a dedicated carrier craft.

The {@i Falo}-class carrier is a heavily armored, modular design based on similar civilian freight haulers. It consists of a long central axis with eight docking mounts for carrier modules, two each of dorsal, ventral, starboard, and aft. These detachable modules can serve as infantry barracks, fighter bays, or even mech hangars. This modular design is a compromise to anti-militarist {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti}, as the {@i Falo}-class carrier can, in theory, serve civilian purposes with the correct cargo modules. In practice, however, these carriers have consistently remained in military roles.

description: As the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} spread to nearby stars and pursued their place among the Great Civilizations, they realized they needed vessels to serve many roles and functions. The first attempt at a mainline battlecruiser was {@i {@vehicle Inferno|Inferno}}, but though it proved a success as a flagship, it was too expensive to serve as the backbone of the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai's|eoti} fledgling navy. The designers considered the elements that they thought vital for a cruiser: mobility, endurance, and more armaments than a {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti}. Then they designed such a vessel within the limitations of what {@i {@vehicle Inferno|Inferno}}'s star forge could construct.

After many attempts, the first {@i Shener}-class cruiser launched from {@i {@vehicle Inferno|Inferno}}'s star forge. The cruiser's ovoid shape, like rounded beads of cooled obsidian, gave it a sort of family resemblance to {@i {@vehicle Inferno|Inferno}}. The new design quickly proved both reliable and formidable, and as the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} built more cruisers, their fleet blossomed from a haphazard system defense force to one capable of projecting power beyond their borders.

Since squadrons of {@i {@vehicle Ammash-class Destroyer|Ammash}}-class destroyers fill some of their conventional roles, {@i Shener}-class cruisers can sacrifice speed in exchange for additional armor and armament. In addition to bearing incendos and plasma weapons, this cruiser is built around a central mass driver that can propel a large volranium shell at near luminal speeds—an exceptionally devastating shipkiller.

description: The {@i Erusha}-class dreadnought is a rare and intimidating sight. Nine forward torpedo tubes can deliver an overwhelming bombardment of volranium-bore nova torpedoes to any ship, station, or planetary installation in range. After unleashing such a volley, the dreadnought does require some time to reload and ready the next salvo, but ideally the first one obliterates the target. In addition, four heavy incendos cannons reduce anything that comes within firing range to burning wreckage.
At least, that is the theory.

This dreadnought was designed during a conflict with the {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti}, who threatened to cut a path through {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} space toward {@rule Mecatol Rex||eoti}. The {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} concluded they needed a dedicated shipkiller to respond to the threat posed by other navies' premiere warships. However, the unfortunate irony of the {@i Erusha}-class' creation was that, by the time the first one was built and fully operational, the inciting conflict had already ended when the {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti} chose to bypass {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} territory. A few {@i Erusha}-class dreadnoughts have entered active service since, though, anticipating the moment when they can prove their mettle in open war.

description: {@i Inferno} is the flagship of the Muaat Defense Fleet, a one of a kind battlecruiser built to be more practical for aggressive naval actions than a {@vehicle War Sun|war sun} without sacrificing much in terms of sheer firepower. {@i Inferno} began life as a prototype war sun. However, when the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} recognized the need for a different sort of vessel, much of its hull was stripped away, leaving only the skeletal superstructure and star forge. The {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} built a new volranium-plated shell around this superstructure, resulting in {@i Inferno}'s oblong shape. Then they fitted the ship with a staggeringly powerful drive system, giving {@i Inferno} greater speed than a war sun, and a dozen weapon batteries to grant it terrifying firepower befitting its name.

The {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} originally intended to build many such ships to serve as their navy's main battlecruisers, but reproducing {@i Inferno} proved far too costly for that purpose. Instead, they designed the smaller {@i {@vehicle Shener-class Cruiser|Shener}}-class cruiser, which strongly resembles {@i Inferno}, and modified {@i Inferno}'s star forge to build it. They then converted a portion of {@i Inferno}'s command center into a war room from which the entire {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} fleet could be directed when the need arose. Today, {@i Inferno} serves as Fire Warden Magmus's flagship, and thus the flagship of the Muaat Defense Fleet. It seldom strays far from {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} space so that it can respond to any threats to {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} territory—and, most importantly, {@rule Muaat||eoti} itself.

description: The original war sun the {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} forced the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} to build was a colossal assault platform built for planetary invasion. With its ovoid shape and spires of weapon batteries and sensor arrays, it was nearly a world on its own. It had numerous hangars and docking clamps for support craft and supply ships. A war sun could carry an army large enough to take a fortified planet, and it mounted enough orbit-to-surface weapons to reduce such a planet to ash if its defenders proved too tenacious.

The {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} did not have immediate use for such an assault platform. As they recovered from {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} occupation, they began to modify the original design. The {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} installed magmus reactors and volranium hull plating. They modified the war sun's internal environment for {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} comfort. Most importantly, they created the star forge, a kilometers-long manufactory that allows the war sun to build mechs, starfighters, and even small capital ships. By the time the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} dispatched an envoy to {@rule Mecatol Rex||eoti} and made their official debut on the galactic stage, their war suns could not just support a fleet, they could build one.

No one outside the {@rule Embers of Muaat||eoti} is sure how many war suns the {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} possess, but most intelligence agencies place the number at two or three. Modern {@archetype Gashlai|Gashlai|eoti} war suns have improved over the original design, increasing speed and firepower at a minor cost to armor. A ring of collecting arrays encircle a war sun's main hull and dramatically increase the efficiency of its magmus reactor and star forge.

vehicle.name: MR Avalanche Land Train
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 400 (without passengers)
description: The Avalanche is a massive twelve-wheeled ground crawler in widespread use throughout the Federal Army. It is very lightly armed (with just a single pintle-mounted anti-infantry weapon), but its boxy, beetle-like body is heavily armored and extremely durable. The Avalanche is also easy and cheap to maintain and repair. Crew joke that the vehicle could drive on transaxles fashioned from tree trunks. It's certainly true that Avalanche spare parts can be sourced from a wide range of civilian and military vehicles.

The land train's interior troop compartments are roomy enough to carry an entire company, forty tons of cargo and supplies, or a mix of the two. This makes them indispensable for units of the Home Defense Corps and Logistics and Support. (The Air Legions, meanwhile, rely almost entirely on {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti} and lifter {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}). The Avalanche is also the most exported military vehicle the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} produces, so many grunts across the galaxy have had a chance to curse its legendarily uncomfortable passenger seats.

vehicle.name: ZS Thunderbolt Mk2

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

abilities.name: Combat Drop
abilities.description: You may equip this vehicle with a single-use impact dampener and attitude thruster pack (price 1,000 aurei, rarity 7). If so equipped, when your character is piloting this vehicle they may drop it from a distance of extreme range from the ground by making an {@difficulty average|piloting}. If they succeed, the vehicle lands safely at the end of the current round. If they fail, the vehicle suffers 5 system strain and a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}. Your character may spend {@symbols aaa} or {@symbols t} from the check to cause all characters within short range of the impact point to become {@rule Staggered|staggered} for one round (whether or not the check succeeds). After a drop, the pack is expended and may no longer be used.

description: The hulking bipedal form of the ZS Thunderbolt is as sleek and handsome as a grav-mallet, and every bit as lethal to someone who gets in its way. {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} soldiers affectionately refer to these metal monsters as "big guys" or just "bolts."

Thunderbolts give the Air Legions their offensive punch. In addition to their complement of arm-mounted beam cannons, their shoulders carry a multibarrel mass driver battery that fires volleys of heavy rocket-assisted projectiles. However, its weapons and even its duranium-reinforced skeletal bracing system aren't what makes the Thunderbolt such a useful element of the Air Legion arsenal. Though the brutish mech may not look it, the ZS Thunderbolt is fully airmobile.

The Thunderbolt's thick legs are filled with heavy shock absorbers. When outfitted with disposable impact dampeners and attitude thruster packs, they can be flown into battle by a variant of the {@vehicle D7 Tempest Combat Dropship Mk7|Tempest gunship} and dropped from as high as a kilometer up (depending on local gravity). Mech pilots like to say that the ground-shattering impact when it lands is what gives the Thunderbolt its name.

vehicle.name: F5 Hurricane Mk5

weapons.name: Lightning mass driver warhead system
weapons.details: After firing, this weapon runs out of ammo and must be reloaded at a base or carrier.

description: The fifth iteration of the venerable {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} Hurricane doesn't seem like a particularly innovative or advanced starfighter. That's because decades ago, {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} designers agreed that there was no reason to discard a proven success.

The Hurricane adheres to {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol's|eoti} blunt design aesthetics, with a bulky fuselage flanked by two engine/weapon pods mounted on stubby wings. This unassuming appearance belies the fact that it's a generalist starfighter beyond compare. It may not specialize in any one area of operations, but in the hands of a skilled pilot it can do just about anything well.

The ship's simplicity means that, unlike most {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti}, it can be operated by a single pilot. Instead of carrying missiles, it sports a single-shot "lightning" warhead launcher that gives the Hurricane punch against larger vessels. Otherwise, the only weapons are a pair of linked assault cannons in the wing pods. Without the need for target tracking equipment (and the weapons officer to operate it), the Hurricane has enough room to mount a superluminal drive that gives it impressive range for a starfighter.

As a result, the Hurricane can do everything from dogfights to ground attack missions to escorting long-range {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} to their targets and back. Due to its general utility, it has almost completely supplanted the navy's need for an {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor|eoti}—though the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} does keep some squadrons of lighter F2 Squalls for defensive operations and reserve units. If the strike carriers are the primary warships of the Federal Fleet, the Hurricane is what gives them their teeth.

Installing the attack pods takes roughly 30 minutes of work.

weapons.name: Stonecracker rockets
weapons.details: Replaces the hullbreaker torpedoes (see Typhoon Attack Pods). When attacking a target that is not an immobile station or planetary structure, increase difficulty by 2.

description: The best way to avoid antifighter defenses is to never get close enough to them to be shot by them. The massive B84 Typhoon exemplifies this strategy perfectly. Its four heavy anti-ship torpedoes allow it to launch strikes from the other side of a star system if need be. This, combined with its reasonable superluminal flight range, means that the Federal Fleet can use it to hit targets at interstellar ranges without ever exposing their precious strike carriers to counterattack.

Of course, this capability does come with some drawbacks. Typhoons are huge, even for {@vehicle Star Bomber|star bombers|eoti}, and correspondingly expensive. They also have mediocre defenses and no ground attack capability at all (the fleet uses {@vehicle F5 Hurricane Mk5|Hurricanes} for that). But a squadron of Typhoons with Hurricane support can approach a target in space from multiple directions, volleying ever-more accurate torpedo salvos at it as they close the distance before breaking away and fading into the darkness.

description: Although dropships like the D7 Tempest are used throughout the Federal Army, they are a vital part of the Air Legion's combat doctrine. Tempests allow the Air Legions to launch overwhelming orbital assaults. Then once the troops are on the ground, they continue to provide vital mobility and punishing air support with their assault cannons and mass drivers.

The Tempest is a fat-bellied and tall-sided flyer with a set of stubby stabilizer wings and an inelegant tail. Its form is only aerodynamic in the loosest sense of the word; without its powerful contragrav thrusters, there's no way the Tempest could remain airborne. But the trade-off for the Tempest being as flightworthy as a rock is that it's also as tough as one. Heavy armor lets the dropship reenter atmosphere at near terminal velocity and then ride out incoming fire long enough to get its cargo on the ground.

The other feature that makes the Tempest so valuable is the ability to remove the troop bay entirely. In this configuration, it can carry one {@vehicle ZS Thunderbolt Mk2|Thunderbolt mech} instead of soldiers or gear. With the right equipment, that Thunderbolt can even be dropped from high altitude, keeping the Tempest out of range of ground fire.

description: The Federal Fleet can ill-afford to have its carrier squadrons dispatched on customs duty and border patrols for extended periods of time. Instead, {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} relies on its corvettes to defend its expanding territory and enforce Federal law throughout the worlds it controls. The {@i Stormrunner}-class corvette is a typical design, with a sharply pointed bow widening back to oversized engines. It's fast enough to run down nearly any civilian vessel in the galaxy, although it risks burning out its drives at top speed.

Since the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} uses these vessels for law and customs enforcement, the Stormrunner carries an oversized detachment of soldiers and a boarding tube rather than the extensive magazines and consumables of other factions' {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti}. The smaller ammunition stowage means this corvette relies primarily on beam weapons. In fact, it only has a single missile tube (lest it fire through its stock of missiles too quickly).

Generally, Stormrunners don't stray from the planetary system they're based in. However, in a few cases, they have accompanied detached fleet elements tasked with extended operations in a single location to provide them with more flexible patrols.

description: Although destroyers are traditionally used as antifighter ships, most navies also equip them with heavy torpedoes that allow them to punch above their weight when engaging enemy capital ships. In the Federal Fleet, that need is reduced since every {@vehicle Carrier|carrier|eoti} has squadrons of {@vehicle B84 Typhoon Torpedo Bomber|Typhoon torpedo bombers} ready to launch strikes. What the fleet does need is antifighter defenses to ensure their carriers aren't taken out by a fighter counterattack. That's where ships like the Nimbus come in.

The Nimbus relies on its heavy flak cannons to throw up a lethal antifighter barrage, then picks off stragglers with its array of antifighter beam weapons. It does still carry a pair of torpedo tubes (after all, the fleet has plenty of those same torpedoes in storage to supply its {@vehicle B84 Typhoon Torpedo Bomber|Typhoon} squadrons), but has a very limited set of reloads. Instead, the extra space has been used to augment the antifighter beam turrets with improved tracking systems and add additional weapons for full coverage.
Serving on a Nimbus isn't glamorous or exciting. However, these ships serve a vital role in the Federal Fleet, and plenty of senior officers spent their first command on a destroyer's bridge.

description: Strike carriers are the heart of the Federal Fleet, heavy warships that can carry scores of starfighters and operate independently for months. They can also take a punch and keep on fighting. The Cyclone is the latest class of strike carrier launched by {@rule Jord|Jord's|eoti} orbital yards. So far, these new ships make up slightly less than half of {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol's|eoti} total carrier strength. However, with the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation's|eoti} ambitious building program, they could replace all existing strike carriers by the end of the decade. Many observers worry that the Federal Fleet then will be fully prepared for a major war with another galactic power.

While previous classes of strike carrier attempted to balance offensive, defensive, and ground operations, the Cyclone is an offensive and invasion support ship through and through. Its larger hull enables an expanded fighter wing made up entirely of heavy {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti} and {@vehicle Star Bomber|torpedo bombers|eoti}. It's also got space for a robust {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropship|eoti} squadron and several thousand troops. Older strike carriers were armed with mass drivers for dual anti-ship operations and surface bombardment, but the Cyclone relies on its squadrons for ground attack. In place of the mass drivers, it carries several heavy beam weapons that give it a reasonable chance of seeing off anything {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti}-sized or smaller—assuming the target makes it through the Cyclone's swarms of attack craft.

All in all, the Cyclone is a terrifying modern warship. With {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} producing more and more of these behemoths, it's only a matter of time before the galaxy finds out if Cyclones can defeat the power of a {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} battle line.

description: Many {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} ships use mass driver weapons, heavy grav-accelerators that can fling a barrage of projectiles at a substantial fraction of the speed of light. The Hailblast takes full advantage of this technology, mounting an especially large multibarreled capital-grade assault cannon that runs through the ship's spine. Even though it takes a long time to reload, it can deliver a punishing barrage.

This heavy cannon plus the attendant capacitors take up a large portion of the interior space and also stress the ship's internal systems. As a result, the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} tends to keep their {@i Hailblast}-class cruisers behind the main battle line or alongside strike carriers. From there, they can lob punishing volleys with impunity while {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol's|eoti} {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} close in for the kill. Unfortunately, these trade-offs make Hailblasts less useful as escorts or commerce raiders. The {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation|eoti} has needed to maintain its large contingent of older {@i Precipice}-class cruisers to fill the roles that a Hailblast cannot.

description: In the terms of naval combat, the Thunderhead is a pugnacious brawler. The basic sloped arrowhead design of {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol's|eoti} principal ship of the line has changed little over the past three decades, and its brutal effectiveness at ship-to-ship combat suggests it will remain in service for decades to come.

Like some of the other great powers' navies, the Federal Fleet prefers not to dedicate any of its capital ships' armament to ground bombardment, instead trusting that its main weapons can handle the job if needed. In the Thunderhead's case, the shipwrights eagerly filled the saved space with a punishing broadside of mass drivers. Their range and firing arcs are limited, but the Thunderhead also boasts powerful engines that can accelerate the ungainly ship to an impressive velocity. The Federal Fleet expects its dreadnoughts to head straight into the enemy formation, weathering incoming fire until they are among their foes. Once there, Thunderheads can lay about in all directions with their heavy weapons. Their effectiveness has led many officers to affectionately nickname these ships "linebreakers" or "gun rams."

vehicle.name: Genesis
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 750, plus 96 {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti}, 48 {@vehicle Star Bomber|torpedo bombers|eoti}, 30 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|combat dropships|eoti}, 8 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and 40 {@vehicle Heavy Mech|heavy mechs|eoti}

abilities.name: Combat Operation Center
abilities.description: While in the ship's COC, as a maneuver, your character may direct up to four minion-piloted starfighters to merge into a new minion group. Starfighters must be of the same type to be affected.

abilities.name: Resilient
abilities.description: When this vehicle suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} while your character is operating it, you may spend a Story Point to roll a second result and choose the result you prefer.

weapons.name: 2 forward, 1 dorsal, and 2 aft triple capital-grade beam turrets
weapons.fireArc: Forward, Port, and Starboard, or All, or Aft, Port, and Starboard
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 4 port and 4 starboard capital-grade quadruple mass driver turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 5 or larger, reduce difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 10 seeker missile pods
weapons.details: When attacking a target silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1; these weapons use a distributed targeting protocol for maximum coverage, so only two may be fired at any one target.

description: Since strike carriers form the core of the Federal Fleet, commanders are very concerned about any potential threats to their survival. Strike carriers are good at defending themselves from enemy fighters and small warships, but {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} and {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} are another matter. They are potentially tough enough to make it through fighter screens and powerful enough to even crack a strike carrier's hull.

{@i Genesis} began as the proof of concept for the future of {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol's|eoti} fleet. A ship with the capacity of a {@vehicle Carrier|carrier|eoti} but the guns and armor of a {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} could defend itself against any foe and still be able to strike targets light years away. This new "ultradreadnought" would serve in both the Federal Fleet's primary battle line and its carrier task forces all at once. The design ended up proving successful, but it cost more than four times the most expensive dreadnought or carrier. In addition, it was very slow, both at standard and superluminal velocities.

Given the price and speed issues, the Chief Councilor of Security has been unwilling to authorize additional construction. It looks like for the moment, {@i Genesis} may be the only ship of its kind. However, that does not mean it has been discarded. Instead, the vessel has become both the flagship for Gryphon Fleet and the key to the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation's|eoti} future plans of planetary conquest.

{@i Genesis} is an absolutely monstrous warship, with more than twice the guns of any conventional dreadnought and nearly double the carrying capacity of a modern strike carrier. Its interior barracks and cavernous flight decks can transport an entire Air Legion with all its associated vehicles and equipment, including whole troops of heavy mechs. Although its slow speed means it has little chance of chasing down a fleeing enemy, {@i Genesis} is certainly capable of crushing any that come within range. For that reason, Supreme Admiral DeLouis brags that the ship can bring a planet to compliance all on its own.

That might be bravado, but many other factions in the galaxy have spent significant sums of aurei to infiltrate spies into the great naval base of Churchill Prima. Every great power wants to have advance notice when {@i Genesis} finally slips its moorings and departs on a mission of conquest.

vehicle.name: Allired Fateweaver

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Coordination} check to steer the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

abilities.name: Exoskeleton
abilities.description: If this vehicle suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, reduce the result suffered by 30 (to a minimum of 01), then apply that result as a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury} against your character.

abilities.name: Jump Jets
abilities.description: When piloting this vehicle, your character can make an {@difficulty average|Athletics or Coordination} to leap to any point within medium range as an action. Your character may spend {@symbols aaa} to instead leap to any point within long range. Your character may spend {@symbols t} generated on the check to make an immediate attack against a single engaged target with the twin energy poniards.

description: This nearly four-meter-tall {@vehicle Light Mech|light mech|eoti} is the preferred and oft-romanticized form in which the officers of the Ebon Horde take the field of battle. More exoskeleton than vehicle, the mech features advanced brainwave and kinesthetic capture technology, empowering the operator to leverage their own physical prowess with {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} dueling poniards to butcher enemy infantry, emplacements, and light armor.

The Allired Fateweaver's advanced defensive systems and armor alloys keep the officer relatively safe within. The exoskeleton is environmentally sealed and features jump jets that allow for heroic leaps directly into enemy battle lines. Officer mechs are built to order in Allired, one of {@rule Arc Prime and Wren Terra|Arc Prime's|eoti} artistic centers. Their owners customize these mechs far beyond their factory cost with metal inlays and engraving that often evoke the sleek lines of a {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} officer's full-dress uniform, complete with scooped shoulder spaulders.

vehicle.name: Dunlain Reaper

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

weapons.name: Hammerfall missile launcher
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all targets within medium range suffer one hit; may not be used against targets within long range.

description: A single Dunlain Reaper can depopulate a small colony or city in hours, making it one of the more terrifying and notorious mechs in the galaxy. Built entirely around the shoulder-mounted hammerfall missile launcher, the Reaper is a lithe walker that stands eleven meters high. Grav-fins help stabilize the machine, ensuring that its feet barely touch the ground when it moves.

{@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} generals typically deploy Reapers in heavy raids, able to surge forward, volley off their heavy missiles, and then retreat before a counterattack can be launched. However, they also serve as useful counterattacking units. Often a unit of Reapers lurks behind {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} lines, waiting to smash an enemy armored breakthrough with precisely applied fury.

vehicle.name: Valeward Drone Fighter

abilities.name: Self-Destruct
abilities.description: While remotely piloting this vehicle, your character can make an {@difficulty average|piloting} to ram a target silhouette 5 or larger within short range. The target vehicle's defense modifies the check. On a success, the target vehicle suffers 2 hull trauma per drone fighter in the minion group (to a maximum of 10). Using this ability destroys the drone fighter (or all drone fighters in a minion group).

description: Drone fighters are popular among the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} Admiralty as expendable distractions and ram-bombs. Typically, commanders deploy them as conventional fighter screens, {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor|eoti} squadrons, and escorts for ace pilots or high value craft. Sometimes, however, forward-thinking officers seed orbital wreckage with squadrons of drone fighters in sleep mode. They might be programmed to passively scan, pursue and attack if their scanners trip, or to lie patiently awaiting further instructions.

The Valeward is a recent model that vaguely resembles an Agiz crystal bat, wings outstretched in flight. Their control algorithm isn't anywhere close to a true artificial intelligence, and when left to their own devices, drones have a very low kill ratio. Having {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} drone operators or aces directing a squadron dramatically increases drone lethality.

vehicle.name: Daltroc Ashbringer

weapons.name: Plasma firebombs
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all targets within short range of the target suffer one hit.

weapons.name: Seeker missiles
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: Bringing nothing but flame and death, the Ashbringer is a feared {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} weapon built to incinerate enemy logistics capabilities. Its plasma firebombs can start fires hot enough to ignite many metals. A full squadron can turn an entire populated city into ash as easily as crop fields or resupply convoys. While Ashbringers are durable, they are not as capable dogfighters as dedicated {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptor fighters|eoti}. Because of this, they typically launch in pairs with at least six {@vehicle Valeward Drone Fighter|Valeward drone fighter} escorts.

The Ashbringer is a flat, wide, triangular-shaped collection of sharp edges and angles. It has a stacked cockpit that seats its pilot forward and the weapons officer just below, offering excellent visibility. The heavy beam cannon fires just over the pilot's right shoulder, while the weapons officer's munitions mount below the wings.

vehicle.name: Denoz Warstalker
description: Like most {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti}, the Denoz Warstalker is a versatile craft built to hunt down trouble and is generally powerful enough to destroy whatever it can't outrun. It can undertake systems patrol, reconnaissance, exploration, and customs missions alone or in pairs with minimal support. When organized into lines of four to ten, Warstalkers can rip through fighter screens or focus fire to attack larger warships. Such corvette lines often hide behind planets, moons, or large asteroids, only emerging after their commanding officer has herded the enemy into a flanked position. The Warstalker's only limitations are its lack of space for troops and supplies—the price of carrying the capacitors for its overcharged primary weapon.

vehicle.name: Allired Voidcarver

weapons.name: Short Burn anti-ship missiles
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 3 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: Seeker missiles
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: The {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony of Letnev|eoti} invests heavily in the selection and training of pilots. Those with five or more combat kills against enemy fighters become aces, true celebrities among the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti}. Since the death of an ace is a cultural tragedy, the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} goes to great lengths to engineer starfighters that provide unmatched survivability and spares no expense to do so.

The Allired Voidcarver is a multi-role fighter that has a twin-prow design with a silhouette almost identical to the Grand Armada's Manifester. All things being equal, it can overcome most enemy {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti} and {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptors|eoti} in one-on-one engagements. It also has great anti-ship capability—but it has to get in close to wield it. Perhaps the Voidcarver's most interesting feature, though, is its ability to seamlessly interface with {@vehicle Valeward Drone Fighter|Valeward drone fighters}. This enables the drones to fly in tight formation alongside the ace, enhancing their firepower and serving as ablative armor.

vehicle.name: Illeprete Starfang
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 75, plus 2 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

abilities.name: Minefield
abilities.description: Once per encounter as an action, while aboard this vessel your character may make an {@difficulty average|operating} to deploy a minefield. If successful, a medium range-sized area behind this ship is now a minefield. Passing through the minefield unharmed requires a {@difficulty hard|Piloting or Operating}. If they fail, they suffer hull trauma equal to their silhouette for each turn they spend in the minefield. Your character may spend {@symbols aaa} generated on the {@skill Operating} check to add +1 additional point of total damage on this failed {@skill Piloting} or {@skill Operating} check. Your character may spend {@symbols t} to increase the minefield's size by one range band.

weapons.name: 2 dorsal, 2 ventral, 2 port, and 2 starboard antifighter beam turrets
weapons.fireArc: Forward, Port, and Starboard, or Port, or Starboard
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 4 port and 4 starboard crevasion heavy cannons
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

description: Engineers designed this destroyer around the crevasion cannon, a devastating beam weapon that can penetrate even stout {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} hulls. Unfortunately, the nature of the beam limits its effective range. That limitation informed the Starfang design—it has to be fast and durable enough to reach its target while under intense fire. To accomplish this, the wedge-shaped Starfang has thick armor and reinforced bulkheads built into the forward slopes of its prow and flanks. These allow the destroyer to shrug off hits that would cripple similarly sized ships from other factions.

The Starfang also has a moderate antifighter capability with which it can punch large holes in enemy fighter screens, but its heavy cannon loadout eliminates room for flak cannons or missile banks. However, it can vent aft compartments to deploy self-assembling smart minefields used to vector enemies into traps. All this gives the Starfang unmatched utility in the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} fleet.

vehicle.name: Goz Voidscepter
vehicle.complement: 70 officers and crew, 90 squadron pilots and support crew
vehicle.passengers: 100 soldiers (change to 1,800 soldiers, 6 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}, 36 {@vehicle Valeward Drone Fighter|drone fighters}, and 6 {@vehicle Allired Voidcarver|Voidcarvers} or {@vehicle Daltroc Ashbringer|Ashbringers} for troop transport variant)

abilities.name: Drone Flight Control Room
abilities.description: While in the control room, your character may switch any allied drones' operating modes as a maneuver and without performing a check (see {@sidebar Drone Fighters} sidebar on page 153). Further, as a maneuver, while your character is in the flight control room they may direct up to four drones to merge into a new minion group.

weapons.name: 20 antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1; these weapons are scattered across the hull of the carrier, so only two may be fired at any one target.

description: This carrier can ferry an entire brigade of troops or a wing of starfighters into a combat theater, depending on its configuration. While its sleek, angular hull suggests otherwise, the Voidscepter is ponderously slow and vulnerable to enemy warships. This relegates them to the rear of formations, though some commanders expertly use them as bait to lure enemies into traps.

The Voidscepter sports two hangars. The main hangar in the belly of the ship is home to most of the crewed starfighters, {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti} on board. Carriers configured for ground invasion convert much of this space into troop berths and assembly areas. The Voidscepter's more modest forward hangar serves as a maintenance bay and contains the carrier's drone racks.

Although bridge crew maneuver the ship and defend it from attack, squadron staff represent the bulk of personnel. They have their own command staff, pilots, maintenance personnel, and more. It's common for squadron or brigade commanding officers to outrank the ship's captain, sometimes resulting in internal power struggles between the two staffs.

vehicle.name: Serzan Dawncrusher
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 200, plus 3 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti} or {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}

abilities.name: Massive
abilities.description: When making an attack targeting this vehicle, the Critical rating of any weapons used counts as 2 higher.

weapons.name: Spinal assault beam cannon
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 2 disruptor torpedo tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; on a successful hit, may spend {@symbols aa} or {@symbols t} to reduce target ship's defense to 0 until the end of your character's next turn.

weapons.name: 2 port and 2 starboard antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

description: The Dawncrusher is an older cruiser design born from a desire to one-up the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} Navy standoff combat capability. The idea was to build a low-cost cruiser around a single {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti}-grade anti-ship beam cannon, with the hope that a battle line of cruisers could replicate the damage output of a {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti}, only more cheaply and with less outside scrutiny. Since cruisers are also expected to command warship squadrons, their bridge features a full command and control suite to direct multiple ships in combat.

The Dawncrusher has the sharp, angular lines common to {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} manufacture, with oversized weapon pods on either flank. The weapon pods are relatively recent additions meant to extend the service life of the design, providing separate generators for the torpedo tubes and antifighter turrets. The disruptor torpedoes can punch brief holes in energy shielding, enhancing the effectiveness of the main cannon against shielded targets.

vehicle.name: Werqan Manifester
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 400, plus 24 starfighters, 5 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and 2 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}

abilities.name: Massive

weapons.fireArc: Forward and Port, or Forward and Starboard
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 6 port and 6 starboard antifighter beam turrets
weapons.fireArc: Forward, Port, and Aft, or Forward, Starboard, and Aft
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: Ultima missile tubes
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all ships within medium range of the target suffer one hit; may not be used to attack targets of silhouette 5 or smaller.

description: The Manifester is an iconic ship class of the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} people, and its angular, double-prowed silhouette instills pride in the poorest ao tender on the edge of {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} space. While most great powers cower behind their {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} in defensive shells, the Grand Armada deploys as many as it holds back, showing the galaxy the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony's|eoti} strength. In the last few decades, Manifesters have participated in over a dozen victorious skirmishes with warships of other galactic powers. {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} media produces stirring epics of {@i Magnifax} scattering a {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} raiding flotilla in {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} space and the heroic stand of {@i Flefleurn} against a {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti} superdreadnought over the defenseless planet of Vorhal (in every depiction {@i Flefleurn} fights {@i alone} against the {@rule L1Z1X Mindnet|L1Z1X|eoti}, and any claims of a {@rule The Keleres of the Council|Keleres|eoti} ship being present are treated as vile slander).

With armor thick enough to ignore most smaller warships, the Manifester valiantly leads strike groups into battle against planetary defense fleets. Its triple-beam turrets can decimate all but the hardiest warships or dreadnoughts in a single volley. It is also loaded with ultima missiles that can crack warship hulls, planetary shields, and cities alike. The Manifester's biggest weakness is its relatively limited operating range; it requires significant resupply and support efforts for longer cruises.

It is common practice for incoming commanding officers to gut and redesign the bridge according to their preferences. Current trends have many captains at the very front of the bridge behind a command pulpit within a cocoon of data, surrounded by sensor readouts, battle simulation computers, and fleet status displays. However, more traditional bridges are cathedral-like, with an aisle for the captain to walk and the crew in recessed pews facing the aisle.

vehicle.name: Arc Secundus
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 400, plus 24 fighters, 36 {@vehicle Valeward Drone Fighter|drones}, 5 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and 5 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}

abilities.name: Massive

abilities.name: Resilient
abilities.description: When this vehicle suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} while your character is operating it, you may spend a Story Point to roll a second result and choose the result you prefer.

abilities.name: Shieldsplitter Torpedoes
abilities.description: On a successful attack, your character may spend {@symbols a} to reduce the target's defense by 1 (to a minimum of 0) until the end of the next round. Alternatively, your character may open a silhouette 5 sized hole in a planetary shield (increase silhouette size by 1 per additional {@symbols a} spent this way) until the end of the next round.

weapons.name: 2 port and 2 starboard quad-barreled capital-grade beam turrets
weapons.fireArc: Forward and Port, or Forward and Starboard
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 4 seeker missile pods
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: Shieldsplitter torpedo tubes
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all ships within medium range of the target suffer one hit; may not be used to attack targets of silhouette 5 or smaller.

description: While the aged {@i Arc Secundus} has undergone many refits, the same keel has served as the Baron's flagship for five centuries. As do many other {@rule Barony of Letnev|Letnev|eoti} grand battleships like {@i Enid Kyraev}, {@i Arc Secundus} features the same angular, cathedral silhouette that gave rise to the {@vehicle Werqan Manifester|Manifester} design. However, {@i Arc Secundus} is significantly larger and refitted with the most advanced technology and durable armor the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} can access.

No expense was spared in {@i Arc Secundus}'s most recent upgrade. Its specialized shieldsplitter torpedoes are designed to open bombardment windows in planetary shielding, and the Baron's pride is plated in a proprietary deverium alloy hull. The {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} claims that energy weapons harmlessly dissipate across the charcoal black plating. Outside observers speculate that the alloy employs a saimoc crystal lattice within a more traditional duranium alloy that dissipates energy weapons across the broad hull or even funnels the energy to supercharge the ship's weapon systems.

{@i Arc Secundus} has an expectedly grand interior. The command-level passageways and spaces feature high vaulted overheads and polished stone finishes for the decks and bulkheads. The ship is used for diplomatic meetings as often as anything else. Its staterooms are as sprawling and lavish as those found in palatial estates, and negotiation rooms have sweeping views, large tables, and several breakout areas. The bridge is considered hallowed ground, and officers vie for private tours as a sort of pilgrimage. It is an order of magnitude larger than most bridges to accommodate the Baron and his retinue in comfort, along with any visiting dignitaries.

vehicle.name: Kjjal Shield Crawler

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

abilities.name: Tactical Magen Field
abilities.description: Allies within medium range increase their ranged defense by 2.

description: {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} ground assaults are anything but fast. Although accurate and heavy fire precedes overland movement, there can be no guarantee this will silence all enemy guns. Enter the Kjjal shield crawler. This mech provides direct protection to advancing {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} ground forces, shielding infantry with localized defense grids and even by physically blocking fire.

The Kjjal is a squat, quadrupedal siege walker well suited to close infantry support. It stands tall enough for {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} heavy infantry to cluster beneath its central body, which is capped by a testudine armored shell with a shield generator. A series of scalelike shield projectors extend a tactical magen defense grid over the immediate vicinity. This crawler's entire crew sits in an enclosed cockpit. Holographic readouts and augmented reality eyepieces allow them to visualize the crawler's exterior without exposure to incoming fire. Up to an entire squad can similarly ensconce themselves in the cramped duranium cocoon of a troop compartment.

vehicle.name: Indomitus Heavy Mech

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

weapons.name: Shoulder-mounted missile pack
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within medium range.

weapons.name: Intercession orbital space cannon
weapons.details: May only be used against targets that are silhouette 5 or larger and are in orbit or beyond; see {@sidebar Intercession and Intervention Orbital and Deep Space Cannons} on page 175.

description: {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} forces do not commit to invasion warfare lightly. However, once the warrior-philosophers leading the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} sccuts decide that heavy ground combat is necessary, they commit to deploying decisive force to avoid prolonged suffering. This heavily armed and armored multimodal walker, dubbed the Indomitus, reflects this doctrine. The Indomitus provides fire support with a lighter version of a capital ship's neutron beam and steady forward movement, enabling a grinding advance in close coordination with dismounted infantry.

Where many other {@vehicle Heavy Mech|heavy mechs|eoti} loosely mimic walking creatures, the Indomitus bears a striking resemblance to a giant armored {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} warrior. The "arms" are actually secondary stabilization legs, allowing the mech to move with more speed and stability in quadrupedal mode or to stand on two legs and fight "hull down" by peeking just the head sensors and shoulder weapons over blocking terrain.

By far the most dangerous element of the Indomitus, however, is the intercession orbital space cannon mounted on the mech's spine. This space cannon can only be fired when the Indomitus is in quadruped mode, and even then, it is quite slow. However, the ability to deploy a truly mobile anti-orbit weapon makes the Indomitus a multispectrum threat.

vehicle.name: Xxlun Interceptor

weapons.name: Seeker missiles
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: While their pensive and diplomatic stereotypes make it hard for some to imagine {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} as fighter pilots, these Xxlun interceptors are the pride of young pilots in the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} service. Far from disapproving of the enthusiasm and aggression exhibited by Xxlun pilots, ship captains and even cchun understand it, as many were once interceptor pilots themselves. These senior leaders not only see this attitude as necessary in strike craft pilots but indeed see the starfighter corps as an outlet for channeling what would otherwise be disruptive and rebellious behavior.

The Xxlun follows a basic saucer design with an elongated "tail" of grav microgenerators for maneuvering. A single assault cannon sits just below the forward-mounted cockpit while protected missile ports snuggle into the flanks. These starfighters are ubiquitous across {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} space, as iconic of {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} militarization as the Archon Invicta superdreadnought. In battle, they protect against {@vehicle Star Bomber|bomber|eoti} attacks, giving the {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} time to deploy their big guns.

vehicle.name: Bbraj Tactical Bomber

abilities.name: Tactical Attack Controllers
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Gunnery} check aboard this vehicle and benefiting from the effects of the {@rule Aim|aim} maneuver (either to add {@dice boost} or to hit a specific part of the target), your character may cancel {@symbols hhh} or {@symbols d} if in contact with an ally who can see the target.

weapons.name: Incision missiles
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within short range.

description: Eschewing the mass devastation of inaccurate strategic {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} pride themselves on accurately striking military targets with tactical bombers. While the former destroy strategic targets such as factories, major infrastructure, and even cities, the latter are designed to go after military targets and enemy combatant units.

The Bbraj, with a bulky shielded fuselage that mimics the structure of {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} capital ships, is the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha's|eoti} premier tactical bomber. With highly precise seeker missiles and an accurate heavy beam cannon, the Bbraj's weapons loadout maximizes the chance for a surgical strike while limiting collateral damage.

{@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} tactical bombing doctrine is relatively straightforward. First, they provide close air support, following directions from {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} attack controllers to land pinpoint hits on dangerous targets and support {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} infantry. Second, they launch deep strikes on enemy forces well behind the front line. {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} bomber crews pride themselves on carrying out these missions, as they believe that their surgical attacks can compel the enemy to surrender before being destroyed.

vehicle.name: Ccostis Border Guardian

weapons.name: 1 dorsal dual heavy beam cannon turret
Paired anti-ship missile tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 3 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within short range.

description: The smallest proper warship in the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} fleet, the Ccostis corvette serves as a system patrol craft and customs enforcer. These border guardians lack the range or endurance to independently traverse the galaxy, making them a rare sight outside of {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} space or systems garrisoned by long-term {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} peacekeepers.

Corvettes fall into an awkward size range for the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha's|eoti} "slow but armored" design ethos. They are too small to mount heavy weapons or large reactors but large enough that extra armor drags down their speed and maneuverability. Rather than do several tasks poorly, the Ccostis design greatly reduces cargo and provision capacity to commit to local system defense. Too slow to chase down fighters and {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, the border patrol deploys in staggered screens to lock down sections of space.

vehicle.name: Xxintral Escort Destroyer
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 100, plus 1 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttle|eoti}

weapons.name: 1 forward, 1 port, and 1 starboard heavy accelerator flak cannon
weapons.fireArc: Forward, Port, and Starboard, or Port, or Starboard
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all ships within short range of the target suffer one hit.

weapons.name: 3 port and 3 starboard antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: Dual dorsal hullbreaker torpedo tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within medium range.

description: The {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha's|eoti} heavily armed and armored ship building philosophy provides a powerful fit for ships at destroyer tonnages and above. The Xxintral destroyer is no different. Although more ungainly than most other destroyers, at this tonnage the Xxintral can mount serious armor and weapon upgrades. Specifically, the Xxintral is equipped to lay waste to enemy fighter strengths.

The Xxintral fits a specific role in the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} order of battle. Their job is to keep {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} away from the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} battle line, throwing up huge clouds of flak in order to discourage attack runs (if not destroying the bombers outright). This lets the superdreadnoughts pummel enemy ships at extreme ranges with impunity. Although the Kingdom won't admit it, the tactic is clearly a counter to the {@rule Federation of Sol|Federation of Sol|eoti}'s investment in carrier forces. Only time will tell which approach is superior.

vehicle.name: Arbitratus Command Carrier
vehicle.passengers: 500 soldiers (increase to 1,500 soldiers and 10 {@vehicle Heavy Mech|heavy mechs|eoti} or {@vehicle Kjjal Shield Crawler|crawlers} if the interceptors and bombers are removed)
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 1,000, plus 48 {@vehicle Xxlun Interceptor|interceptors}, 24 {@vehicle Bbraj Tactical Bomber|tactical bombers}, 8 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}, and 4 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

abilities.name: Calming Atmosphere
abilities.description: If your character has allegiance to the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom||eoti}, you may add {@symbols sa} to {@skill Negotiation} and {@skill Discipline} checks you make in this ship's diplomatic suites.

abilities.name: Combat Operations Center
abilities.description: While in the carrier's COC, as a maneuver, your character may direct up to four minion-piloted starfighters to merge into a new minion group. Starfighters must be of the same type to be affected.

abilities.name: Massive

weapons.name: 6 antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1; these weapons are scattered across the hull of the carrier, so only two may be fired at any one target.

weapons.name: 2 vertical launch seeker missile bays
weapons.details: May not be used against targets within short range.

description: Although the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom|eoti} favors heavy ship fleets, most sccuts have extensive use for dedicated carrier vessels. The {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} bring their trademark focus on defense to the design of the Arbitratus. The entire front section of the command carrier is taken up by a heavy duranium shell that protects the carrier and launching fighters alike from hostile fire.

Behind this shell, the rest of the ship is a boxy affair with multiple hangar decks and cargo bays pockmarking the port and starboard surfaces. The command deck bulges slightly from the aft dorsal edge. The diplomatic suites—decorated with fresh flowers from onboard arboretums, perfumed with the heady smell of gently burning gerr root, and complete with observation decks—hang closely from the ventral surface. The placement of the diplomatic deck at the bottom, rather than the top, allows for delegations to see planetary surfaces more clearly should an Arbitratus enter atmosphere. Many {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} diplomats feel this puts what matters on display: a world worth saving or a war worth ending.

Beyond its strike carrier and diplomatic roles, the Arbitratus contributes to the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha's|eoti} unique way of war by serving as a troop ship, logistics platform, and in extremis vessel of mercy.

Almost all {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} formations rely greatly on defensive supplies and heavy ordnance to feed their steady campaigns. Arbitratus carriers can support dedicated supply ships both by flying interceptor cover and by storing critical supplies within their heavily armored hulls.

vehicle.name: Clarus Heavy Cruiser
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 150, plus 2 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

abilities.name: Siege Shield

description: Heavy cruisers are the workhorse of the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} fleet, used to show the flag, signal military concern, and enact blockades and peace enforcements. Most {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} admirals remember their time aboard a Clarus cruiser fondly, and therefore trust these older vessels for a wide variety of tasks.

Much like other {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} ships, Clarus cruisers are slow and lack maneuverability at subluminal speeds when compared to the ships of the other great powers. However, these heavy cruisers are powered by oversized reactors that allow good speed and excellent endurance over interstellar distances. This is despite the massive slabs of prow armor that give the cruiser incredible forward resilience.

The Clarus mounts a diverse range of armaments suitable for engaging other capital ships, smaller multicrew vessels, and—in a pinch—a handful of starfighters. Heavier armor and shields help the Clarus gain the edge against enemy cruisers in one-on-one battle, but the risk to a lone heavy cruiser from fighter and torpedo bomber swarms is real. {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} doctrine stresses that cruisers be escorted by {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} for this exact reason.

description: As a symbol of the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} resolve to never again suffer the fate of Archon Tau, this latest model of {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} superdreadnought proudly bears the name Archon Invicta.

The {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} employ superdreadnoughts as the inexorable core of their battlefleet. However, they rarely send superdreadnoughts beyond the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Kingdom's|eoti} borders. A deployment like that signals such a significant escalation that the king's war court does not suggest it lightly. When superdreadnoughts are deployed, they are often used to lock down regions of space and slowly roll forward a zone of {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} control. These deployments cover the establishment of permanent bases, fortifications, and surface-based space cannons.

Tactically, {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} admirals hold their superdreadnoughts toward the center of a fleet formation. Covered by heavy cruisers and escort destroyers, the superdreadnoughts engage at long range at the decisive phase of battle. Their spinal-mounted mass drivers known as {@i resolution cannons} impart enough kinetic energy to knock even fellow dreadnoughts off course.

In contrast to the {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} of other major powers, the Archon Invicta has a notable absence of dedicated surface bombardment arrays. Even with hearts hardened by the subjugation of Xxlak and the burning of Archon Tau, most {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} cannot bring themselves to contemplate visiting the same fate on others. It's true that an Archon Invicta could turn its mass drivers onto surface targets, but few {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} captains could bear to issue those orders and even fewer crews would likely follow them.
