description: The great warship {@i Loncara Ssodu} serves King Ccrysus both as his personal flagship and as the crown jewel of the entire {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} armada. With tonnage far above the largest superdreadnought, this mighty ship of war boasts the thickest armor and most destructive weapons the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} can bring to bear.

For good or for ill, {@i Loncara Ssodu} perfectly channels the militarized cultural mood of a peaceful people steeling themselves for war. The majority of the ship's proper superstructure is a rectangular affair of jutting power relays, sensors, landing bays, and other scarcely concealed functional elements.

Multiple interlocking armored shells mark {@i Loncara Ssodu} as clearly {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti}. These shells are constructed from hundreds of layers of crystal-laced duranium alloy. The front section of the hull is thus thicker than any other interstellar-capable ships in the {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} fleet. Shield projectors overlaid on these shells enhance the testudine appearance. Beyond the practicality of these physical shields, many {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} troubled by the construction of this fearsome warship take some comfort that its most visually striking feature is a defensive one.

Despite the visual impact of these duranium shells, what truly distinguishes {@i Loncara Ssodu} is the incredible long-range firepower on board. The superheavy neutron beams provide a conventional means of attack, but it is the intervention deep space cannon system that gives this ship its teeth. {@rule Xxcha Kingdom|Xxcha|eoti} weapons engineers hope the very presence of these weapons capable of firing across an entire star system will mean that they do not need to be used.

vehicle.name: Char'eet "Valkyrie" Exoskeleton

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct the vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

abilities.name: Exoskeleton
abilities.description: If this vehicle suffers a {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit}, reduce the result suffered by 30 (to a minimum of 01), then apply that result as a {@rule Critical Injuries|Critical Injury} against your character.

description: Classified as a {@vehicle Light Mech|light mech|eoti}, this exoskeleton is standard issue for many Tekklar Elite units, perhaps most famously the Tekklar Elite's Valkyrie scurry, named for a bloody encounter with a {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} Spec Ops brigade of the same name. Legends say Valkyrie scurry took out the entire {@rule Federation of Sol|Sol|eoti} brigade and their Carnivore tanks using the first models of still-experimental exoskeletons. As is their custom, the unit then claimed the name for themselves. Now, after decades of combat, that name has become synonymous with the exoskeletons even more than the pilots who operate them. The latest versions have simply been named "Valkyrie" officially.

The Valkyrie is standard issue to mechanized infantry units, and it is often used by officers to provide extra survivability on the front lines of a swarm. Because the round armor plates have an oily sheen, in early encounters, enemies believed the Valkyrie was actually a new {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} morphology rather than a machine. The suit makes a soldier powerful enough to slaughter whole infantry squads and even platoons on their own. In groups, they can close the distance and penetrate enemy vehicles from angles where their armor is weakest.

vehicle.name: Kess'or "Fury" Fighter

weapons.name: Anti-ship missiles
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 3 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1; may not be used against targets within short range.

description: Fury fighters are meant to intimidate and spread chaos on the battlefield. The {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr's|eoti} swarming instinct enables these fighters to fly in compact, roiling cloud formations, and they often deploy in waves thick enough to block out sensor readings of the parent ships behind them. When they swarm over a {@vehicle Cruiser|cruiser|eoti} or {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyer|eoti}, they engulf it, blinding it entirely as they chew through its armor. Their multifiring beam arrays make ten fighters seem like a hundred, making their swarm very difficult for enemy {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} or missiles to get past.

The Fury is a sleek, rounded craft with thin retractable wings that deploy in atmosphere. Its hull vaguely resembles an {@i acri'did}, a leaping mount sometimes still used by scouts but these days largely relegated to a status symbol among the wealthier strata of {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} society. Fury fighters also possess swarm shields, which use fine-tuned electromagnetic fields to prevent collisions and do a good job repelling shrapnel.

vehicle.name: Chuliss'Or "Bile" Bomber
vehicle.complement: 1 pilot, 1 copilot, 2 gunners, and 1 electronics/weapons officer

weapons.name: 2 multifiring beam array turrets and 1 mandible-mounted multifiring beam array

description: Primarily a ground support bomber, the Bile spends a lot of time in atmospheric combat, softening targets and even creating trenches for ground forces. While a bit slow and lumbering by {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} standards, these bombers are more than capable of keeping up with the {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti} and troop carriers they usually escort. They are also sturdy enough to withstand most handheld antiair weaponry, at least long enough to drop their specialized payloads.

The scarab-like body of the Bile houses a large rotary bomb dispenser that can mount a variety of munitions, the most popular of which is called the {@i bile bomb}. It spreads a sticky gel over a twenty-meter radius upon detonation. Instead of igniting, this chemical payload mixes into a potent acid, melting through rock, armor plating, flesh, and electrical components indiscriminately.

vehicle.name: Saltat'torr "Pilgrim" Scout Ship

weapons.name: Sensor mask missiles
weapons.details: If this attack hits, may spend {@symbols aa} to disable the target's sensors or comms for the rest of the encounter. If the comms are disabled, the target cannot communicate. If the sensors are disabled, the target cannot detect anything or make attacks beyond medium range. This may be repaired with a {@difficulty hard|mechanics}.

description: The {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} military strategy relies on fast scouting and patrol vessels that can discover threats and potential colony sites. The elongated Pilgrims are built for speed and range—both sublight and superluminal—and are meant to push the boundaries of {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} space ever outward. Unfortunately, that speed comes at the expense of durability and firepower. In large engagements, the Pilgrim typically swarms with fighters or {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, providing extra cover against gunships and other threats to its fighter escort.

Most of the scout ship's weaponry is meant to facilitate escape. The ventral plasma cannon running along the lower hull of the ship can fire ahead or behind, forcing pursuit craft to keep their distance. The Pilgrim also has a pair of light turrets for close defense against small craft that manage to keep up with it. Finally, it has a small missile that detonates to release a viscous opaque black gel. While it's largely harmless, it does adhere to metal. If it coats sensor pods, comms arrays, or even bridge viewports, it acts as an impermeable barrier to most electromagnetic frequencies, leaving a ship blind, deaf, and disoriented.

vehicle.name: Rakti'torr "Exoraider" Destroyer
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 50, plus 2 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti} and 20 boarding stingers

abilities.name: Boarding Stinger
abilities.description: When the boarding stinger hits an enemy ship, it burrows into the target's hull and then disgorges six {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} marines onto the vessel (use the {@adversary Infantry Soldier (Sardakk N'orr)|infantry soldier profile for the Sardakk N'orr|eoti} on page 251 of {@title Embers of the Imperium}). Where the stinger hits is up to the GM, but {@symbols aa} or {@symbols hh} could be spent by either the players or GM to have it hit a more or less advantageous location (the engine room versus water storage tanks, for example). The marines can reboard the stinger and detach it from the target ship. However, the stinger has very limited fuel and steering, so once it detaches, the occupants are left waiting to be picked up by a friendly vessel. Boarding stingers suffer a fair amount of damage in the boarding process and cannot be reused even if recovered.

weapons.name: 6 port and 6 starboard antifighter beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 2 port and 2 starboard boarding stinger tubes
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 2; if the hit deals damage, 6 {@rule Sardakk N'orr||eoti} soldiers are deployed into the ship [see Boarding Stinger on page 183].

description: The modern {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} destroyer, or exoraider, has a tall, compressed, obovate hull design similar to small predatory river fish. Its dual plasma cannon can decimate enemy {@vehicle Corvette|corvettes|eoti}, {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and defense platforms, and it can even rain plasma planetside in devastating orbital bombardments. In a swarm, exoraiders tend to flank larger warships to protect them from fighters and {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti} with their many antifighter turrets. The exoraider's boarding stinger tubes launch ballistic boarding craft containing six {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} soldiers at enemy vessels. When a stinger pierces a ship's hull, it disgorges its soldiers to capture the vessel, be it an enemy supply ship or even a warship.

The narrow exoraider is quite claustrophobic to non-N'orr, particularly the cylindrical passageways with low overheads. The ship's crew and troops scurry over and around each other to get from sleeping piles to duty stations without any sense of personal space, but the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} don't seem to mind. The company of soldiers aboard are trained as marines, comfortable fighting in low or no gravity and familiar with basic ship layouts and systems.

vehicle.name: Oss'orr "Exolander" Carrier
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 200, plus 36 {@vehicle Kess'or "Fury" Fighter|Fury fighters}, 18 {@vehicle Chuliss'Or "Bile" Bomber|Bile bombers}, and 12 {@vehicle Rambler|ramblers|eoti} or imported {@vehicle MR Avalanche Land Train|Avalanche land trains}

description: The blocky exolander carrier vessel features a squat, boxy design that looks like a marine crustacean with a long vertical tail. Smaller than most {@vehicle Carrier|carriers|eoti}, it packs troops into quarters so tight they'd be considered criminal in other civilizations. This doesn't matter to the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti}, though, as they spend much of their time aboard in diapause hibernation until they're called to fight. The K'dar in charge of the exolander's swarm of soldiers typically has overall command of the vessel, including selecting landing sites and approving orbital approach vectors.

While small for a carrier, the exolander is enormous for a {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropship|eoti} and is one of the largest {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} vessels designed to make planetfall. The ship lands with its thrusters to the ground, disgorging troops via large ramps under the cover of the engine assembly and a dozen light beam turrets. The exolander can also serve as a field headquarters for its regiment or act as a garrison to defend a colony, providing shelter, long-range communications, and resupply. Launching back into orbit is a struggle, though; it takes all the ship's power to lumber back to the stars.

vehicle.name: Curr'soral "Exobireme" Cruiser
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 100, plus 12 docked {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}, 12 {@vehicle Kess'or "Fury" Fighter|Fury fighters}, and 3 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

weapons.name: 2 port and 2 starboard light beam turrets
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

description: Designed to invade uninhabited planets or small colonies with minimal support, the exobireme is a cruiser that balances several mission profiles. Its prawny form, resembling a tapered, undulating sea creature, is similar to that of its larger cousin, the {@vehicle Natat'torr "Exotrireme" Dreadnought|exotrireme}. Unlike that dreadnought's underbelly, though, the exobireme's forward ventral surface sports two dozen blisters that serve as docking ports for {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti} and launch tubes for fighters and {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}.

Exobiremes lead most small- and medium-sized response units and might travel with nothing but a pair of {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} to take over uninhabited worlds or small colonies. However, they can also lead armadas of several other cruisers with dozens of destroyers, {@vehicle Carrier|carriers|eoti}, and scout ships to destroy pirate flotillas, seize larger colonies, or probe enemy fleet strengths. In the largest battles, exobiremes swarm like any other fleet unit, often leading clusters of fighters and destroyers or defending {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} from enemy warships. The exobireme's only weakness is against enemy {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, as it is almost entirely dependent on its own fighter complement and flanking destroyers for fighter defense.

Conditions within an exobireme are cramped, but there is a certain beauty to the polished, organic curves of the passageways and spaces within. Most non-N'orr, however, describe the interior as unsettling, filled as it is with displays meant for compound eyes and sharp, pungent insectoid odors that most species associate with danger. For a ship with so many lives aboard, it's also remarkably quiet, as most of the complement is packed into dropships in diapause.

vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 400, plus 12 {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptors|eoti} or {@vehicle Escort Fighter|escort fighters|eoti}, 3 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, and 2 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}

abilities.description: When the exotrireme deliberately {@rule Collisions|collides} with another ship (see page 222 of the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook), the other ship suffers 30 damage to its {@rule Hull Trauma Threshold|hull trauma threshold} and adds +40 to the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} result it suffers; the exotrireme reduces the result of the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Critical Hit} it suffers by 20.

weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all ships within medium range of the target suffer one hit; when attacking a target that is not an immobile station or planetary structure, increase difficulty by 2.

description: Among the largest warships in the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} fleet, the Natat'torr dreadnought, or exotrireme, seems almost like a living creature swimming through the stars. Its long, tapered hull features segmented plates that fold over each other in a manner common to most aquatic arthropods. The sharp prow has four massive spikes that almost look like mandibles. When exotriremes swarm, it's common for them to ram large enemy ships and continue fighting, now using the skewered vessel as a kind of ablative armor.

Exotriremes are rarely alone, typically fighting as part of a large swarm of fighters and support ships. They lead large-scale battles and planetary invasions, decimating enemy warships as they close the distance to threaten enemy {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} or dreadnoughts with their rams. The {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} willingness to trade ships with the enemy and turn every engagement into a war of attrition means just the threat of ramming causes most enemies to flinch and sound a retreat.

The Natat'torr hull shape has largely gone unchanged since before the Twilight Wars. The iconic design is meant to evoke a benevolent god from a {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} creation myth that carried the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr's|eoti} progenitor ancestor from paradise to conquer {@rule Quinarra and Tren'lak|Quinarra|eoti}. The being's name roughly translates to "the one who swims to stars," and the {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} exotriremes remain symbolic of seizing a bountiful, hopeful future.

vehicle.name: C'Morran N'orr
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 1,500, plus 48 {@vehicle Kess'or "Fury" Fighter|Fury fighters} and 12 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}

abilities.name: Swarm Command
abilities.description: While on the bridge of {@i C'Morran N'orr} your character can make an {@difficulty average|leadership} as an action. On a success, all {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} vehicles within the same star system with at least one other active {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} vehicle within long range add {@symbols s} to all {@skill Driving}, {@skill Piloting}, and {@skill Gunnery} checks until the end of your character's next turn. Your character may spend {@symbols aaa} or {@symbols t} from the check to increase all affected units' defense by 1.

weapons.name: 3 port and 3 starboard capital-grade plasma batteries
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

weapons.name: 6 seeker missile pods
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, reduce difficulty by 1.

description: While many flagships are effectively superdreadnoughts, {@i C'Morran N'orr} is a unique command and control craft capable of directing fleet swarms with lethal precision. Although the ship looks similar to the {@vehicle Natat'torr "Exotrireme" Dreadnought|exotrireme} in basic form, it is nearly four times as long from prow to "tail," and instead of having a vicious ram, the prow bristles with antennae that can connect with any {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} ship within the same system. Once connected to {@i C'Morran N'orr}, the teams of swarm tacticians aboard each vessel can induce more complex and cooperative swarm behaviors in their soldiers.

The {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} typically station their flagship in a major shipyard where it can coordinate starship construction, increasing efficiency significantly. {@i C'Morran N'orr} is only present at the largest fleet engagements or at invasions of worlds with defenses on par with the homeworld of one of the great powers. Even then, it is never left unprotected, and thick fighter screens and dozens of {@vehicle Destroyer|destroyers|eoti} and {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}, if not {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}, protect its flanks.

The Veiled Brood controls a large chamber at the heart of {@i C'Morran N'orr}. Most believe this is just because the flagship has an inherently political function. They think the order presides over a shrine there to Sardakk the Queen Mother while advising the military leaders aboard. However, some {@rule Sardakk N'orr|N'orr|eoti} believe {@i C'Morran N'orr}'s unique command and control capabilities are because the queen herself maintains private suites aboard the flagship. Other conspiracy theorists agree but assert she is instead a prisoner of the Veiled Brood. This is a notion the Veiled Brood work tirelessly to suppress, though no one can say if that's because it's true or because it's heresy.

vehicle.name: Katapalta Tank

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct this vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

abilities.name: Catastrophic Failure
abilities.description: After your character makes a combat check to fire the plasma sphere launcher, the target may spend {@symbols hhhh} or {@symbols d} to have the weapon become damaged two steps (see page 89 in the {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook). If the plasma sphere launcher is destroyed or becomes unusable for any reason, your character must make a successful {@difficulty hard|mechanics} as an out-of-turn {@rule Incidentals|incidental}. If they fail, this vehicle suffers the {@rule Vehicle Critical Hits|Vaporized Critical Hit} (see {@title Genesys} Core Rulebook, page 230).

description: Capable of withstanding heavy enemy fire, the Katapalta is a staple of {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} forces. Its main weapon uses stabilized plasma orbs that can level protective city walls, shield generators, and weapon emplacements. Deep within its design, however, lies a terrible flaw.

The plasma sphere launcher siphons plasma directly from the Katapalta's reactor and forms it into a sphere using electromagnetic "bottles." However, if the projectors are even just slightly misaligned, they can cause weak points in the bottle, leading to a sphere rupture in the launch tube if the gunner doesn't vent the system quickly enough.

vehicle.name: Reclaimer Mech

abilities.name: All-Terrain
abilities.description: When making a {@skill Driving} check to direct this vehicle, your character may remove {@dice setback|2} added to the check due to terrain.

abilities.name: Lifting-Field Projector
abilities.description: If a target is immobilized by the lifting-field projector, your character may make an {@difficulty average|mechanics} as an action. If the check succeeds, the target is lifted directly up one range band (to a maximum of medium range from the ground). If the check fails, the vehicle suffers 4 system strain.

description: Initially created for mining and construction work, this durable heavy mech now serves in frontline combat, thanks to modifications by the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} military. With a towering fifteen-meter bipedal frame, the modified Reclaimer sports two shoulder-mounted heavy beam cannons that make it a match for any other mech on the battlefield. It also retains the resilience of an industrial mech, which its crews greatly appreciate.

During the redesign process, the engineers were worried that removing the Reclaimer's heavy manipulator arms would unbalance the mech, so they left both them and its chest-mounted lifting-field projector installed. This has proven remarkably useful, and many legions temporarily assign their Reclaimers to their combat engineering detachments. Constructing fortifications or rebuilding destroyed infrastructure is much easier with a Reclaimer to do the heavy lifting.

vehicle.name: Validor Superiority Interceptor

abilities.name: Advanced Sensor Suite
abilities.description: When your character makes a check to use sensors or scan space, add {@dice boost} to the check.

weapons.name: Javis interceptor darts
weapons.details: If an attack with this weapon misses, the {@quality Guided} quality triggers without spending {@symbols aa}.

description: A light frame, superior sensors, and speed are the tools of the starfighter's trade, and the Validor has them all. Designed by the legendary engineer Aarcus Aarctius, the Validor's purpose is to act as a forward scout for small fleets and then overwhelm any enemy fighters it finds. Skilled Validor pilots can quickly outmaneuver enemy fighters before blasting their opponent from behind with either a beam cannon or long, slim javis missiles fired from underwing racks.

Considered the {@rule Winnu|Winnu's|eoti} most agile vessel, the Validor is still notably tougher than other {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptors|eoti}. It also has much better endurance to support its scout role. However, the extra space required for additional fuel and structural reinforcements means that the Validor can carry far less weaponry. Aarctius's design compensates for this by equipping the Validor with a more accurate beam cannon and filling its limited missile bay with advanced javis interceptors that have semi-independent tracking abilities. However, the Validor has a distinct disadvantage in a protracted dogfight, so {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} pilots know to get their strikes in and get out as quickly as possible.

vehicle.name: Princeps Subjugation Bomber

weapons.name: Bombardment rocket racks
weapons.details: When attacking a target of silhouette 4 or smaller, increase difficulty by 1.

description: The {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} see the roles of fighters and bombers as fixed and clearly defined. Fighters serve as scouts and interceptors, protecting larger vessels from the small craft of the enemy. Similarly, bombers have no place engaging enemy warships; that's a job for {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti} and {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti}. Instead, bombers exist to pound ground targets during an invasion.

Designed as a fast, effective, and relatively inexpensive ground attack craft, the Princeps subjugation bomber easily fits the Navis Guard's requirements. The removal of its FTL drives allowed {@rule Winnu||eoti} engineers to equip it with larger engines for devastating speed and efficiency. This, coupled with powerful deflection shield generators, allows the Princeps to be sent on deep penetration raids through enemy air defenses.

Many Princeps crews decorate their bombers with horrifying visages of vicious creatures from around the galaxy like the flying lizards of Ra'idae and the {@adversary Arctic Sharak|arctic sharak|eoti}. The flashing teeth, ivory claws, and bright red or yellow eyes are hardly regulation, but most commanders let these infractions slide for the sake of morale.

vehicle.name: Tribune-class Auxiliary Medical Frigate
vehicle.passengers: 20, plus medical suites for up to 50 patients
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 200 in medical supplies

abilities.name: Medical Operations Center
abilities.description: When making a check to heal wounds, strain, or {@rule Critical Injuries} while on this ship, your character adds {@symbols sa} to the results and may spend {@symbols aaa} or {@symbols t} from that check to heal a Critical Injury the target is suffering (if the original check was to also heal a Critical Injury, the target can have up to two Critical Injuries healed).

abilities.name: Missile Bafflers
abilities.description: As a maneuver, your character may activate a Tribune's missile bafflers. While active, upgrade the difficulty of all combat checks made with weapons with the {@quality Guided} quality targeting this vessel twice. For every five minutes that the bafflers remain active (or one round in structured gameplay), this vessel suffers 1 system strain. System strain cannot be repaired while the missile bafflers are active.

description: Nothing relieves the victims of a disaster like the arrival of a {@i Tribune}-class frigate. Stark white paneling with crimson trim helps easily identify the vessel, and that's the point. After all, the Tribune's role isn't to fight wars but to provide comfort to the injured and the sick.

Each Tribune carries enough medical supplies and personnel to care for a major colony settlement. Some have their own dedicated staff of medical professionals, while others are based on major worlds, ready to take on local medical personnel and ferry them where they are needed. A Tribune has enough fuel and fast enough superluminal engines to respond quickly to any crisis.

Since the Tribune is a medical aid ship, its weaponry is extremely limited and used only in self-defense. In fact, the most powerful military system aboard is a missile-baffling jammer. The frigate also has a single defensive turret along its spine and a retractable gas lobber hidden in a compartment near the main hatch. In case of riot or panic, the pilot can disperse crowds with a few clouds of soporific fumes.

The captains of these vessels are generally renowned as brash risk-takers. Many honored pilots received their accolades from flying a Tribune through dense debris fields or ion storms to get civilians and military personnel the medical help they need.

Until the end of your character's next turn, add {@symbols f} to the results of any combat check targeting the other vessel. Whenever {@symbols f} is added to the results in that way, this ship suffers 4 system strain.

description: The stubby and pugnacious {@i Victus}-class support destroyer possesses potent firepower mostly geared toward antifighter defenses. While {@vehicle Interceptor Starfighter|interceptors|eoti} patrol the outer envelope of an engagement to hunt down enemy fighters and {@vehicle Star Bomber|bombers|eoti}, the Victus keeps close to its larger kin, the Navis Guard's {@vehicle Cruiser|cruisers|eoti} and {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnoughts|eoti}. There it lays down a punishing antifighter barrage with its many beam turrets and keel javis launcher. Since this destroyer isn't expected to stray far from the main fleet, it forgoes torpedo or missile tubes. Instead, it sports an extra main gun turret just in case it finds itself in a tight situation.

What truly makes the Victus stand out, though, is its boosted magen defense screen projectors. A {@i Victus}-class destroyer can throw a magen defense screen around another nearby ship, saving the smaller vessel from enemy fire. Although it severely strains the Victus' generators, the projectors can be activated nearly instantly. Victus crews train in engaging the remote screen just in time to absorb enemy fire and then deactivating it rapidly before their ship's capacitors suffer a catastrophic energy drain. This nearly always works, but there are a few fleet stories about destroyers reduced to powerless hulks after their crew pushed the ship past its limits.

vehicle.name: Nobilis-class Planetary Assault Carrier
vehicle.encumbranceCapacity: 200, plus 24 {@vehicle Validor Superiority Interceptor|interceptors}, 24 {@vehicle Princeps Subjugation Bomber|bombers}, 12 {@vehicle Combat Dropship|dropships|eoti}, 6 {@vehicle Shuttle|shuttles|eoti}, 10 {@vehicle Light Mech|light mechs|eoti}, and 5 {@vehicle Rambler|ramblers|eoti}

description: The planetary assault carriers of the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} are staggeringly large. Designed to carry both aerospace and ground-based forces into battle, {@i Nobilis}-class carriers also supply colonies, outposts, and major mercantile centers with food, munitions, and trade materials. They can even hold prefabricated housing facilities, allowing the Nobilis to serve as an armed colony vessel or a rapid response ship for some huge natural disaster.

The bulky, wedge-shaped hull's most distinctive features are the half dozen hemispherical domes running along each flank. These are ready-to-use habitation structures, hospitals, administration centers, mechanic shops, and motor pools. The Nobilis' oversized ventral thrusters allow the huge ship to enter the atmosphere of a world. Then, while it hovers with engines straining, the domes detach from the sides of the carrier, and powerful grav-tethers lower them to the ground below. In this way, the Nobilis can establish the core of a new colony in a matter of hours or set up aid and recovery facilities right in the midst of a devastated area.

The {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} speak about the humanitarian uses of this ship class with pride while downplaying its considerable military utility. The huge hull can just as easily carry dozens of fighters and bombers and thousands of troops as it can colonists and their supplies. It is something of an open secret that the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} produce variant versions of the detachable domes designed for military use. These barracks, armories, command centers, and infirmaries can lower to form a self-sufficient base before the legion's soldiers have even finished clearing the surrounding territory of enemy forces.

abilities.name: Operation Modules
abilities.description: The Hyperion must be equipped with one of the following bridge modules, which modifies the vessel's profile as follows: {@b Survey and Reconnaissance:} When your character makes a check to use sensors or scan space, add {@dice boost|2} to the check. {@b Command:} The crews of allied ships under this vessel's command add {@dice boost} to any {@skill Piloting} or {@skill Gunnery} checks they make while within extreme range of this ship. {@b Battle Bridge:} Increase this ship's defense to 3. {@b Oversight Module:} All other ships add {@dice setback|2} to checks made to detect or scan this vessel. While engaged with a stationary ship, your character may spend an action to activate this vessel's boarding tube and cut into the side of that ship, allowing characters to pass between the two vessels without space suits or shuttles and without worrying about locked hatches. Finally, your character may make a {@difficulty daunting|computers} as an action. If they succeed, one other {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} ship within long range suffers 20 system strain, plus 5 additional system strain per uncanceled {@symbols s}.

weapons.fireArc: Forward, Port, and Starboard, or Aft, Port, and Starboard

weapons.name: 1 dorsal and 1 ventral javis interceptor dart launcher
weapons.details: If an attack with this weapon misses, the {@quality Guided} quality triggers without spending {@symbols aa}.

description: With the {@rule Winnu|Winnu's|eoti} military stretched thin, fleet commanders regularly allocate cruisers to function as command vessels, primarily due to the speed at which their shipyards can produce them. The {@i Hyperion}-class high cruiser's sleek design is a contrast to some of the bulkier vessels the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} are known for. More maneuverable and versatile than its larger cousins, the Hyperion has become the mainstay of the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} galactic forces. It is even large enough to carry multiple heavy graviton beam cannons, allowing the ship to fire them in volleys to compensate for the weapon's slow recharge time.

The distinctive design of the cruiser's superstructure is a unique modular construction that allows the bridge and topside equipment to be removed and replaced with several days' work at a properly equipped space dock. Although some designers laugh this off as a strange eccentricity, it allows the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} to maintain a smaller number of cruisers that can be specially refitted for specific roles depending on the needs of the Navis Guard.

The bridge modules range from ones focused on survey and reconnaissance with additional sensor arrays to battle bridges equipped with improved antimass deflectors to command and control bridges that allow the Hyperion to become the squadron leader of a military flotilla.

There is another bridge option that sees rarer use: the oversight module, used exclusively by the Lumenari Inspectorate. The Inspectorate serves the emperor as both an internal and external intelligence operation, and their remit is to ensure loyalty among the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} military just as much as it is to spy on foreign powers. The oversight module gives the Hyperion limited stealth capabilities, signal interceptors, and a pair of boarding tubes. It is also rumored to provide the cruiser with the emperor's own computer authority code, which is capable of shutting down the power systems of any {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} vessel.

weapons.name: Dorsal mounted superheavy graviton bombardment array
weapons.details: When the {@quality Blast} item quality is triggered, all ships within medium range of the target suffer one hit; when attacking a target that is not an immobile station or planetary structure, increase difficulty by 2.

description: Upon the announcement of the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} emperor's mandate, the Navis Guard quickly realized it would need a cheap and relatively simple {@vehicle Dreadnought|dreadnought|eoti} if it was going to bulk up its fleet with any speed. The Antiphon was developed to meet those needs. Although it may come up a bit short when compared to the graceful dreadnoughts of the {@rule Barony of Letnev|Barony|eoti} or the lethal {@vehicle Natat'torr "Exotrireme" Dreadnought|Exotriremes} of the {@rule Sardakk N'orr||eoti}, it is still a respectable warship of the line.

The Antiphon is bulky and boxy, with massive wingpods extending from the port and starboard sides that give the whole vessel a mammoth girth exceeded only by its considerable length. The design is entirely unlovely, but its brutal simplicity commands respect from those who find themselves in its presence. In short, the Antiphon is a vessel built solely for war—and it looks it.

The main armaments of the Antiphon are batteries of graviton beam cannons. Graviton beams are a relatively recent technological development for the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} (and the focus of several {@rule Universities of Jol-Nar|Jol-Nar|eoti} scientific acquisition operations). They have proven more effective at cutting through heavier armor and damaging systems than standard capital-grade beam weaponry. In addition, they have pinpoint accuracy that allows them to be used more reliably against much smaller targets. However, their substantial recharge rates result in long pauses between firings. The {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} get around this by mounting additional batteries on the Antiphon. One cannon fires while another recharges, allowing the ship to keep up a constant barrage. Of course, some commanders choose to fire all their cannons in one huge volley, risking several minutes of being virtually unarmed in order to disable their foe in a single strike.

weapons.details: May only target vessels of silhouette 5 or larger; may activate the {@quality Auto-Fire} quality by spending {@symbols a}.

description: The {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} flagship {@i Salai Sai Corian} is the largest vessel in the fleet and takes its name from the praefectus who captained the vessel's first voyage to {@rule Mecatol Rex||eoti} when Emperor Muad Di Faruuq attempted to claim the galactic throne. Although the multiple graviton cannons that stud its hull allow the vessel to engage a whole flotilla and emerge triumphant, {@i Salai Sai Corian}'s role in the {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} strategy is not to win battles, but to demonstrate the power of the empire.

The interior of the vessel is a monument to the greatness of the Lazax and their loyal {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} stewards. Lofty ceilings bedecked with golden moulding arch over every passageway, and each wall holds a holoportrait of a great {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} or Lazax leader. Dozens of palatial staterooms occupy the forward section of the vessel, each designed for command staff and visitors to use as either lavish bedrooms or meeting spaces. Though the crew quarters are much less ostentatious, no {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} serving aboard {@i Salai Sai Corian} would trade their duties for a palatial mansion on their homeworld.

Some naval architects are critical of {@i Salai Sai Corian}'s design, particularly how its main weapons are scattered across the hull and lack overlapping firing arcs. The {@rule Winnu|Winnu|eoti} counter that this makes the ship {@i more} effective when it plunges into the midst of enemy vessels, as it can fire in all directions. This strategy is enhanced by a unique weapon system installed on the flagship by the express orders of the emperor: the fulgur emitter array. The array uses a remote multi-targeting system that unleashes a stream of highly charged tricascadic energy that can leap from one enemy ship to another without losing cohesion or strength. The energy blasts through the target's hull, scrambling computer systems and leaving vessels dead in space.
